The documentation build does not rerun these examples. Thirteen original Apache-2.0 examples for FontLab 9. Each entry verifies a fixture SHA-256, copies its VFJ to a new temporary directory, opens that copy and closes exactly that package in finally . Copy paths are resolved before opening so macOS /var and /private/var refer to the same owned document. Successful cleanup removes the working directory; failed close retains it. Nothing saves over testdata. Font attribution and licences remain in the fixture manifest . All modules import outside FontLab. Entry functions need FontLab's fontlab , fontgate objects and fontpr bridge. The pen/export entries additionally need FontTools installed in FontLab's Python 3.11 interpreter. TypeRig and Fontport are not required for these thirteen scripts. Run edits in a dedicated no-document FontLab session through the workspace native runner. Native status: 13/13 passed on 2026-10-16, FontLab 9.0.9783 (workspace receipt: verification/issue-106/evidence/getgo/examples3-all/receipt.json ). The receipt covers run() , declared assertions, owned cleanup and unchanged fixtures; host-free tests remain separate.
title: Real GetGo fonts, disposable working copies

text: These are repository-checkout demos, not standalone Scripts-folder installations. Keep the checkout (including testdata/getgo ) together and put its root on sys.path once, then import an example: import sys sys . path . insert ( 0 , "/path/to/fontlab-python-examples" ) from examples.getgo import font_audit print ( font_audit . run ()) Each script also has a MenuTitle and prints its result when executed from the Scripting panel as __main__ ; keep that root on sys.path for this route too. No script chooses the current font. The UI returns an explicitly owned handle; all other results are dictionaries. Mutation entries enforce the no-document requirement before reading fixtures or creating a working directory and name any open documents in the error. Read-only examples may coexist with other fonts.
title: Repository-checkout demos: run inside FontLab

text: font_audit.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Measured: 96 glyphs, 95 encoded scalars, 2048 UPM, and no anchors. The report also covers vertical metrics, unencoded names and Unicode collisions. GG Baar has zero anchors: both counts make that explicit, alongside missing A/H top anchors. The explicit anchor policy demonstrates a check; an absent anchor is not automatically a font defect.
title: font_audit — metrics, encoding and anchor policy (native passed; 0.21 s)

text: unicode_coverage.py uses Zoto Kufi Arabic (Apache-2.0). run(text="مرحبا بالعالم 123") compares native encodings against unique scalars through a Unicode-only reader. Measured: eight covered code points; U+0031/U+0032/U+0033 are missing. U+0627 is covered; no layer/anchor lookup is needed. Encoding coverage does not prove contextual shaping.
title: unicode_coverage — Arabic sample text (native passed; 0.27 s)

text: outline_pens.py uses GG Hint (Apache-2.0). A/B/O contours pass through FontTools BoundsPen/AreaPen for exact curve bounds and signed areas. Measured A/B/O: 2/3/2 contours, 11/55/42 points; winding labels and FontLab hasIntersPoints boundary-intersection index pairs. Contained counters and self-intersections are outside the pairwise test; this is not filled-region boolean overlap detection or overlap removal. Each native recording converts QPointF operands to tuples before segment-pen validation; open paths require endPath , closed paths closePath . This receipt validates closed native contours; native open-path coverage remains a follow-up.
title: outline_pens — bounds, direction and complexity (native passed; 0.18 s)

text: naming.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Measured: assigned family, style, preferred and PostScript names read back; family becomes Scripting Sample , PS name ScriptingSample-Regular . Copyright/licence stay intact. The small policy accepts ASCII letters, digits and spaces and enforces the 63-character PS limit. Changes are discarded on close.
title: naming — name a disposable derivative (native passed; 0.12 s)

text: kerning_classes.py uses GG Stroke Chan OFL Italic (OFL-1.1). Measured on the Italic master: default-master pair count, typed pair sides, explicit zero values, class members/modes and dangling member names. The default run(limit=5) returns totals (619 pairs across 79 left sides, 233 classes) and up to five pairs, classes and members per class; run(limit=None) returns complete data. Opaque native modes become text for JSON. No class expansion or OFL font renaming occurs.
title: kerning_classes — pairs retain their meaning (native passed; 0.19 s)

text: designspace.py uses GG Cosm (CC0-1.0). Measured: three masters, one wght axis, separate user/design ranges, master and eight export-instance coordinates in axis order. valueWeight reads design coordinates. The selected master stays unchanged; no interpolation is implied.
title: designspace — axes, masters and instances (native passed; 0.26 s)

text: master_compatibility.py uses GG Plum (CC0-1.0). Measured: A/V/a match across all three masters; reports include closed flags, compatible and missing_layers . Missing layers differ from empty layers. Equal topology does not prove component compatibility, contour correspondence or interpolation quality.
title: master_compatibility — compare direct-contour topology (native passed; 0.23 s)

text: spacing.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). It plans I's shift/new width, moves direct nodes and anchors and reads bearings back. Measured: I's bearings [128, 0], shift 48, new width 416, plus plan and resulting sidebearings . The fixed H/I inputs have direct outlines; only I on the owned font's default master changes. The basic node/anchor move follows the existing sidebearing recipe ; this demo adds an owned real input, an RSB-aware plan and bounds from re-read nodes of the straight-line I outline; native cached boundingBox/contourRect remain stale.
title: spacing — I borrows H's bearings (native passed; 0.11 s)

text: batch_transform.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). run(scale=1.1) preflights both glyphs and scales direct node/anchor x coordinates and advances, retaining y coordinates. Expected: A/V point counts Measured A/V widths: 640 → 704. Readback re-fetches the layer and contours instead of inspecting the wrappers just assigned; anchors and advance widths are checked too. Scaling about x=0 also scales both sidebearings. Only the disposable default master changes; source data stays intact.
title: batch_transform — widen A and V (native passed; 0.11 s)

text: export_ttf.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Native contour pens capture .notdef , space , A , V ; the font closes before Cu2QuPen/TTGlyphPen and FontBuilder create a TTF geometry subset. The native pen adapter detaches QPointF coordinates into ordinary tuples for both exports. Measured: verified: true , format: glyf , retained binary path, exact glyph order/cmap/advances/UPM and full licence name record. Reopened bounds must agree within two units for curve conversion and coordinate rounding. Every contour is also measured with AreaPen after binary reopening: TTF signs must reverse the source signs, and CFF signs must match. winding_verified and per-contour winding reports expose those checks without assuming absolute source winding.
title: export_ttf — compile and reopen quadratic outlines (native passed; 0.17 s)

text: export_otf.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). T2CharStringPen builds the same subset as CFF OpenType. Measured: verified: true , format: CFF and the same readback checks. Both exports accept run(destination="/absolute/new-sample.otf") (use .ttf for TTF); the default retains a new temporary export directory. Existing files and symlinks are refused. Outputs are named Scripting Sample , with complete CC0 text, copyright and public source URL. These geometry subsets omit native hints, features, kerning, axes and other layers. They demonstrate pen interchange, not FontLab's export profiles.
title: export_otf — compile and reopen CFF outlines (native passed; 0.11 s)

text: font_info_ui.py uses GG Stroke Chan OFL Italic (OFL-1.1). It closes the font before showing a QtGui QDialog with a plain text QLabel. Measured: GG Stroke Chan OFL, 106 glyphs, 1000 UPM, Italic master. Retain the handle: tool = font_info_ui.run() , inspect tool.report / tool.widget , call tool.close() in finally , then drain deferred deletion events in the native runner. The Scripting-panel __main__ route calls canonical-module show() , which retains font_info_ui.TOOL even when panel globals are discarded; a second launch closes the predecessor. Native acceptance must exercise this route and verify the plain-text enum, visibility and deferred deletion. Cleanup is idempotent. No signals, QApplication or second loop are created.
title: font_info_ui — a tiny PythonQt tool (native passed; 0.15 s)

text: compare_fonts.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0) and GG Hint (Apache-2.0). Measured: 96 common glyphs, 274 Hint-only glyphs, none Baar-only; width differences in em units (right minus left), using each font's own UPM. Nested owned contexts close both documents even if opening or inspecting the second fails.
title: compare_fonts — compare in em units (native passed; 0.31 s)

text: native_manifest.json lists all entries, fonts, dependencies, observable checks, cleanup and measured native passes from the linked receipt. PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD = 1 uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest -q tests FontLab's run_python has a fixed 5-second deadline . Never execute a complete run() synchronously through it: file opening, import cold starts and compilation can exceed it. Use the Scripting panel or an event-loop callback outside the request, keeping run_python calls to short setup/enqueue/poll operations. Preserve a detached result/error receipt and poll it; a client timeout is not a native pass. Manifest expected entries are machine assertions ( path plus exactly one of equals , len , contains , gt ), executed by _checks.assert_expected(result, row["expected"]) . Paths include dictionary keys, list indices and UI handle attributes. UI cleanup is explicitly handle.close . The manifest's native_followups retain save-prompt, metadata-renormalization, refreshed-bounds, segment-pen and Scripting-panel UI checks for the native worker. Add --with fonttools to uv run and target tests/test_getgo_scripts.py for real pens, binary and winding-tamper checks. No Fontport dependency or legacy scripts.py API remains; the needed master-report helper now lives in designspace.py.
title: Native execution and host-free verification

text: Retained catalogue This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2 , rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples. 106 single-file PythonQt dialogs for everyday font work: anchors, metrics, kerning, outlines, masters, names, guides, font info, features, hinting, cleanup, generators, reports and proofs. Each one works on the current font and offers a master scope where that makes sense; most list what an Apply will change before you press it, and a few (such as mark-colour swatches) apply on click. Report, browser and proof scripts change no font data (some select glyphs, copy to the clipboard or export files). Many glyph-editing tools group their edits into one Undo step, but Undo coverage varies. Seven metrics scripts warn that moved stem hints are not restored, and font-wide data (font info, OpenType features, master settings) is written directly: Italic Angle (Masters) states that Undo does not restore its change. Read each script's notes before applying changes. Copy any file into FontLab's Scripts folder (for example Scripts/Samples ) and run it from the Scripts menu, or open it in the Scripting panel. A script needs only FontLab 9 and its bundled PythonQt; nothing else is installed. Dialogs are modeless, so the Font window stays usable, and every dialog disconnects its signals when closed. Each script was run in FontLab 9.0.9783 through its menu path on disposable copies of GetGo fonts, with screenshots and before/after reads of the changed glyphs. Edits on glyphs used by automatic composites warn first: FontLab may rebuild those composites' anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore that rebuild.
title: Samples: GUI scripts for FontLab 9

text: Script What it does Remove Empty Auxiliary Layers Delete empty auxiliary layers (no outlines, anchors, guides, note or other data) from the selected glyphs. Select Unreferenced Glyphs List unencoded glyphs that nothing references, and select them in the Font window for review.
title: Cleanup (2)

text: Script What it does Bump Font Version Bump the numeric version and version name; optionally append a dated font note. Calculate Vertical Metrics Set hhea, Win (and optionally OS/2 typo) vertical metrics to enclose every glyph, per master. Glyph Order Preview & Export Sort by Unicode, name or Unicode script; export one glyph name per line for the whole font. Master Metrics Table Edit ascender, descender, x-height and cap-height across masters; diagram follows the selected row. Names & Credits Edit family, style, credits and version naming for the current font. Unicode Ranges & Codepage Hints Report OS/2 range bits and complete printable codepage coverage from every glyph encoding; no font changes.
title: Font Info (6)

text: Script What it does Outline Effect Turn the selected glyphs into outlined (hollow) letters. Placeholder Glyphs Create empty placeholder glyphs from pasted glyph names or characters, on every master. Shadow Copy Add a shifted copy of the selected glyphs' outlines as a separate shadow element. Small Caps from Capitals Create small-cap glyphs (h.sc, a.sc ...) from the selected capitals, on every master. Superior & Inferior Figures Create superior (.sups) or inferior (.subs) copies of the selected figures, on every master. Tabular Figure Copies Create tabular (.tf) copies of the selected figures, on every master.
title: Generators (6)

text: Script What it does Clear Glyph Guides Remove glyph guides from the selected glyphs by direction and name. Copy Guides Between Masters Copy the glyph guides of one master to the other masters of the selected glyphs. Font Guides Panel Show the font's guides and add one named guide to every master of the selected glyphs. Grid Generator Add a regular grid of named glyph guides: N lines every S units from an origin. Guide List Editor Edit the glyph guides of one glyph as a table: X, Y, angle and name per master. Metric Reference Lines Add named horizontal glyph guides at the font's vertical metrics, plus an offset.
title: Guides (6)

text: Script What it does Autohint Selected Layers Run FontLab's PostScript autohinter on the selected glyphs, per master. Remove PostScript Hints Remove PostScript stem hints from the selected glyphs, horizontal and/or vertical, per master. Suggest Zones from Overshoots Set PostScript alignment zones from the overshoots of H/O (baseline, caps) and x/o (x-height).
title: Hinting (3)

text: Script What it does Classes Browser Browse kerning classes: their side, members, and every pair that uses them on each master. Compare Masters Line up every kerning pair across all masters and flag the ones that look inconsistent. Copy Between Masters Copy the kerning of one master to other masters, optionally scaled. Exceptions Finder Find kerning exceptions: pairs that override a class pair, and remove the ones you tick. Missing Pairs List the combinations of two glyph groups that no kerning pair covers on a master. Pair Editor Edit every kerning pair that involves one glyph, with one column per master. Pair List Browse every kerning pair of a master: filter, sort by any column, export to CSV. Pairs from Text Type a word, see each adjacent pair's kerning on every master, and set the ones you tick. Remove Small Pairs Delete kerning pairs whose value is smaller than a threshold, on one or all masters. Round Values Round kerning values to a step (5, 10 …) on one or all masters, previewing every change. Scale Values Scale all kerning values by a percentage on one or all masters. Text Preview Set text from the font's outlines with its kerning applied, per master, at any size.
title: Kerning (12)

text: Script What it does Back Up Master Layers Copy the master layers of the selected glyphs to named backup layers before risky edits. Compatibility Check Check that every master of each glyph can interpolate: same contours, nodes, anchors, components. Copy Layer Between Masters Copy the outline (and optionally anchors and advance width) from one master to others. Copy Outline to Mask Copy the outline of each selected glyph's master layer into its mask layer, for reference. Glyph Weight Chart Bar chart of the ink area of the selected glyphs in every master. Interpolation Preview Preview a glyph between two masters with a slider, from the masters' own nodes. Italic Angle Read and set the italic angle of every master, with a painted gauge comparing them. Layer Cleanup List the non-master layers of the selected glyphs (masks, backups, others) and delete the ticked ones. Master Switcher A small palette with one button per master: click to make that master current. Masters Overview One table of all masters: axis location, vertical metrics and italic angle. Restore Backup Layer Restore a backup layer (such as "Regular backup") into the master it was taken from. Sync Sidebearings Copy side-bearings from a reference master to the other masters, proportionally or as-is. Width Chart Line chart of the advance widths of the selected glyphs across masters.
title: Masters (13)

text: Script What it does Alignment Zones Edit the PostScript alignment zones (blue zones) of each master in a table. Centre in Advance Centre the outlines of the selected glyphs in their advance width, optionally with a new width. Copy from Reference Give the selected glyphs the sidebearings or the advance width of a reference glyph. Equalize Sidebearings Make the left and right sidebearings of the selected glyphs equal, on one or all masters. Italic Sidebearings Report and set sidebearings measured along the italic angle, not straight up. Round Advances Round advance widths to a step (2, 5, 10 … units), keeping every outline where it is. Scale Advances Scale the advance widths of the selected glyphs by a percentage, each outline staying centred. Sidebearings Tuner Set, add to or scale the side-bearings of the selected glyphs on one or all masters. Spacing String Preview Render a spacing control string such as HOHnono from the font's own outlines and advances. Tabular Width Give figures (and optionally currency signs) one shared advance width, each outline centred. Vertical Metrics Diagram See and edit ascender, cap height, x-height and descender of every master in one diagram. Width Table Advance widths of the selected glyphs across all masters, sortable, with odd progressions flagged. Zero-Width Marks Set the advance width of combining marks to zero, keeping or re-placing their outlines.
title: Metrics (13)

text: Script What it does Batch Rename Find and replace in glyph names (plain text or regular expression) with a live preview. Case Pairs Find the upper- or lowercase counterparts of the selected glyphs and select them. Character Info A live panel describing the character of the glyph selected in the Font window. Charset Compare Paste a text or a character set and compare it with the font's encoded characters. Duplicate Unicodes Find code points assigned to more than one glyph and remove them from the extra glyphs. Glyph Finder Type to find glyphs by name, character or code point; Enter selects them in the Font window. Glyph Notes Read and edit the note of the selected glyph, and browse every glyph that has a note. Glyph Tags View, add and remove glyph tags across the selected glyphs. Mark Color Palette Click a colour swatch to mark the selected glyphs with it (or clear the mark). Select by Mark Select glyphs in the Font window by their mark colour. Suffix Tool Add, remove or replace a glyph-name suffix (.ss01, .sc, .alt…) on the selected glyphs. Unicode from Names Assign Unicode code points derived from glyph names, with a preview first.
title: Names (12)

text: Script What it does Alternate Glyph Proof Compare a base glyph and its suffixed alternates in each master. Read-only; outlines share one scale per row. Feature Code Inspector Read-only feature source for the whole font. Choose a feature and search its code. Ligature Recipe Finder Find underscore-named glyphs and existing input glyphs. Name-derived recipes do not imply outline components. OpenType Class Browser Browse feature classes and their members. Filter by class name or glyph; font-wide across masters. Suffix Feature Report Suffix inventory across the whole font. Suggestions are naming hints; review the generated code. Suffix Substitution Builder Preview a font-wide suffix substitution. Append to source only; compile and test in the Features panel.
title: OpenType (6)

text: Script What it does Add Extremes Insert on-curve nodes at the horizontal and vertical extremes of curve segments. Contour Order View Show every master of a glyph side by side with numbered contours, start points and directions. Correct Contour Direction Set PostScript contour direction on the selected glyphs and report what changed per master. Delete Duplicate Contours Find contours drawn twice in the same layer and keep only the first copy. Delete Small Contours Remove contours whose area is below a threshold: stray specks left by drawing or tracing. Fix Zero Handles Find curve handles that sit on their own node and clean them up. Node Coordinates Panel A small live panel listing the selected nodes of the current glyph with coordinates. Node Statistics Contours and nodes per glyph and master in one table, with incompatible glyphs flagged. Optimize Start Points Move every contour's start node to its bottom-left on-curve node, consistently across masters. Remove Overlap Remove overlaps on the chosen masters of the selected glyphs, master compatibility checked first. Round Coordinates Round node coordinates of the selected glyphs to a grid, optionally anchors and component offsets. Slant Slant (skew) the selected glyphs by an angle, optionally the font's italic angle. Straighten Short Curves Turn short curve segments whose handles lie on the chord into straight lines. Transform Scale, skew, rotate and move the outlines of the selected glyphs with a live preview.
title: Outlines (14)

text: Script What it does Glyph Grid Show the selected glyphs on every master side by side, drawn from their outlines. Text by Master Render the same text once per master, stacked, to compare weight and width at a glance. Waterfall Render a line of text in a cascade of sizes, drawn straight from the glyph outlines. Word Finder Find real words to proof with: words the font can set, that use the letters you are working on.
title: Proofs (4)

text: Script What it does Empty Glyphs List glyphs that have no outlines and no components on some or all masters, and select them. Font Overview A one-screen dashboard of the current font: glyphs, encoding, masters, kerning, composites. Glyph Info Live A live panel for the glyph you are working on: widths, side-bearings, bounds and counts per master. Glyph Table CSV A sortable table of glyphs (name, Unicode, width per master, contours, components) with CSV export. Label Statistics Count glyphs by mark colour and by name suffix (.sc, .ss01, .loclPLK…); click a row to select them. Nodes Near Zones Find on-curve nodes that sit within a few units of a vertical metric but not on it. Open Contours Find open contours on every master and select the glyphs that have them. Unicode Coverage Unicode coverage of the current font, block by block, with progress bars.
title: Reports (8)

text: Script What it does Batch Glyph Notes Set or append a note on every selected glyph at once.

text: Retained catalogue This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2 , rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples. Purpose. Give every closed contour of the current master PostScript direction: outer contours counter-clockwise, counters clockwise (y-up). Nesting decides which is which, so a counter inside a counter turns outward again. Each contour then starts at its lowest, then leftmost on-curve node, which keeps start points compatible across masters. run () # all glyphs run ( glyph_names = [ "O" , "Q" ]) Orientation and nesting use the actual outline. Nesting is an exact ray-crossing test on the cubic and TrueType quadratic segments (recursive subdivision, not a fixed flattening), so a contour inside a curve's handles but outside the curve is an outer contour, and one hugging the inside of a curve is a counter. The recipe reads and plans every glyph before its first edit, so an unreadable glyph leaves the font unchanged. Collapsed contours (a single node, or all on-curve nodes at one point) have no direction: they are left alone and listed under skipped in the report. FontLab API. flContour.reverse() (keeps the first node, reverses the rest), flContour.setStartPoint(index) , flNode.isOn() . Orientation is computed from the node positions with the shoelace formula: in this FontLab 9 build flContour.clockwise reported False for a contour that runs clockwise in y-up coordinates, so the recipe doesn't rely on it. Native check ( native.py , owned font): an "O" drawn with both contours wrong ends with a counter-clockwise outer contour and a clockwise counter, both starting bottom-left, with the same points; a correct glyph is left alone. Provenance. The kind of task done by the clockwise/counter-clockwise and start-point (bottom-left) buttons of the TypeRig GUI Contour panel ( typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Panel/Contour.py , MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the panel's button labels and tooltips were consulted, never its implementation. Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

Give figures one shared advance width and centre each outline in it. tabular_figures.py is written as an ordinary Glyphs 3 script (in Glyphs it would work on the selected glyphs; its functions were run inside Glyphs 3.5.1 and 4.2 on an in-memory test font, including the anchor move). recipe.py runs the same file, unchanged in FontLab through glyport ( fontlab-glyport ), whose GlyphsApp module is backed by the current FontLab font. run () # zero..nine that exist, width 600 run ( glyph_names = [ "one" , "seven" ], width = 620 ) Bounds are the real outline extents (cubic and quadratic extrema), not the handles. Glyport has no layer.bounds yet, so the script measures the outline from its nodes (which works in Glyphs too). Glyport cannot move anchors yet ( GSAnchor.position write is unsupported), so in FontLab, figures with anchors raise glyport's UnsupportedCapability instead of being left half-moved. The behaviour is the common "tabular figures / centre glyphs in width" task, as in the public mekkablue Glyphs scripts (https://github.com/mekkablue/Glyphs-Scripts, Metrics folder); their code was not read or copied. text: The reference consumes Echopy's captured/enriched Python sources and adjacent stubs. It renders as the actual fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , PythonQt.* namespaces. Runtime inspection is disabled throughout normal documentation builds. Source checkout mode uses sibling ecosystem repositories. Installed artifact mode selects one provisioned Python package directory with FONTLAB_API_SOURCE_ROOT . Private sources are provisioned using authenticated GitHub tooling, without embedding credentials in the project. ./build.sh ./build.sh --check ./build.sh --serve The first environment synchronization may fetch locked dependencies. Once the dependency cache and source inputs exist, normal builds require neither FontLab nor network access. Explicit native refresh is a separate source-production operation; it captures inside FontLab before generation and enrichment. Generated coverage records every identity and exact source hash. Class indexes retain each member occurrence; identical captured text is linked to one full declaration. This sharing does not assert native inheritance or object identity. Before contributing, agree to the repository's FontLab contributor license agreement. Change source or enrichment inputs, regenerate, verify rendered references and cross-links, and include tests for changed behavior. Preserve source attribution and the Qt/PySide documentation licenses.

text: The source-lock helper compares documented inputs with their recorded SHA256 hashes. A normal build refuses changed input bytes. Review producer changes before requesting a lock refresh. Source-lock helper # this_file: scripts/source_lock.py """Pin the exact API source bytes across checkout and installed-artifact builds.""" import json from pathlib import Path def input_hashes ( inputs : list [ dict ]) -> dict [ str , str ]: """Reject duplicate input identities instead of silently dropping their bytes.""" actual = {} for row in inputs : if row [ "source" ] in actual : raise ValueError ( "Duplicate API source input: " + row [ "source" ]) actual [ row [ "source" ]] = row [ "sha256" ] return actual def verify_inputs ( locked : dict [ str , str ], inputs : list [ dict ]) -> None : """Fail for missing, new or modified source; never silently refresh a lock.""" actual = input_hashes ( inputs ) changed = sorted ( name for name in locked . keys () | actual . keys () if locked . get ( name ) != actual . get ( name ) ) if changed : raise ValueError ( "API source lock differs: " + ", " . join ( changed [: 10 ]) + "; use --update-source-lock after reviewing source changes." ) def apply_lock ( path : Path , inputs : list [ dict ], * , update : bool ) -> dict : """Write only when explicitly requested; ordinary builds verify the pin.""" sources = input_hashes ( inputs ) if update : path . write_text ( json . dumps ( { "schema_version" : 1 , "sources" : sources , }, indent = 2 , sort_keys = True , ) + " \n " ) if not path . exists (): raise FileNotFoundError ( "API source lock missing; use --update-source-lock." ) lock = json . loads ( path . read_text ()) verify_inputs ( lock [ "sources" ], inputs ) return lock

text: A report can declare every name it captured while missing an entire namespace. Echopy now restores the useful discovery behavior of the retained introspection tools: it combines advertised and stored names, discovers loaded PythonQt children and tries qualified imports when a child is absent from the root. It preserves ordinary inspection failures instead of silently counting them as successful absence. These five independent experiments use owned Python objects and the actual maintained tooling. Run each block in a fresh namespace. They require the discovery repair from Echopy's issue-123-capture-discovery-20261102 feature; older versions omit some of these scopes. No FontLab, Qt, native framework, font, preference or user document is accessed. Temporary generated declarations in the last experiment belong only to its disposable owned directory. The experiments verify source behavior, not the deployed FontLab API. Existing native-capture, generated-reference, source-lock, site and publication holds remain in force. A successful example does not authorize refreshing those inputs. For live attribute delegation, see native values and aliases .
title: Find API scopes before measuring declaration coverage

text: dir() is useful discovery evidence, but a custom implementation can omit public dictionary names. The collector unions both sources, removes duplicates and dunder names, and sorts the result. It records names and types rather than values. from types import ModuleType from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace class Partial ( ModuleType ): def __dir__ ( self ): return [ "advertised" , "advertised" , "__doc__" ] owned = Partial ( "owned_example" ) owned . advertised , owned . stored = 1 , 2 scope = namespace ( owned , owned . __name__ ) assert scope [ "names" ] == [ "advertised" , "stored" ] assert scope [ "errors" ] == [] assert all ( "value" not in item for item in scope [ "attributes" ])

text: PythonQt can expose pseudo-namespaces as root attributes, separately registered modules, or importable children. Resolution prefers the root object, then the registered immediate child, then a qualified import. A registry name such as PythonQt.A.B identifies candidate A ; it does not invent a flattened A.B . Registry keys are snapshotted before imports can modify them. This experiment temporarily installs only owned module entries and restores them on leaving the context. Empty seeds keep the experiment entirely within those owned objects; they do not model every actual PythonQt namespace. import sys from types import ModuleType from unittest.mock import patch from fontlab_echopy.tooling import capture as tool root = ModuleType ( "PythonQt" ) registered = ModuleType ( "PythonQt.QtOwnedGuide" ) registered . from_registry = 1 with patch . dict ( sys . modules , { "PythonQt" : root , registered . __name__ : registered }): with patch . object ( tool , "QT_SEEDS" , ()): first = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert first [ "subpackages" ][ "QtOwnedGuide" ][ "namespace" ][ "names" ] == [ "from_registry" ] authoritative = ModuleType ( "PythonQt.QtOwnedGuide" ) authoritative . from_root = 1 root . QtOwnedGuide = authoritative second = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert second [ "subpackages" ][ "QtOwnedGuide" ][ "namespace" ][ "names" ] == [ "from_root" ]
title: Discover a loaded child without replacing the root's object

text: An import reporting that the requested child does not exist is an optional absence. A missing dependency inside that child is an inspection failure. The latter keeps its child name and exception type in the report; it must not become a successful empty namespace. Exception messages and local paths are not copied into the error record. The following import hook is an owned experiment, not a substitute implementation of discovery. from types import ModuleType from unittest.mock import patch from fontlab_echopy.tooling import capture as tool def missing_dependency ( name ): raise ModuleNotFoundError ( "owned failure" , name = "owned_dependency" ) root = ModuleType ( "PythonQt" ) with patch . object ( tool , "resolve" , return_value = root ): with patch . object ( tool , "QT_SEEDS" , ( "QtOwnedGuide" ,)): with patch ( "importlib.import_module" , side_effect = missing_dependency ): item = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert item [ "subpackages" ] == {} assert item [ "namespace" ][ "errors" ] == [{ "name" : "QtOwnedGuide" , "error" : "ModuleNotFoundError" }]
title: Distinguish an absent optional child from a broken dependency

text: Ordinary discovery errors preserve other usable scopes. Timeouts, keyboard interrupts and process-exit signals propagate. In particular, swallowing a host trace deadline can disable its execution guard. A failed root getter is recorded once and is not retried by child discovery. from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace class Deadline : def __dir__ ( self ): raise TimeoutError ( "owned deadline" ) try : namespace ( Deadline (), "owned_deadline" ) except TimeoutError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned deadline" else : raise AssertionError ( "A deadline must not become partial API success" )
title: Treat a deadline as cancellation

ClassDef )) operation = next ( node for node in cls . body if isinstance ( node , ast . FunctionDef ) and node . name == "operation" ) assert ast . literal_eval ( operation . args . defaults [ 0 ]) == 3 Actual completeness still requires an approved capture from the intended FontLab build, reconciliation against the real bindings and native behavior checks. Echopy module values and their documentation

text: Echopy keeps a native module value connected to its owner. A read through the facade sees the current object; an accepted module write or deletion reaches the native namespace. The adjacent declaration records documentation and a type without inventing an offline value. Maintainers need to check both routes: correct names alone cannot reveal a hidden write or a lost attribute docstring. This guide explains the source contract with invented, owned modules. The names owned_echopy_values , value-with-dash and _echopy_value below are test inputs, not claims that a FontLab build exposes those names. Every assignment changes an owned ModuleType object. For real native import and read-only class identity examples, start with the Echopy package guide . An arbitrary native module assignment can change application state; these examples do not authorize copying invented assignments into FontLab.
title: Echopy module values and their documentation

text: Use Python 3.11 in a fresh directory that you own, with the Echopy revision being checked and its docs extra already provisioned ( griffe is required). Check fontlab_echopy.__file__ before proceeding so the source or installed copy is unambiguous. No FontLab, native Qt or macOS framework is required. The source runner and installed-prefix runner execute this exact setup anew before each marked example; they never rewrite the setup or example body. Save this setup followed by one marked example in a Python file and run that file. Each example is independent. TemporaryDirectory owns the raw/merged outputs and overlays; leaving the context removes those scratch files and the invented module registrations, even if an assertion fails. title: Set up an owned experiment

text: The first example keeps an earlier local reference, replaces the value through the facade, then changes the native owner directly. Both module reads follow the owner. The earlier local reference keeps ordinary Python snapshot semantics. initial , replacement , final = object (), object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : "value" , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { "value" : initial }) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native saved_reference = facade . value assert facade . value is native . value is initial facade . value = replacement assert facade . value is native . value is replacement native . value = final assert facade . value is native . value is final assert saved_reference is initial Echopy preserves native object identity; it does not clone a value or wrap it in a documentation object. This test proves dispatch on an owned Python module. It says nothing about whether a particular native attribute has a writable setter, accepts a type, or changes a document safely. Native setter errors propagate through either spelling. Any partial native side effects require their own preservation check.
title: Read the current object and forward a write

text: A native name that cannot appear in Python source receives a source identifier. For this invented name, source_name("value-with-dash") is value_with_dash . Use getattr / setattr / delattr for the original spelling; the source identifier supports ordinary attribute syntax. Both routes must reach the same object. Deletion must remove both visible spellings, and re-creation must reconnect them. native_name = "value-with-dash" alias = source_name ( native_name ) assert alias == "value_with_dash" initial , replacement = object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : native_name , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { native_name : initial }) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is facade . value_with_dash is initial facade . value_with_dash = replacement assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is facade . value_with_dash is replacement assert { native_name , alias } . issubset ( dir ( facade )) delattr ( facade , native_name ) assert not hasattr ( native , native_name ) assert not hasattr ( facade , native_name ) and not hasattr ( facade , alias ) assert native_name not in dir ( facade ) and alias not in dir ( facade ) setattr ( facade , alias , initial ) assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is getattr ( facade , native_name ) is initial This is module dispatch. A sanitized class-member declaration does not add a renamed member to an original native class: returning that class unchanged preserves its identity. Consult the native spelling with getattr when needed. The package import aliases echopy and fontlab_echopy are a separate mechanism; the package guide checks those.

text: The runtime keeps _echopy_native , _echopy_name and _echopy_aliases local. Its child-facade import bookkeeping also remains special, so importing a child facade cannot overwrite a native pseudo-namespace. These rules do not reserve all _echopy_ spellings. The generator separately refuses helper-name collisions before writing output; do not broaden its refusal policy to hide valid names. This matrix exercises accepted invented names at both raw and merged stages. It writes by both spellings, checks exact runtime state identities, deletes and checks dir() again. _echopy_builtins is an accepted invented value here; raw generation selects another private import alias when that name is occupied. None of these spellings is asserted to exist in the running FontLab. for stage in ( "raw" , "merged" ): for native_name in ( "_echopy_value" , "_echopy-value" , "_echopy_value-with-dash" , "_echopy_builtins" ): for route in ( native_name , source_name ( native_name )): initial , replacement = object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : native_name , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { native_name : initial }, stage = stage ) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native state = { key : facade . __dict__ [ key ] for key in ( "_echopy_native" , "_echopy_name" , "_echopy_aliases" )} setattr ( facade , route , replacement ) assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , source_name ( native_name )) is replacement assert all ( facade . __dict__ [ key ] is value for key , value in state . items ()) delattr ( facade , route ) assert not hasattr ( native , native_name ) for spelling in { native_name , source_name ( native_name )}: assert not hasattr ( facade , spelling ) and spelling not in dir ( facade )

text: An annotation is documentation, not a value assignment. The generated source and merged sidecar record an AnnAssign without a value. Offline loading keeps the annotation while attribute reads fail. AnnAssign )) assert value . value is None and ast . unparse ( value . annotation ) == "str" For callable declarations, offline operations raise NativeUnavailable ; see unavailable native operations . A missing annotation-only value instead has normal absent-attribute behavior. A dir() entry or a declared type is not proof that an offline value exists.
title: Keep annotation-only values absent offline

text: Here a property object is stored directly on a plain owned module. Reading that module member returns the descriptor itself; capture can read its documentation without invoking the property getter. The deliberately failing getter makes the boundary testable. This is not a claim that every native module getattr is side-effect free, nor permission to run a fresh capture against a live host. calls = [] def forbidden_getter ( owner ): """Owned captured descriptor documentation.""" calls . append ( owner ) raise AssertionError ( "The property getter must never run" ) owned = ModuleType ( OWNED_NATIVE ) owned . value = property ( forbidden_getter ) captured = capture_namespace ( owned , OWNED_NATIVE ) before = copy . deepcopy ( captured ) assert captured [ "attributes" ][ 0 ][ "doc" ] == forbidden_getter . __doc__ with owned_pipeline ( captured ) as case : raw_text = ( case . raw / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .py" ) . read_text () stub_text = ( case . output / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .pyi" ) . read_text () assert forbidden_getter . __doc__ in raw_text and forbidden_getter . __doc__ in stub_text assert case . result == { "applied" : 0 , "unmatched" : []} assert captured == before and calls == [] Capture records errors explicitly. Documentation and a recorded descriptor type do not establish whether a native property is readable, writable or callable. A docstring that includes parentheses is not enough to turn an attribute into a method. Preserve recorded fields and limitations rather than guessing a setter.
title: Capture descriptor documentation without invoking its getter

text: The generator accepts module attributes , constants and modules collections. Those are input collections; capture need not classify every object into all three. Each collection emits an annotation followed immediately by its captured docstring. The adjacent string belongs to the annotated value for documentation consumers; moving it to the module header loses that association. for collection in ( "attributes" , "constants" , "modules" ): captured_doc = f "Owned { collection } documentation." scope = { collection : [{ "name" : "value-with-dash" , "type" : "Any" , "doc" : captured_doc }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope ) as case : for path in ( case . raw / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .py" , case . output / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .pyi" ): tree = ast . parse ( path . read_text ()) index = next ( i for i , node in enumerate ( tree . body ) if isinstance ( node , ast . AnnAssign )) annotation , documentation = tree . body [ index : index + 2 ] assert annotation . target . id == "value_with_dash" and annotation . value is None assert isinstance ( documentation , ast . Expr ) assert documentation . value . value == captured_doc assert not hasattr ( case . facade , "value_with_dash" ) Unknown captured types remain Any . That expresses missing type information; it does not mean every object can safely be passed to a native setter. The Python annotated assignment AST records the target, annotation and optional value independently.
title: Preserve docs for each value collection

text:
Overlay keys use the emitted source identifier: owned_echopy_values.value_with_dash for native value-with-dash . On annotated attributes, the existing returns field specifies the annotation override; it does not call a getter or describe a method return. doc supplies supplemental prose and source gives its origin. Overlays are combined in list order, field by field. A later field replaces the earlier value for that field. Omitting a field in a later overlay retains the earlier setting. The following intentionally includes one unmatched native-name key to show the diagnostic, then verifies the correctly targeted source key. The later doc replaces the earlier supplemental doc; the earlier float type survives. Captured documentation remains first and appears once. scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : "value-with-dash" , "type" : "int" , "doc" : "Captured value." }]} first = { f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .value_with_dash" : { "doc" : "First supplement." , "returns" : "float" , "source" : "owned-first" }} last = { f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .value_with_dash" : { "doc" : "Final supplement." , "source" : "owned-final" }, f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .value-with-dash" : { "doc" : "Wrong target." }} with owned_pipeline ( scope , overlays = [ first , last ]) as case : assert case . result == { "applied" : 1 , "unmatched" : [ f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .value-with-dash" ]} tree = ast . parse (( case . output / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .pyi" ) . read_text ()) index = next ( i for i , node in enumerate ( tree . body ) if isinstance ( node , ast . AnnAssign )) annotation , documentation = tree . body [ index : index + 2 ] assert ast . unparse ( annotation . annotation ) == "float" assert documentation . value . value == ( "Captured value. 

 Supplemental documentation: 
 " "Final supplement. 

 Source: owned-final" ) assert "First supplement." not in documentation . value . value An unmatched target must be investigated. It can mean a spelling error, an obsolete capture target or a patch for another producer; a green identity count does not prove the overlay was applied. text: Detailed value docs belong in the sidecar. Native loading must not parse that sidecar merely to obtain a value. This example generates an owned facade, removes its sidecar only inside the temporary directory, and re-executes it while its owned native module remains registered. title: Retain the acceptance boundaries
Preserve distinct foreground layers with repeated names

text: glyph.layers keeps declared master slots first, followed by other valid stored foreground identities in native order. A repeated name does not merge records. String lookup uses exact IDs; it does not add an ambiguous display-name alias. Missing declared masters retain pending slots without creating native layers. FontLab's isMasterLayer is name-derived and also recognizes interpolation and bracket names. It is broader than a declared master slot. Current upstream source shows that case-sensitive findLayer(name) selects the last matching stored identity. Glyport uses that finder consistently, then assigns separate tokens to the remaining foreground records. Its public isMasterLayer describes the declared slot, not that broader native name classification. These experiments run the actual backend, Model and layer proxies against owned Python objects. Only the native boundary data and finder are invented; no projection, lookup, cache or history algorithm is replaced. They make no FontLab, Qt, framework, font, preference, selection or document calls. Run the visible setup afresh before each tagged body.

The six fields are case , group , script , category , subCategory and direction ; their flags are storeCase , storeGroup , storeScript , storeCategory , storeSubCategory and storeDirection . The summary runs at the intermediate barrier before those rows are appended, so its script list need not contain han . with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) assert manager is not GSGlyphsInfo . sharedManager () assert len ( manager . _index . records ) == 71 + 38206 + 4 ranges = [( 0x2E80 , 0x2E99 ), ( 0x2E9B , 0x2EF3 ), ( 0x2F00 , 0x2FD5 ), ( 0x3400 , 0x57EE ), ( 0x57EF , 0x7BDC ), ( 0x7BDD , 0x9FFF ), ( 0xF900 , 0xFAD9 ), ( 0x30000 , 0x3134A ), ( 0x31350 , 0x323AF ), ( 0x2EBF0 , 0x2EE5F )] for first , last in ranges : for scalar in range ( first , last + 1 ): code = f " { scalar : 04X } " row = manager . _index . unicodes [ code ] assert row . name == ( "uni" if first <= 0xFFFE else "u" ) + code assert row . sortName == ( "uni0" if first <= 0xFFFE else "unj" ) + code assert row . script == "han" and row . category == "Letter" and row . _locked assert manager . _index . names [ row . name ] is row assert [ row . index for row in manager . _index . records ] == list ( range ( 38281 )) for gap in ( "2E9A" , "3134B" , "3134F" , "323B0" , "2EE60" ): assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( gap ) is None assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "2E80" ) . subCategory == "Radical" assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "F900" ) . subCategory == "Compatibility" for code , sort_name , subcategory in [( "2FF0" , "uni02FF0" , "Compatibility" ), ( "20000" , "unj20000" , "Compatibility" ), ( "20001" , "unj20001" , None ), ( "20002" , "unj20002" , None )]: row = manager . _index . unicodes [ code ] assert ( row . sortName , row . subCategory ) == ( sort_name , subcategory ) raw = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "30000" ) for profile in ( "glyphs2" , "glyphs3" , "glyphs4" ): app , font = owned_exports ( manager , profile ) assert app . Glyphs . glyphInfoForUnicode ( 0x30000 , font = font ) is raw assert app . title: Inspect every fixed Chinese range and profile lookup

text: The generation jobs consult the captured Unicode map before committing their new rows. A pre-existing encoding suppresses a generated row. A pre-existing name with another encoding does not. The final name map can therefore select a new row while the old encoding still selects the original row. Repeated bank entries remain distinct listed records; the last commit wins in both maps. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): provider . base . write_text ( provider . base . read_text () + '<glyph name="uni2FF0" unicode="E000" script="owned" subCategory="Other"/>' ) provider . banks = (( "2FF0" , "2FF0" , "0041" ), ( "20000" ,), ( "20000" ,), ( "20002" ,)) manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) old = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "E000" ) current = manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "uni2FF0" ) assert old . name == current . name and old is not current assert old . unicode == "E000" and current . unicode == "2FF0" duplicates = [ row for row in manager . _index . records if row . unicode == "2FF0" ] assert len ( duplicates ) == 2 and duplicates [ 0 ] is not duplicates [ 1 ] assert current . _resolved_record is duplicates [ - 1 ] assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "2FF0" ) is current assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "0041" ) . name == "owned.base" assert not any ( row . name == "uni0041" for row in manager . _index . records ) repeated = [ row for row in manager . _index . records if row . unicode == "20000" ] assert len ( repeated ) == 2 and repeated [ 0 ] is not repeated [ 1 ] assert manager . _index . unicodes [ "20000" ] is repeated [ - 1 ] assert manager . _index . names [ "u20000" ] is repeated [ - 1 ]
title: Distinguish name collisions from Unicode identity

text: Each Chinese callback collects a whole chunk before publishing it. The final listed order follows callback completion order, and the commit uses the captured name and Unicode maps. This invented reverse scheduler runs every callback and all fixed ranges, but finishes the last submitted job first. It demonstrates a second permitted order; it does not model concurrent native queue timing. class ReverseQueue ( OwnedQueue ): def waitUntilAllOperationsAreFinished ( self ): self . events . append (( "wait" , self )) while self . pending : self . pending . pop ()() with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): def reverse_queue (): queue = ReverseQueue ( provider . events ) provider . queues . append ( queue ) return queue provider . new_queue = reverse_queue manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) rows = manager . _index . records assert len ( rows ) == 38281 assert rows [ 71 ] . name == "u2EBF0" and rows [ - 1 ] . name == "uni2FD5" assert manager . _index . unicodes [ "2EBF0" ] is rows [ 71 ] assert manager . _index . names [ "uni2FD5" ] is rows [ - 1 ] assert all ( row . index == position for position , row in enumerate ( rows )) assert manager . _index . unicodes [ "AC00" ] . _component_records == ( manager . _index . unicodes [ "1100" ], manager . _index . unicodes [ "1161" ]) assert not manager . _lifecycle . queue . pending
title: Keep chunk completion order visible

text: The queued operation visits every syllable from AC00 through D7A3 . For each one it looks up the target, leading Jamo, vowel Jamo and optional trailing Jamo, in that order. This example checks the three supplied syllable targets against Unicode NFD and checks their exact component-record identities. It exercises the complete operation even though the fixture stores only three syllable targets. Unicode NFD supplies an independent scalar oracle, not a proprietary recipe bank. import unicodedata with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) for code in ( 0xAC00 , 0xAC01 , 0xD7A3 ): target = manager . _index . unicodes [ f " { code : 04X } " ] expected = tuple ( manager . _index . unicodes [ f " { ord ( part ) : 04X } " ] for part in unicodedata . normalize ( "NFD" , chr ( code ))) assert len ( expected ) == ( 2 if code == 0xAC00 else 3 ) assert target . _component_records == expected assert all ( actual is wanted for actual , wanted in zip ( target . _component_records , expected )) assert target . _locked and target . baseString == chr ( code ) view = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( f " { code : 04X } " ) assert all ( part . _resolved_record is raw for part , raw in zip ( view . components , expected )) assert not manager . _lifecycle . queue . pending
title: Match actual Hangul target and Jamo identities

text: The generated-component adapter replaces the raw component tuple, clears its old name list and removes only the components unavailable-field marker. It does not rerun general component finalization or rebuild unrelated caches. The following snapshot checks every existing raw field by identity. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) raw = manager . _index . unicodes [ "AC00" ] raw . baseString , raw . unicharString = "keep base" , "keep cached text" raw . _component_names = [ "old names" ] raw . _unavailable_fields = frozenset ({ "components" , "owned unknown" }) before = vars ( raw ) . copy () manager . _addHangulGlyphInfos () assert raw . _component_names is before [ "_component_names" ] manager . _lifecycle . queue . waitUntilAllOperationsAreFinished () assert raw . _component_records == ( manager . _index . unicodes [ "1100" ], manager . _index . unicodes [ "1161" ]) assert raw . _component_names is None assert raw . _unavailable_fields == frozenset ({ "owned unknown" }) for field in before . keys () - { "_component_records" , "_component_names" , "_unavailable_fields" }: assert vars ( raw )[ field ] is before [ field ], field
title: Preserve locks and caches when replacing component storage

text: Enqueuing captures the manager, not a frozen index snapshot. Replacing a target or Jamo in its Unicode map before execution changes the later component links. These direct map assignments are owned source controls; production callers should use their qualified loading path. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) old = manager . _index . unicodes [ "AC00" ] retained = old . _component_records manager . _addHangulGlyphInfos () target , vowel = new_record ( "owned.new.target" ), new_record ( "owned.new.vowel" ) add_unicode ( target , "AC00" ) add_unicode ( vowel , "1161" ) manager . _index . unicodes [ "AC00" ] = target manager . _index . unicodes [ "1161" ] = vowel assert target . _component_records is None manager . _lifecycle . queue . waitUntilAllOperationsAreFinished () assert target . _component_records == ( manager . _index . unicodes [ "1100" ], vowel ) assert target . _component_records [ 1 ] is vowel assert old . _component_records is retained assert manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "owned.AC00" ) . _resolved_record is old assert manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "AC00" ) . _resolved_record is target
title: Resolve the current Unicode map after enqueue

text: The following subclass explicitly injects a missing Jamo lookup. A real lookup may synthesize a result, so deleting a raw map key alone does not establish a nil lookup. The full queued operation completes AC00 , then fails while constructing the AC01 component tuple. Its error escapes the wait; the earlier assignment and the unrelated later queue entry remain. The constructor's protected enqueue interval does not catch an error raised by a later callback. class MissingTrailing ( GSGlyphsInfo ): def glyphInfoForUnicode_ ( self , code ): return None if code == "11A8" else super () . glyphInfoForUnicode_ ( code ) with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) receiver = MissingTrailing . _from_index ( manager . _index ) receiver . _lifecycle = manager . _lifecycle target = manager . _index . unicodes [ "AC00" ] target . _component_records = None receiver . _addHangulGlyphInfos () marker = [] receiver . _lifecycle . queue . addOperationWithBlock_ ( lambda : marker . append ( "later" )) try : receiver . _lifecycle . queue . waitUntilAllOperationsAreFinished () except InfoNativeException as error : assert "AC01" in str ( error ) and "nil" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "Missing Jamo must refuse the deferred tuple" ) assert target . _component_records == ( manager . _index . unicodes [ "1100" ], manager . _index . unicodes [ "1161" ]) assert len ( receiver . _lifecycle . queue . pending ) == 1 and marker == []
title: Retain partial writes and pending work on deferred failure

text: The full generator requires each of four lawful lists or tuples of strings. An absent bank is a dependency refusal; it does not become an empty successful callback. The constructor below fails during the Chinese intermediate barrier. It does not append any partially collected Chinese rows or drain the remaining jobs on unwind. The supplied base rows remain and later work stays queued. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): provider . chinese_codes = lambda slot : None if slot == 2 else provider . banks [ slot ] receiver = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () try : receiver . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphsInfo.provider.chinese_codes" else : raise AssertionError ( "Missing lawful bank must refuse initialization" ) assert len ( receiver . _index . records ) == 71 assert "2E80" not in receiver . _index . unicodes assert receiver . _lifecycle . queue . pending assert receiver . _lifecycle . iMatraCombinations is None

title: Legacy Unicode snapshots and ROS metadata

text: The global name factory reads maintained GlyphData. Its unicode and unicodeLegacy fields answer different questions: Requested name Canonical name unicode unicodeLegacy A A "0041" None alef-ar alef-ar "0627" None alef-ar.isol alef-ar.isol None "FE8D" aleffinalarabic alef-ar.fina None "FE8E" The owned application fixture supplies no host bridge or persistent defaults. It does not activate the synthetic GlyphsApp module. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for name , primary , legacy in [ ( "A" , "0041" , None ), ( "alef-ar" , "0627" , None ), ( "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ), ]: info = app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) Aliases resolve to the maintained canonical record, including its legacy field. They do not create a second independent primary-Unicode record. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) alias = app . glyphInfoForName ( "aleffinalarabic" ) canonical = app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.fina" ) assert alias . name == canonical . name == "alef-ar.fina" assert alias . unicode is canonical . unicode is None assert alias . unicodeLegacy == canonical . unicodeLegacy == "FE8E" The shared Unicode index includes each record’s primary keys followed by its non-nil legacy key in source order; later assignments replace earlier ones. Global Unicode lookup therefore selects alef-ar.isol for FE8D , with primary Unicode None and legacy Unicode FE8D . It selects hamza-ar.isol for FE80 and the later NULL record for duplicated 0000 . These examples qualify specific maintained records, not complete custom GlyphData. The linked guide separates exact combined-index lookup, raw synthesis on a true miss and remaining input boundaries.
title: Keep primary and legacy Unicode separate

text: Omitting font , passing positional None or using font=None selects shared data without reading the active font. An explicit font now selects that font's manager; the earlier unconditional .localData refusal is superseded. Integer Name dispatch discards font only in Glyphs2/3; Glyphs4 forwards it through the instance Unicode method. See the current manager/profile examples . The fixture below preserves active-font isolation while explicitly checking selected-manager delegation and propagation of an invalid font's access error. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class UnreadableFont : def __getattribute__ ( self , name ): raise AssertionError ( "Global lookup must not read an active font" ) active = UnreadableFont () app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = active ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , None ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = None ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" local = owned_parsed_manager () explicit = SimpleNamespace ( glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = explicit ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "alef-ar.isol" ) try : app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = active ) except AssertionError as error : assert str ( error ) == "Global lookup must not read an active font" else : raise AssertionError ( "An explicitly selected invalid font must expose its access failure" )
title: Global lookup ignores active-font data

text: Direct GSGlyphInfo construction from a namespace snapshots the supplied legacy value exactly. Missing means None ; empty strings, lowercase hex and arbitrary owned text remain distinct. Editing the source object later does not edit the snapshot. This package makes snapshots read-only and refuses assignment with GSGlyphInfo.unicodeLegacy . Native Glyph Info has a setter; package read-only policy does not describe the native object's mutability. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSGlyphInfo for legacy in ( None , "" , "fe8d" , "unparsed owned value" ): source = SimpleNamespace ( name = "owned" , unicode = None , unicodeLegacy = legacy , category = "Letter" , subCategory = None , script = "arabic" , case = 0 ) snapshot = GSGlyphInfo ( source ) source . unicodeLegacy = "changed" assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == legacy try : snapshot . unicodeLegacy = "FE8D" except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.unicodeLegacy" else : raise AssertionError ( "The package snapshot must be read-only" ) assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == legacy del source . unicodeLegacy assert GSGlyphInfo ( source ) . unicodeLegacy is None
title: Snapshot raw values without normalizing them

text: For an actual package GSGlyph , the constructor resolves only the new legacy field through owned metadata. Existing name, primary Unicode, category, subcategory, script and case snapshot behaviour is retained. This constructor does not replace those fields with a wholesale resolved record. Resolution can refuse unsupported data; it does not query a native application. An unencoded alef-ar.isol draft has a legacy value without acquiring an encoding. A generic derived suffix clears inherited legacy metadata. A nil resolved record gives no legacy value, even when the stored name resembles an isolated-form record. An already captured snapshot remains independent. Global indexing and model postprocessing are different paths. The detached, already encoded Arabic glyph below still reaches the retained parentless Arabic nil-return branch: its snapshot keeps stored primary FE8D and legacy None . Direct global lookup of FE8D returns alef-ar.isol with database primary None and legacy FE8D . The shared-index correction does not bypass the model branch. from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSGlyphInfo from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph glyph = GSGlyph ( "alef-ar.isol" ) snapshot = GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) assert ( snapshot . name , snapshot . unicode , snapshot . unicodeLegacy ) == ( "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ) assert glyph . unicodes == [] with owned_parsed_manager () . _scope (): glyph . name = "alef-ar.isol.owned" assert GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) . unicodeLegacy is None assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" encoded = GSGlyph ( "alef-ar.isol" ) encoded . unicode = "FE8D" current = GSGlyphInfo ( encoded ) assert current . unicode == "FE8D" and current . unicodeLegacy is None assert encoded . unicodes == [ "FE8D" ] assert GSGlyphInfo ( GSGlyph ( "unknown-owned" )) . unicodeLegacy is None
title: Construct from an owned model glyph

text: The audited shared manager places ROS replacement after additional Unicode and before Arabic presentation. With its actual maps, it replaces the complete ordered Unicode set using the resolved metadata name . Glyport does not bundle those proprietary MapFiles. Adobe CMaps and maintained GlyphData are not equivalent substitutes; no approximated map is supplied. The exact shared-manager text contract is: Split on a hyphen ( - ). Only when that result has a count other than three, retry with comma plus one space ( , ). Require exactly three pieces. Preserve case and whitespace. Use the first two pieces for the map name. Ignore the supplement; it need not be numeric or nonempty. Requests naming Adobe-CNS1 , Adobe-GB1 , Adobe-Japan1 , Adobe-KR or Adobe-Korea1 raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData before presentation and metadata writes. The guard cannot know whether a particular glyph would be absent from the unavailable map, so that does not bypass refusal. The revision comparison below is an explicitly owned backend diagnostic, not native dirty-state proof. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend for ordering in ( "CNS1" , "GB1" , "Japan1" , "KR" , "Korea1" ): for separator in ( "-" , ", " ): for supplement in ( "7" , "" , "owned" ): backend = FakeBackend () font = Model ( backend ) . font glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] font . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = separator . join (( "Adobe" , ordering , supplement )) before = ( glyph . name , glyph . unicodes , glyph . case , glyph . script , glyph . category ) revision = backend . revision ( "font" ) try : glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unavailable ROS mapping must refuse" ) assert ( glyph . name , glyph . unicodes , glyph . case , glyph . script , glyph . category ) == before assert backend . revision ( "font" ) == revision
title: Recognize ROS requests before writing

text: Nil, malformed text and unknown map names leave the preceding record unchanged at the ROS stage. That shared-bundle no-op does not make an entire metadata refresh a no-op: earlier additional-Unicode processing can still add encodings. It is not a guarantee about arbitrary custom managers or user-supplied resources. For example, Adobe,Japan1,7 lacks the required spaces. Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra-more has exactly three hyphen pieces, so comma fallback is suppressed and no shipped map matches. Conversely, Adobe-Japan1-7\n and Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra still require the missing map: the supplement is ignored after delimiter selection. from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend for value in ( None , "" , "Adobe-Japan1" , "Adobe-Japan1-7-extra" , "Adobe,Japan1,7" , "Adobe, Japan1, 7" , " Adobe-Japan1-7" , "adobe-Japan1-7" , "Adobe-Unknown-7" , "Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra-more" ): font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] font . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = value glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . name == "A" assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0041" , "0061" ] # Earlier additional-Unicode stage. Normal first-active parameter selection applies to ROS. An inactive or shadowed map request is not the selected value. Nontext values require an unqualified Objective-C description conversion; they raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.value rather than using Python str , truthiness or an invented native representation. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] first = GSCustomParameter ( "ROS" , "Adobe-Unknown-7" ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , GSCustomParameter ( "ROS" , "Adobe-Japan1-7" )]) glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0041" , "0061" ] first . active = False try : glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData" else : raise AssertionError ( "The now-selected map request must refuse" ) other = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font other . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () other . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = False try : other . glyphs [ "A" ] . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.value" else : raise AssertionError ( "Nontext ROS description is unqualified" )
