text: The same collection supports two different questions: Operation Meaning parameters["Name"] Value of the first active matching parameter, or None "Name" in parameters A matching object exists, including an inactive one parameters[index] The actual ordered parameter object parameters["Name"] = value Change the first matching object, retaining its active flag; append if absent parameters["Name"] = None Remove the first matching object del parameters["Name"] Remove the first match; missing or empty names are a no-op parameters.remove(parameter) Remove that parameter object (by identity); ValueError if it is not in the collection Indexed replacement/deletion Replace/remove that position and detach the old object Do not treat name lookup as an ordinary dictionary when duplicates or inactive entries matter. A name assignment can change an inactive object while a later active duplicate still supplies the effective value. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font first = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "first" ) second = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "second" ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , second ]) assert font . customParameters [ 0 ] is first assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "first" first . active = False assert "Owned Setting" in font . customParameters assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second" font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] = "changed inactive object" assert first . value == "changed inactive object" and not first . active assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second" font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] = None assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ second ] assert first . parent is None first . value = "detached edit" assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second"
title: Choose a value or an object

text: Insertion order is retained. insert uses strict bounds rather than clamping a large positive or negative index. A negative index adds the current length once; insert(-1, parameter) therefore inserts before the last item. Replacing or removing an object detaches it, while the supplied replacement becomes live. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font first = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned duplicate" , 1 ) later = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned duplicate" , 2 ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , later ]) font . customParameters . remove ( later ) assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ first ] # Removal is by object identity. assert later . parent is None before = GSCustomParameter ( "Before last" , 3 ) font . customParameters . insert ( - 1 , before ) assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ before , first ] replacement = GSCustomParameter ( "Replacement" , 4 ) font . customParameters [ - 1 ] = replacement assert first . parent is None and replacement . parent is font try : font . customParameters . insert ( 99 , GSCustomParameter ( "Outside" , 0 )) except IndexError : pass else : raise AssertionError ( "Out-of-range insertion must not clamp silently" ) Iteration captures the initial count and fetches each object as it advances. Appending does not extend an existing iterator; shrinking the collection can make its next indexed access raise IndexError . Finish iteration before editing its structure, or collect the intended positions first. Nested mutation of an attached value container is not a qualified notification route; assign the whole replacement value instead. Same-object multiple insertion, cross-owner reparenting and complete native identity remain open. A copied parameter owns its nested value but retains its recorded parent pointer; a copy is not proven to be a detached native object.
title: Keep positional edits explicit

text: A font and its masters have distinct parameter collections. Ordinary master userData excludes reserved parameter storage and preserves it when other user data changes. The presentation setting is read from the glyph's parent font ; a master parameter does not enable the font setting. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font master = font . masters [ 0 ] master . userData [ "Owned note" ] = { "tags" : [ "proof" ]} font . userData [ "Owned font data" ] = 7 master . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "master" )) font . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "font" )) assert master . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "master" assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "font" assert dict ( master . userData ) == { "Owned note" : { "tags" : [ "proof" ]}} master . userData [ "Another note" ] = 8 assert master . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "master" assert dict ( font . userData ) == { "Owned font data" : 7 } The persistence representation uses ordered records and compatible flat-key mirrors. Old flat values import in their former sorted order because the old format recorded no original insertion order or active flags. New external flat names are retained. An external edit or deletion of an existing mirrored value wins: the collection follows the flat keys, reads never raise, and one CUSTOM_PARAMETERS_REBUILT warning is queued. This storage diagnostic reconstructs a Python model over the same owned backend. It is not a native font save/reopen test: from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend from fontlab_glyport.model.proxies import CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX backend = FakeBackend () # "font" is this test backend's owned font identity, not a native font ID. backend . set_lib ( "font" , { CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX + "Z owned" : [ 1 ], CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX + "A owned" : 2 , "unrelated" : { "keep" : [ 3 ]}, }) font = Model ( backend ) . font assert [ p . name for p in font . customParameters ] == [ "A owned" , "Z owned" ] font . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "A owned" , 4 )) font . customParameters [ 0 ] . active = False reconstructed = Model ( backend ) . font assert [( p . name , p . active ) for p in reconstructed . customParameters ] == [ ( "A owned" , False ), ( "Z owned" , True ), ( "A owned" , True ) ] assert reconstructed . customParameters [ "A owned" ] == 4 assert backend . lib ( "font" )[ "unrelated" ] == { "keep" : [ 3 ]}
title: Separate font, master and user data

text: The exact key is Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes , including its spaces and case. UseArabicPresentationFormUnicodes is a different key. Prefer an explicit Boolean for a setting; raw Python truthiness does not describe the upstream string-conversion rules. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "alef-ar" )) font . masters [ 0 ] . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] # A master setting does not enable it. font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . name == "alef-ar" assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] # Ordered deduplication. font . customParameters [ KEY ] = False glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] # Refresh removes the previous addition. The ordinary additional-Unicode helper and this presentation stage are separate. The former has its own gates and uses ordinary .isol.unicode ; legacy-only .isol data does not become a primary encoding just because that helper ran. Presentation instead reads unicodeLegacy . A separately named .isol glyph can block the earlier helper's manager lookup without blocking the presentation stage's raw legacy lookup.
title: Enable Arabic presentation encodings

text: The stage tests the resolved record's script, then uses its canonical name. A direct non-nil unicodeLegacy takes precedence. Only nil triggers a raw <resolved name>.isol database lookup. An empty string is non-nil: it blocks fallback, then adds no encoding. Additions retain order, deduplicate and follow the upstream nonempty/shorter-than-eight length gate. Generic constructed suffixes clear inherited legacy; direct database suffix records retain their own. Implemented ordering is resolution/private-use handling, the ordinary additional-Unicode helper, ROS processing, presentation processing, then stored metadata overlays. Requests for the five proprietary shipped ROS maps now refuse before presentation and metadata writes because their mapping data is unavailable. Malformed/unknown text leaves this stage unchanged under the audited shared-bundle contract. See the legacy and ROS guide for exact delimiters, supplement handling, nontext refusal and owned no-write examples. Full ROS mapping, complete local initialization/private resources and unqualified suffix routes remain outside this bounded example matrix. A stored Latin script does not suppress presentation on an Arabic resolved record; the overlay runs later. Conversely, storing Arabic script on a Latin resolved record does not make it an Arabic presentation candidate. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () alias = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "OwnedArabicAlias" )) alias . unicode = "0627" alias . storeScript = True alias . script = "latin" font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True alias . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert alias . name == "OwnedArabicAlias" and alias . script == "latin" assert alias . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] Resetting a storage flag refreshes that metadata field without writing encodings. The next explicit refresh can apply presentation encodings. Native name-collision adjustment is a separate open route: it can clear encodings even with changeName=False . The no-conflict examples do not prove that route. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "alef-ar" )) glyph . storeScript = True glyph . script = "latin" font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "arabic" and glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ]
title: Direct, nil and empty legacy data

text: For this exact BOOL-schema key, plain Python bool , int and float retain their numeric type and precision; None on the object becomes False . Assigning None by parameter name still removes the first matching object. A string containing the current locale's decimal separator uses real NSNumberFormatter parsing, then float32. Other strings use NSString.integerValue. The default formatter is process-cached; an explicit locale below owns a temporary formatter and changes no global preferences. Input and route Result Enables presentation? Numeric 0.5 Retained 0.5 Yes Numeric 1e-46 Retained double precision Yes String "YES" or "true" Integer 0 No String "1e-3" without the decimal separator Leading integer 1 Yes String "1.0e-46" , dot-decimal locale Float32 0.0 No String "0,5" , comma-decimal locale Float32 0.5 Yes Malformed decimal "0.5junk" , dot-decimal locale Nonzero float 2**63 sentinel Yes The failed-parse sentinel is an upstream quirk established by retained machine code and independent Foundation observations. It is not a recommendation to use malformed input. Guessing bool(text) or treating every parse failure as zero would change the setting's behaviour. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend from fontlab_glyport.model.parameter_numbers import normalize assert normalize ( "YES" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0 assert normalize ( "true" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0 assert normalize ( "0,5" , locale_name = "de_DE" ) == 0.5 assert normalize ( "1.0e-46" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0.0 assert normalize ( 1e-46 ) == 1e-46 assert normalize ( "0.5junk" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == float ( 2 ** 63 ) KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font parameter = GSCustomParameter ( KEY , True ) font . customParameters . append ( parameter ) parameter . value = None assert parameter . value is False and len ( font . customParameters ) == 1 font . customParameters [ KEY ] = None assert len ( font . customParameters ) == 0 This string route is measured on macOS 27.2 arm64 Foundation, not every Foundation version. Non-macOS strings and arbitrary object/container conversions explicitly raise UnsupportedCapability ; their implementation/qualification remains open. Existing numeric NaN retains numeric enabling semantics and must not be mistaken for an external mirror conflict. Active-value cache construction validates all active duplicates, including shadowed ones. Indexed/name/active inspection and name-based removal remain available for an inactive imported value whose conversion is unsupported. Name membership is a separate object lookup that can still validate the first matching object; it is not a substitute for those recovery operations.
title: Read typed values on macOS

text: The numerical ordinary-artifact results below identify their retained predecessor checkpoint. The current manager/profile guide documents the H source changes. Earlier source assumptions are corrected below; original preimages remain in verification evidence. Old receipts do not qualify the new ordinary tuple or native behavior. Read GSGlyphInfo.productionName when you need the stored production metadata of an identified record. Keep None , empty text and explicit text distinct. An explicit value equal to the nice name remains that text; it is not changed to None . This describes the retained Glyphs 4 getter contract implemented by the current private source candidate, not every Glyphs version or a published release. The field is separate from GSGlyph.production , glyph storage flags and Glyphs.productionGlyphName . A Glyph Info read does not qualify those glyph write/export or application conversion workflows. Access Production result Direct Unicode record Read its stored value without filling it Exact represented name or accepted alias Fill a known nil value, then read it Explicit empty value Preserve it; exact-name access does not fill it Copied record Retain the value present when the copy was made Generic derived suffix Compute the derived output from its base and exact suffix tokens Metadata with no established production source Raise an explicit unsupported-capability error All examples below use owned data and actual exported classes outside FontLab. They exercise source behavior through ExecutionContext and FontLabSession , with empty packages/defaults and inert host objects. They do not run an original script, access user fonts or create a native application. title: Stored production names in Glyph Info

text: Run this setup once before the examples. It temporarily substitutes a small owned in-memory dataset and restores the maintained dataset in finally . It never edits the dependency's source files or dictionaries. This is a test fixture; a normal script obtains Glyphs and the classes from its own GlyphsApp execution context. from contextlib import contextmanager from pathlib import Path from types import ModuleType from glyphsLib import glyphdata from fontlab_glyport import ExecutionContext from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp.fontlab_session import FontLabSession @contextmanager def owned_glyphs ( rows ): glyphdata . get_glyph ( "A" ) previous = glyphdata . GLYPHDATA records = [ dict ( row ) for row in rows ] names = { row [ "name" ]: row for row in records } alternatives , productions , encodings = {}, {}, {} for row in records : for alias in row . get ( "altNames" , "" ) . replace ( " " , "" ) . split ( "," ): if alias : alternatives [ alias ] = row if row . get ( "production" ): productions [ row [ "production" ]] = row if row . get ( "unicode" ): encodings [ row [ "unicode" ]] = row owned = glyphdata . GlyphData ( names , alternatives , productions , encodings ) ctx = ExecutionContext ( Path . cwd (), "glyphs3" ) session = FontLabSession ( ctx , version = ( 3.2 , 3234.0 ), packages = [], defaults = {}, qt = object (), fontlab = ModuleType ( "fontlab" ), ) ctx . adapters . update ( session . adapters ()) glyphdata . GLYPHDATA = owned try : with ctx : yield ctx . import_module ( "GlyphsApp" ) finally : ctx . close () glyphdata . GLYPHDATA = previous assert records == rows , "Queries must preserve the owned source records"
title: Prepare an owned offline session

text: A known absent field is None . Empty text is a present value. Both an explicit nice-name value and a different explicit production value survive direct and exact-name reads. The raw nil example uses a fresh dataset: an earlier name query can already have filled that shared record. rows = [ { "name" : "nil" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "empty" , "unicode" : "0042" , "production" : "" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "equal" , "unicode" : "0043" , "production" : "equal" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "explicit" , "unicode" : "0044" , "production" : "OwnedProd" , "category" : "Letter" }, ] with owned_glyphs ( rows ) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName is None for code , name , expected in [ ( "0042" , "empty" , "" ), ( "0043" , "equal" , "equal" ), ( "0044" , "explicit" , "OwnedProd" ), ]: assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( code ) . productionName == expected assert app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . productionName == expected assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "nil" ) . productionName == "nil"
title: Preserve nil, empty, equal and explicit values

text: Exact names, alternate names and accepted production aliases refer to the same represented record. A name read fills only a nil stored value. A raw handle obtained earlier observes that fill. copy and deepcopy retain independent production values from the time they were copied; neither is a live view of the later shared fill. from copy import copy , deepcopy with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "ownedLetter" , "unicode" : "0041" , "altNames" : "ownedAlias" , "script" : "latin" , "category" : "Letter" , }]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs raw = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) shallow , deep = copy ( raw ), deepcopy ( raw ) assert raw . productionName is None alias = app . glyphInfoForName ( "ownedAlias" ) assert ( alias . name , alias . productionName ) == ( "ownedLetter" , "ownedLetter" ) assert raw . productionName == "ownedLetter" assert shallow . productionName is None and deep . productionName is None
title: Observe shared fill and independent copies

text: A bare character that reaches Unicode lookup retains the raw shared record. A represented single-record uni or u name takes a copy, preserving its raw production at that time. Exact stored names still take priority over decoding. A direct Unicode miss can synthesize a record whose production is its constructed name. The name-factory fallback for a rejected scalar is a different route with a known nil value; these results do not qualify general complex-name synthesis. with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "ownedLetter" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" , }]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs raw = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) uni = app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041" ) u = app . glyphInfoForName ( "u0041" ) assert raw . productionName is None assert uni . productionName is None and u . productionName is None app . glyphInfoForName ( "ownedLetter" ) assert raw . productionName == "ownedLetter" assert uni . productionName is None and u . productionName is None synthesized = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0378" ) assert ( synthesized . name , synthesized . productionName ) == ( "uni0378" , "uni0378" ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "u10FFFF" ) . productionName is None
title: Distinguish Unicode text, uni/u copies and synthesized records

text: The manager's production helper computes an output; it does not rewrite an existing explicit raw field. Its represented rules are: Preserve nonempty explicit text, except a seven-UTF16-unit lowercase uni value with four-UTF16-unit Unicode produces uni plus that Unicode. For nil or empty helper input with Unicode, private-use encodings and Latin dotted/hyphenated names use uni or u plus the unchanged Unicode text. Other encoded names use the nice name. Without Unicode, remove hyphens and retain dots. If removal leaves empty text, retain the original name. Those helper rules do not override the getter's empty-value preservation. Derived suffix results expose the distinction. UTF16 units matter: a supplementary character occupies two units, unlike Python's scalar count. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "owned-ar" , "unicode" : "0627" , "production" : "uniFFFF" , "script" : "arabic" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "empty-latin" , "unicode" : "00C1" , "production" : "" , "script" : "latin" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "utf16" , "unicode" : "0041" , "production" : "uni😀xx" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "owned-name" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0627" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "owned-ar.ss01.alt" ) . productionName == "uni0627.ss01.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0627" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "empty-latin" ) . productionName == "" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "empty-latin.alt" ) . productionName == "uni00C1.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "utf16.alt" ) . productionName == "uni0041.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName == "uni😀xx" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "owned-name" ) . productionName == "ownedname"
title: Keep normalization separate from the stored getter

text: The represented name lookup follows record order. Each record contributes its primary name, its production alias unless it starts with lowercase uni , and then alternate names. Later assignments win, even over an earlier primary name. The maintained public loader normalizes separator spaces in alternate names. Direct Unicode still selects its own stored record, even when that record's name has been shadowed in the name index. Lowercase uni exclusion applies to a production alias alone; it does not remove an exact stored primary name. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "earlier" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "later" , "production" : "earlier" , "altNames" : "First, Second" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "uni0041" , "production" : "Exact" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "excludedAlias" , "production" : "uni0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "earlier" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . name == "earlier" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName is None assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "First" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "Second" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041" ) . productionName == "Exact"
title: Preserve alias order and lowercase uni exclusions

text: Generic suffix output appends the exact remaining tokens to the base helper output. Repeated and empty suffix tokens are retained. A represented longer prefix takes priority over a shorter base; intermediate synthesized prefixes are not invented. Global lookup can fill the chosen shared base. The special case / cap context copies before its fill, preserving the earlier raw record. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "A.alt" , "unicode" : "0042" , "production" : "OwnedLongest" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A.alt.ss01..ss01" ) . productionName == "OwnedLongest.ss01..ss01" raw = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) assert raw . productionName is None cap = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A.cap" ) assert ( cap . case , cap . productionName ) == ( 1 , "A.cap" ) assert raw . productionName is None A represented canonical suffix after a uni/u copy has a separate boundary. When the last token is consumed, the copy retains the raw production of that canonical record. With tokens remaining, the helper computes their derived output. The canonical record's explicit raw value remains unchanged. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "A.alt" , "unicode" : "0042" , "unicodeLegacy" : "E001" , "production" : "uniFFFF" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs consumed = app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041.alt" ) assert ( consumed . name , consumed . unicode , consumed . unicodeLegacy ) == ( "A.alt" , None , None ) assert consumed . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041.alt.ss01" ) . productionName == "uni0042.ss01" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0042" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF"
title: Retain suffix tokens and choose the represented longest prefix

text: A model's Glyph Info can share a global raw production field until a copy branch applies. An enabled stored metadata flag forces a copy even when its value is equal to the resolved value. The example uses an owned fake font backend; it does not qualify an actual FontLab edit, history step or saved font. from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }]) as exports : app , Info = exports . Glyphs , exports . GSGlyphInfo shared_glyph = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font . glyphs [ "A" ] stored_glyph = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font . glyphs [ "A" ] shared = Info ( shared_glyph ) stored_glyph . case = 0 stored_glyph . storeCase = True detached = Info ( stored_glyph ) assert shared . productionName is None and detached . productionName is None app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) assert shared . productionName == "A" assert detached . productionName is None Private-use renaming also copies before a later global fill. Additional-Unicode and Arabic presentation processing have distinct lookup order: the additional stage can fill an isolated named record, while presentation reads that record raw. Copying can occur even if an encoding is already present. None of these metadata fixtures establish glyph production storage or export behavior. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "ownedPrivate" , "unicode" : "E123" , "category" : "Private Use" , }]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs glyph = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "ownedPrivate" )) detached = exports . GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) assert detached . productionName is None app . glyphInfoForName ( "ownedPrivate" ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "E123" ) . productionName == "uniE123" assert detached . productionName is None from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend rows = [ { "name" : "owned-ar" , "unicode" : "0627" , "script" : "arabic" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "owned-ar.isol" , "unicodeLegacy" : "FE8D" , "script" : "arabic" , "category" : "Letter" }, ] with owned_glyphs ( rows ) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs isolated = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "FE8D" ) glyph = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "owned-ar" )) detached = exports . GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) assert isolated . productionName == "ownedar.isol" assert detached . productionName is None app . glyphInfoForName ( "owned-ar" ) assert detached . productionName is None with owned_glyphs ( rows ) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs isolated = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "FE8D" ) font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font glyph = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "owned-ar" )) glyph . unicodes = [] font . customParameters [ "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" ] = True detached = exports . GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) assert isolated . productionName is None assert detached . productionName is None
title: Keep model copy boundaries distinct

text: Known nil metadata is different from metadata whose production source is unestablished. Classification inferred by a library does not establish a production value. The latter getter raises GSGlyphInfo.productionName.source ; do not replace that exception with a guessed None , empty string or sanitized export name. The qualified snapshot remains read-only: attempts to assign its production name refuse separately. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }]) as exports : unknown = exports . GSGlyphInfo ( SimpleNamespace ( name = "owned" , unicode = None , category = None , subCategory = None , script = None , case = 0 , )) try : value = unknown . productionName except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.productionName.source" else : raise AssertionError ( "An unavailable source must refuse" ) known = exports . Glyphs . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) try : known . productionName = "changed" except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.productionName" else : raise AssertionError ( "The snapshot must remain read-only" ) assert known . productionName == "A"
title: Refuse an unavailable source explicitly

title: Keep the qualified scope visible
Understand sidebar trees and document metadata

text: The manager state, ranks and placeholder-font experiments show raw container identity, retained rank caches, debug/shared construction, observer cleanup and source-derived font/error control flow over visible owned primitives. Actual native fonts/defaults/resources remain separately qualified. A sidebar tree is a view of current font data, saved visibility preferences and filter resources. Its rows also hold mutable parent, count and scheduling state. These experiments show which objects survive each operation, when work actually runs, and what remains after a failure. They use the current Glyport algorithms over invented inputs. They do not open a font or contact FontLab. The described bodies are pinned to Glyport source checkpoint 788959172108d684bf84816d53aeca2d392eba6f . Matching ordinary installations and native behavior require their own verification. Start with metadata managers and execution profiles for record lookup and complete local loading. The examples here complement that guide: filtering a row is different from expanding its name list, and counting it is different again from publishing the result.
title: Understand sidebar trees and document metadata

text: Run the owned graph setup , followed by the glyport-local-lifecycle setup in connected local initialization . Then run the following sidebar setup and the document setup below. For every tagged experiment, execute all four setup blocks in that order in a fresh namespace, then execute that single example body. Examples do not depend on earlier example mutations. GSGlyphsInfo and GSDocument are actual exported classes. SidebarItem and InfoState are implementation surfaces used explicitly for source experiments. Attaching an InfoState below exercises selected dynamic operations without pretending to initialize complete resources. The document experiment instead calls the actual initializer, parsers, sidebar builder and queued summaries. The provider supplies individual primitives: defaults, a comparison function, predicate objects and count results, field access, record allocation/copy/name assignment, alerts and dispatch. It never implements tree filtering, name-list expansion, count precedence, Smallcaps processing or publication. Its localization is deliberately identity localization; its comparator deliberately sorts in reverse order. Empty folders and nil-array no-op handling are explicit fixture choices. title: Prepare the experiments

text: Hidden state reads the defaults provider on every access, using the current row identifier. A missing provider is a capability error, rather than a hidden or visible default. This makes a renamed identifier a different preference key. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "OwnedGreek" ) assert item . hidden is False item . setHidden_ ( True ) assert p . defaults == { "GSSidebarItemHidden_OwnedGreek" : True } p . defaults [ item . hiddenKey ()] = False assert item . hidden is False item . setIdentifier_ ( None ) assert item . hiddenKey () == "GSSidebarItemHidden_(null)" item . setHidden_ ( True ) assert item . hidden is True try : _ = SidebarItem () . hidden except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert "defaults_bool_for_key" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "Missing defaults must refuse" )
title: Read the current preference key

text: Filtering first locks the font, reads the script collection and constructs the owned set, even for an empty group. Hidden rows with no predicate disappear. The exact script == prefix takes the UTF16 range (11, length - 12) unless the format contains the exact string OR . It does not parse a predicate grammar. The emoji below occupies two UTF16 units; lowercase or still takes the shortcut. General counts use option 1 inside their own lock/unlock pair. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) for pattern , scripts , counts , expected , general in [ ( 'script == "😀"' , [ "😀" ], {}, True , False ), ( 'script == "latin" OR name == "A"' , [], { 'script == "latin" OR name == "A"' : 2 }, True , True ), ( 'script == "latin" or name == "A"' , [ "latin" ], {}, False , False ), ]: item = row ( p , "Owned" , predicate = p . compile_predicate ( pattern )) item . setHidden_ ( True ) group = row ( p , "Group" ) group . setSubItems_ ([ item ]) p . events . clear () answer = manager . filterGroup_forFont_ ( group , OwnedFont ( p , scripts = scripts , counts = counts )) assert answer is ( group if expected else None ) assert any ( e [ 0 ] == "general-count" for e in p . events ) is general assert sum ( e == ( "lock" ,) for e in p . events ) == ( 2 if general else 1 ) assert sum ( e == ( "unlock" ,) for e in p . events ) == ( 2 if general else 1 ) item . setPredicate_ ( p . compile_predicate ( "script == " )) try : manager . filterGroup_forFont_ ( group , OwnedFont ( p )) except ValueError as error : assert "UTF-16 range" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "Malformed exact shortcut must retain its range failure" )
title: Distinguish the UTF16 shortcut from general counting

text: A partial projection allocates a plain SidebarItem , transfers selected fields through their setters and reparents the retained original children. It does not copy them. Setting transferred list coverage schedules a count; transferring codes or the old badge is not part of this projection. The original group still contains the same child whose parent now points to the projection. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) old = row ( p , "Original" , coverage = [ "A" ]) kept , removed = row ( p , "Kept" ), row ( p , "Removed" ) removed . setHidden_ ( True ) old . setSubItems_ ([ kept , removed ]) old . codes , old . badgeString , old . editable = [ "0041" ], "old badge" , True projected = manager . filterGroup_forFont_ ( old , OwnedFont ( p )) assert type ( projected ) is SidebarItem and projected is not old assert projected . subItems == [ kept ] and projected . subItems [ 0 ] is kept assert old . subItems == [ kept , removed ] assert kept . parent is projected and removed . parent is old assert projected . coverage is old . coverage assert projected . codes is None and projected . badgeString is None assert projected . editable is False and projected . isCalculating () assert p . events [ - 1 ] == ( "schedule" , 10_000_000 ) drain ( p . pending ) # No current font: update does no work and calculating stays set. assert projected . isCalculating () and not p . main
title: Keep original child identities when projecting
Order, categories and current resource reads

text: Category order follows the font's first encounters. Missing categories form the Other group, with an explicit NULL predicate. Only subcategories use the supplied comparison primitive. The mapping changes icon names; no mapping entry leaves the category name as the icon name. No native image is loaded here. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) font = OwnedFont ( p , rows = [ SimpleNamespace ( category = "Mark" , subCategory = "Below" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = None , subCategory = "" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = "Mark" , subCategory = "Above" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = "Letter" , subCategory = None ), ]) groups = manager . categoriesFromFont_categoryToIconMapping_ ( font , { "Mark" : "OwnedIcon" }) assert [ g . identifier for g in groups ] == [ "Mark" , "Other" , "Letter" ] assert [ g . iconName for g in groups ] == [ "OwnedIcon" , "Other" , "Letter" ] assert [ g . identifier for g in groups [ 0 ] . subItems ] == [ "Below" , "Above" ] assert groups [ 0 ] . subItems [ 0 ] . parent is groups [ 0 ] assert groups [ 1 ] . predicate . predicateFormat == "category == NULL" assert groups [ 1 ] . subItems is None assert all ( g . cellType == "ImageTextCell" for g in groups )
title: Retain encounter order and sort only subcategories

text: The first receiver supplies default category overrides. Its dictionary object, including a nil result, becomes the process-once result. Later receivers and providers cannot refresh it merely by calling the method again. Mutations to that same returned dictionary remain visible. The isolated cache context keeps these experiments from contaminating other source examples. first , later = SidebarPrimitives (), SidebarPrimitives () first . mapping = { "Mark" : "base" , "Retained" : "keep" } first . category_rows = [{ "name" : "Mark" , "icon" : "override" }] later . mapping = { "Mark" : "later" } with fresh_category_cache (): with using_info_provider ( first ): mapping = GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () assert mapping is first . mapping assert mapping == { "Mark" : "override" , "Retained" : "keep" } mapping [ "OwnedNew" ] = "new" with using_info_provider ( later ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is mapping assert later . events == [] and mapping [ "OwnedNew" ] == "new" with fresh_category_cache (): first . mapping = None with using_info_provider ( first ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is None with using_info_provider ( later ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is None
title: Share the first category mapping object

text: Image lookup tries the original name, compact name and their Template forms, then system symbols. A successful image is cached on the row. Changing the stored icon name alone does not clear that image. These owned image objects are plain tokens; no image registry or native UI is consulted. p = SidebarPrimitives () image , calls = object (), [] def image_named ( name ): calls . append ( name ) return image if name == "OwnedIconTemplate" else None p . image_named = image_named item = row ( p , "Icon" ) item . setIconName_ ( "Owned Icon" ) assert item . icon is image assert calls == [ "Owned Icon" , "OwnedIcon" , "Owned IconTemplate" , "OwnedIconTemplate" ] item . setIconName_ ( "Changed" ) assert item . icon is image and len ( calls ) == 4
title: Resolve an icon once per row

text: The builder reads fontType() twice and, for a nonempty first tag result, reads allTags again for coverage. It does not cache a final tree. These intentionally changing primitives make the repeated reads observable: the first type creates categories; the second type still includes languages. Tags take the second coverage object and schedule actual count work. Prefix construction stops at the first nil item, while later languages/tags/filters can still be appended. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) state . allItem = row ( p , "All" ) state . languagesGroup = row ( p , "LANGUAGES" ) language = row ( p , "OwnedLanguage" ) state . languagesGroup . setSubItems_ ([ language ]) custom = row ( p , "OwnedFilter" ) state . filterGroups = [ custom ] coverage = [ "second tag" ] font = OwnedFont ( p , types = ( 3 , 0 ), tags = ([ "first tag" ], coverage ), rows = [ SimpleNamespace ( category = "Letter" , subCategory = None ), ]) with fresh_category_cache (): tree = manager . glyphGroupsTreeForFont_ ( font ) assert [ g . identifier for g in tree ] == [ "All" , "CATEGORIES" , "LANGUAGES" , "TAGS" , "OwnedFilter" ] assert tree [ 2 ] is state . languagesGroup and tree [ - 1 ] is custom assert tree [ 3 ] . coverage is coverage and tree [ 3 ] . cellType == "TagsCell" assert [ e for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] == "fontType" ] == [( "fontType" , 3 ), ( "fontType" , 0 )] assert [ e [ 1 ] for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] == "tags" ] == [[ "first tag" ], coverage ] state . allItem = None state . filterGroups = None again = manager . glyphGroupsTreeForFont_ ( OwnedFont ( p )) assert again == [ state . languagesGroup ] assert p . events [ - 1 ] == ( "owned-nil-array" ,)
title: Observe repeated tree reads and tag coverage

text: The reload method replaces filter storage only after its actual loader returns. An exception leaves the old array in place. Successful processing still uses the persistent name map: duplicate identifiers do not replace the first map identity, although new filter rows are returned. The example invokes the real file-list loader and group processor, with only the property-list read supplied. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) p . filter_rows = [{ "name" : "Owned first" , "id" : "same" }] manager . reloadCustomFilterGroup () old = manager . filterGroups () mapped = state . name2Group [ "same" ] original_read = p . load_property_list def broken_read ( path ): raise OSError ( "owned unreadable filter" ) p . load_property_list = broken_read try : manager . reloadCustomFilterGroup () except OSError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned unreadable filter" else : raise AssertionError ( "Read failure must propagate" ) assert manager . filterGroups () is old p . load_property_list = original_read p . filter_rows = [{ "name" : "Owned second" , "id" : "same" }] assert manager . reloadCustomFilterGroup () is None assert manager . filterGroups () is not old new = manager . filterGroups ()[ 0 ] . subItems [ 0 ] assert new . name == "Owned second" and new is not mapped assert state . name2Group [ "same" ] is mapped assert new . parent is manager . filterGroups ()[ 0 ]
title: Reload filters without inventing rollback
Row insertion, copying and delayed work

text: Copying retains coverage and infos by identity while recursively copying children. Normal count values reset; the shallHaveCount == -2 sentinel preserves counts and badge. Bulk insertion outside the current array bounds inserts at zero. Removing a child removes duplicate occurrences but retains its old parent field. p = SidebarPrimitives () parent = row ( p , "Parent" , coverage = [ "A" ]) a , b , c = row ( p , "A" ), row ( p , "B" ), row ( p , "C" ) children = [ a ] parent . setSubItems_ ( children ) parent . insertObject_inSubItemsAtIndex_ ( b , 1 ) parent . insertSubItems_atIndex_ ([ c , b ], 100 ) assert parent . subItems is children and children == [ c , b , a , b ] parent . removeSubItemsObject_ ( b ) assert children == [ c , a ] and b . parent is parent parent . infos , parent . count , parent . shallHaveCount = [ record ( "A" )], 1 , 2 parent . badgeString = "1/2" duplicate = parent . copyWithZone_ ( None ) assert duplicate . coverage is parent . coverage and duplicate . infos is parent . infos assert duplicate . subItems [ 0 ] is not c and duplicate . subItems [ 0 ] . parent is duplicate assert c . parent is parent assert ( duplicate . count , duplicate . shallHaveCount , duplicate . badgeString ) == ( - 1 , - 1 , None ) parent . shallHaveCount = - 2 preserved = parent . copyWithZone_ ( None ) assert ( preserved . count , preserved . shallHaveCount , preserved . badgeString ) == ( 1 , - 2 , "1/2" ) nil_array = row ( p , "Nil array" ) nil_array . insertObject_inSubItemsAtIndex_ ( b , 500 ) assert nil_array . subItems is None and b . parent is nil_array

text: Setting a font expands its current manager's name list and schedules a delayed count, then forwards to children. A second assignment while calculating changes the weak reference without adding a second count request. The scheduled body reads that current reference, so it counts the second font. A collected font becomes nil; nil-font count work does not clear calculating state. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Codes" ) item . codes = [ "0041" , "0042" ] first = OwnedFont ( p , label = "first" , codes = [ "0041" ]) second = OwnedFont ( p , label = "second" , codes = [ "0041" , "0042" ]) item . setFont_ ( first ) item . setFont_ ( second ) assert len ( p . pending ) == 1 and item . font is second drain ( p . pending ) assert ( "codes-count" , "second" ) in p . events assert item . count == - 1 and len ( p . main ) == 2 drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 2 , 2 , "✓" ) assert not item . isCalculating () item . setFont_ ( first ) del first gc . collect () assert item . font is None drain ( p . pending ) assert item . isCalculating () and not p . main
title: Resolve the weak font when the callback runs

text: Both range endpoints are looked up by name, then every code is looked up in the current Unicode index. Repeated rows remain repeated. A reversed range is consumed without output. Missing endpoint Unicode falls back to the whole name token and the new-record primitive. A nil record inside a valid range raises, preserving old infos and original coverage. p = SidebarPrimitives () a , b , c = record ( "A" , "0041" ), record ( "B" , "0042" ), record ( "C" , "0043" ) lookup = Lookup ({ "A" : a , "C" : c }, { "0041" : a , "0042" : b , "0043" : c }) item = row ( p , "Range" , coverage = [ "A:C" , "A" , "C:A" , "missing:end" ]) original = item . coverage item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert item . coverage is original assert item . infos [: 4 ] == [ a , b , c , a ] assert item . infos [ 4 ] . name == "missing:end" old = item . infos lookup . codes . pop ( "0042" ) item . coverage = [ "A:C" ] try : item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) except InfoNativeException as error : assert "range contains nil" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "A nil range member must fail" ) assert item . infos is old and item . coverage == [ "A:C" ]
title: Expand inclusive ranges without deduplicating

text: An ASCII-leading multi-unit alias with a different stored name is renamed. Locked records are copied first; unlocked records are renamed in place. These are explicit owned record fields, not inferred proprietary metadata. A malformed list member clears stored coverage and warns once per item name, but expansion continues over the original array. Later valid members are still included. p = SidebarPrimitives () locked , mutable = record ( "canonical" , locked = True ), record ( "mutable" ) lookup = Lookup ({ "Alias" : locked , "MutableAlias" : mutable }) item = row ( p , "Owned malformed list" , coverage = [ "Alias" , 123 , "MutableAlias" , "Alias" ]) item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert item . coverage is None assert [ r . name for r in item . infos ] == [ "Alias" , "MutableAlias" , "Alias" ] assert item . infos [ 0 ] is not locked and locked . name == "canonical" assert item . infos [ 1 ] is mutable and mutable . name == "MutableAlias" assert item . infos [ 2 ] is not item . infos [ 0 ] assert sum ( e [ 0 ] == "modal" for e in p . events ) == 1 item . coverage = [ False , "Alias" ] item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert sum ( e [ 0 ] == "modal" for e in p . events ) == 1 assert len ( item . infos ) == 1 and item . infos [ 0 ] . name == "Alias"
title: Copy locked aliases and retain the original enumerator

text: Nonempty infos take precedence over predicate and codes. Expected count includes only infos with type zero. Calculation enqueues a working checkmark, then a publication callback. Until those callbacks run, stored count fields are unchanged. Only changed tuples emit hasShallHaveCount notifications. Repeating a successful publication still clears calculating and updates the badge. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Count" , predicate = p . compile_predicate ( "must not count" )) item . infos = [ record ( "A" ), record ( "B" , kind = 1 ), record ( "C" )] item . codes = [ "ignored" ] font = OwnedFont ( p , names = [ "A" , "C" ]) item . setIsCalculating_ ( True ) item . updateCount_ ( font ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( - 1 , - 1 , None ) assert len ( p . main ) == 2 and not any ( e [ 0 ] == "predicate-count" for e in p . events ) p . main . pop ( 0 )() assert item . badgeString == "✓" and item . count == - 1 p . main . pop ( 0 )() assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 2 , 2 , "✓" ) notifications = [ e for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] in ( "will" , "did" )] assert notifications == [( "will" , "hasShallHaveCount" , - 1 , - 1 ), ( "did" , "hasShallHaveCount" , 2 , 2 )] item . setIsCalculating_ ( True ) item . _publish_count ( 2 , 2 ) assert not item . isCalculating () assert [ e for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] in ( "will" , "did" )] == notifications
title: Separate calculation from main-thread publication

text: The exact case-two predicate supplies the expected source count; .sc lookup retains available records. The case-three predicate supplies the actual count. The resulting list is assigned to infos , while missingInfos remains intact. A marked exception in the second filter keeps the newly computed expected count but leaves old infos and the base count in place. Ordinary Python errors are not swallowed by this marked native-exception analogue. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Smallcaps" ) item . codes = [ "0041" ] sentinel = item . missingInfos = [ record ( "untouched" )] source_pattern = "(case == 2) AND NOT (name contains '.0') AND (export == True)" p . filtered [ source_pattern ] = [ record ( "a" ), record ( "b" )] p . filtered [ "case == 3" ] = [ record ( "a.sc" )] sc = record ( "a.sc" ) font = OwnedFont ( p , manager = Lookup ({ "a.sc" : sc }), names = [ "a.sc" ], codes = [ "0041" ]) item . updateCount_ ( font ) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 1 , 2 , "1/2" ) assert item . infos == [ sc ] and item . infos [ 0 ] is sc assert item . missingInfos is sentinel old_infos = item . infos p . filtered [ "case == 3" ] = InfoNativeException ( "owned second filter failure" ) item . updateCount_ ( font ) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount ) == ( 1 , 2 ) assert item . infos is old_infos and item . missingInfos is sentinel assert any ( e [ 0 ] == "log" and "second filter failure" in e [ 1 ] for e in p . events ) assert old_infos == [ sc ]
title: Follow Smallcaps success and partial failure

text: Calling this selector is an explicit source experiment. Python does not invoke Objective-C automatic class initialization. For five active processors, the retained float32 half-count and nearest-away rounding yield three workers, with QoS 17. A second call retains the first queue object. This queue is independent of a manager's queue and does not itself replace the delayed scheduler primitive. from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import info_sidebar_support class CountQueue : def setMaxConcurrentOperationCount_ ( self , count ): self . limit = count def setQualityOfService_ ( self , quality ): self . quality = quality p = SidebarPrimitives () queue = CountQueue () allocations = [] def new_queue (): allocations . append ( queue ) return queue p . new_queue = new_queue p . active_processor_count = lambda : 5 saved = info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized , info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue try : info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized = False info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue = None with using_info_provider ( p ): SidebarItem . initialize () SidebarItem . initialize () assert allocations == [ queue ] assert ( queue . limit , queue . quality ) == ( 3 , 17 ) assert info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue is queue finally : ( info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized , info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue ) = saved
title: Initialize the independent sidebar queue explicitly

text: The format setter catches only marked compilation failures, queues an alert and retains the previous predicate. It does not assign predicateFormat , create the constructor's fallback predicate or force a stop badge. Marked count failures instead report error 992 and publish (-2, -2) . They deduplicate by the current predicate format; an ordinary error still propagates before publication. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Owned count failure" ) item . setPredicateFormat_ ( "owned prior" ) prior = item . predicate item . setPredicateFormat_ ( "owned bad filter" ) assert item . predicate is prior and item . predicateFormat is None assert item . count == - 1 and len ( p . main ) == 1 drain ( p . main ) assert p . events [ - 1 ] == ( "alert" , "owned compilation failure" ) p . predicate_counts [ "owned prior" ] = InfoNativeException ( "owned count failure" ) item . updateCount_ ( OwnedFont ( p )) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( - 2 , - 2 , None ) assert ( "error" , 992 ) in p . events p . predicate_counts [ "owned prior" ] = ValueError ( "ordinary error" ) try : item . updateCount_ ( OwnedFont ( p )) except ValueError as error : assert str ( error ) == "ordinary error" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unmarked errors must propagate" ) assert len ( p . main ) == 1 # The working badge was already queued before failure. drain ( p . main )
title: Keep compilation and count errors distinct

text: The document calls its file primitives rather than treating a path string as an NSDocument. The following setup supplies URL selectors and a superclass file setter only. Optional observer methods on the owned subclass record their order; they do not watch the filesystem. All font data lives in a temporary owned tree. class OwnedURL : def __init__ ( self , name , parent = None ): self . name , self . parent = name , parent def path ( self ): return self . name def URLByDeletingLastPathComponent ( self ): return self . parent def isEqual_ ( self , other ): return isinstance ( other , OwnedURL ) and self . name == other . name class FilePrimitives : def __init__ ( self , url , kind = "com.schriftgestaltung.glyphs" ): self . url , self . kind , self . events = url , kind , [] def file_url ( self , document ): return self . url def set_file_url ( self , document , url ): self . events . append ( "super-set-url" ) self . url = url def file_type ( self , document ): return self . kind class OwnedDocument ( GSDocument ): def stopObservingFile ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "stop" ) def startObservingFile ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "start" ) def updateFileObservers ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "update" )
title: Documents: real local loading and explicit missing adapters

text: The document computes the parent URL before entering its manager lock. It keeps the old local manager until the new initializer returns. This example runs the actual sidebar initialization, local XML parsing, shared-manager fallback and queue drain through the earlier complete lifecycle fixture. The first load's temporary rows are real parsed invented data, rather than a fabricated manager return. title: Global Unicode Glyph Info

text: Glyphs2/3 bind String , with a capital S; Glyphs4 binds string_or_int . The human-readable label Unicode is not a keyword alias. Missing/unknown/ duplicate arguments fail at Python binding before lookup. Current indexed records retain canonical record views. Public NFD does not establish a physical metadata recipe; an unknown components source now refuses instead of publishing NFD as that recipe. The example checks that public refusal, then verifies a known owned recipe. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication , GSGlyphInfo app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = None )) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( String = "004a" , font = None ) . name == "J" info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "00C1" ) assert isinstance ( info , GSGlyphInfo ) and info . name == "Aacute" try : _ = info . components except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.components.source" else : raise AssertionError ( "Public NFD does not establish a physical recipe" ) manager = owned_parsed_manager () manager . updateComponentsInfos () info = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "00C1" ) assert [ part . name for part in info . components ] == [ "A" , "acutecomb" ] assert all ( isinstance ( part , GSGlyphInfo ) for part in info . components ) info . components . clear () assert [ part . name for part in info . components ] == [ "A" , "acutecomb" ] try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( Unicode = "0041" ) except TypeError : pass else : raise AssertionError ( "Unicode is not the executable keyword" ) Current known component records are shallow references in independent returned lists. Explicit custom finalization shows an established recipe without inferring one from an encoding or outline.
title: Call the executable keyword

text: Glyphs3 tests isinstance(String, int) and applies exactly "%04X" % String ; Glyphs2 uses an exact-int test. Glyphs4 uses isinstance and f-string 04X formatting, including subclass __format__ . Four is a minimum width and does not validate scalar range. The example selects the real Glyphs3 profile to retain its percent-formatting assertions. The new guide also exercises Glyphs2 and Glyphs4. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class OwnedInt ( int ): def __int__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not coerce an integer subclass" ) def __format__ ( self , specification ): raise AssertionError ( "Preserve percent formatting" ) app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = None )) for value , spelling in [( 65 , "0041" ), ( OwnedInt ( 65 ), "0041" ), ( True , "0001" ), ( False , "0000" ), ( - 1 , "-001" )]: actual = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) expected = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( spelling ) assert ( actual . name , actual . unicode ) == ( expected . name , expected . unicode ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( OwnedInt ( 65 )) . name == "A" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( - 1 ) . name == "uni-001" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( 0x10FFFF ) is None
title: Preserve integer formatting

text: Glyphs2/3 integer Name dispatch calls the instance Unicode method without a font keyword. Glyphs4 passes font=font , including None, through the instance method. An explicit-font string Name query selects that font's manager in all three profiles. The former unconditional .localData refusal is superseded; a selected manager's actual result/error now propagates. The explicit Glyphs3 example below retains its integer/override contract while checking real string-name font delegation and its access-error propagation. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class UnreadableFont : def __getattribute__ ( self , name ): raise AssertionError ( "Global lookup must not read the active font" ) active = UnreadableFont () app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = active )) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( 65 , font = active ) . name == "A" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" , font = None ) . name == "A" local = owned_parsed_manager () explicit = SimpleNamespace ( glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = explicit ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "A" ) try : app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = active ) except AssertionError as error : assert str ( error ) == "Global lookup must not read the active font" else : raise AssertionError ( "Explicit font access errors must propagate" ) calls = [] class OwnedApplication ( type ( app )): def glyphInfoForUnicode ( self , * args , ** kwargs ): calls . append (( args , kwargs )) return "owned override" owned = OwnedApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = active ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert owned . glyphInfoForName ( True , font = active ) == "owned override" assert calls == [(( True ,), {})] Both global routes ignore active-font glyph state, parameters, ROS and stored overrides. They do not invoke the per-glyph metadata postprocessing pipeline. A result of None does not trigger a search of font.glyphs .
title: Glyphs2/3 integer name lookup discards the font first

text: Integer formatting occurs before selecting an explicit font manager. Only None selects shared; a false-valued font still receives glyphsInfo() . There is no unconditional .localData refusal. A malformed object used as a font can fail at its own method access. With the default manager, built-in strings and None remain supported after profile-specific integer dispatch; unqualified bridge payload types retain .inputType refusal. The example exercises conversion and selected-manager identity before default manager payload checks; it does not manufacture a blanket local-data refusal. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class NoCoercion : def __str__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not stringify bridge inputs" ) def __index__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not coerce bridge inputs to integers" ) class OwnedString ( str ): pass app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) class Recorder : def glyphInfoForUnicode_ ( self , value ): return value class ExplicitFont : def glyphsInfo ( self ): return Recorder () def __bool__ ( self ): return False for value in ( None , [], 65 , True , "" , " \ud800 00" ): actual = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value , font = ExplicitFont ()) if isinstance ( value , int ): assert actual == f " { value : 04X } " else : assert actual is value try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" , font = False ) except AttributeError as error : assert "glyphsInfo" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "False is an explicit font object, not omitted font" ) for value in ( 65.0 , b "0041" , [], NoCoercion (), OwnedString ( "0041" )): try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.inputType" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unqualified bridge inputs must refuse" )
title: Respect refusal precedence

text: After the original-length gate, the uppercase text is the exact Unicode-index key. There is no trimming, zero padding, prefix removal or numeric canonicalization. Thus 004a selects J , while 041 and 000041 miss 0041 and synthesize their own raw names. Each source record contributes its primary encodings, then its non-nil legacy encoding to the same index, in record/file order; the last assignment wins. The parser/loader contract and retained ARM instructions establish this ordering, rather than a new native run. The pinned public glyphsLib 6.16.2 GlyphData snapshot has 74,247 records and 71,401 primary keys. Its 730 distinct legacy keys produce 72,131 combined keys, with no overlap or change to existing primary entries in this snapshot. The duplicated legacy key 0000 belongs first to .null , then to NULL ; lookup selects NULL . FE8D selects alef-ar.isol , and FE80 selects hamza-ar.isol . Their primary Unicode remains None ; a legacy hit never promotes its key into that field. These public counts do not establish proprietary database completeness or the same record set in every resource/version. Synthesis applies only after a true combined-index miss. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "004a" ) . name == "J" for text , name in [( "041" , "uni041" ), ( "000041" , "uni000041" )]: info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , text , None ) for text , name , primary , legacy in [ ( "FE8D" , "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ), ( "FE80" , "hamza-ar.isol" , None , "FE80" ), ( "0000" , "NULL" , None , "0000" ), ]: info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) named = app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) assert ( named . name , named . unicode , named . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) assert info is named # Canonical views of the same selected raw record. assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "fe8d" ) . name == "alef-ar.isol" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "U+0041" ) is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0x41" ) is None
title: Exact combined-index lookup precedes raw synthesis

text: None and text shorter than three UTF-16 code units return None before uppercasing, lookup or parsing. Count UTF-16 units rather than Python code points: a supplementary scalar occupies two. An uppercase expansion cannot rescue a too-short input. 0ﬀ returns None; 00ﬀ becomes 00FF and selects ydieresis ; 000ﬀ becomes 000FF and synthesizes. Actual malformed UTF16 and hex text naming a surrogate are different domains. After the minimum-length gate, malformed actual UTF16 refuses with .UTF16 : Foundation can return a NULL UTF8 pointer that the retained upstream helper would dereference unchecked. Do not execute that native failure path. A shorter lone surrogate returns None at the earlier length gate; valid surrogate pairs are not rejected as malformed. Literal ASCII D800 is accepted synthesis text. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for value in ( None , "" , "0" , "00" , "0ﬀ" , " \ud800 " , " \ud800 0" , "😀0" , " \ud83d\ude00 0" ): assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "00ﬀ" ) . name == "ydieresis" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "000ﬀ" ) . name == "uni000FF" for value in ( " \ud800 00" , "00 \ud800 " , " \udc00 00" ): try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.UTF16" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unsafe malformed UTF16 must refuse" ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "D800" ) . unicode == "D800" Standalone macOS 27.2 Foundation calibration checked all 1,112,064 valid Unicode scalars against Python 3.11 Unicode 14 uppercasing. There were 55 differences; only non-ASCII ﬀ uppercased entirely into the parser alphabet, identically in both systems. That establishes this measured parser-alphabet boundary. It does not establish arbitrary Foundation-version equivalence, PyObjC conversion or native font-workflow compatibility.
title: Check original UTF16 length before uppercase expansion

text: On a combined-index miss, the retained helper scans ASCII hex in reverse. Spaces contribute nothing; any minus sign requests final negation, regardless of its position, and repeated minuses do not toggle the sign. Both are skipped without advancing the nibble position. Other characters return sentinel 0x7FFFFFFF , which fails the manager’s range check. Nonempty spaces/minuses alone parse as zero. Nibble contributions are added modulo 2³² with shifts (4 * position) & 31 . This differs from parsing an unlimited integer and truncating it: 100000000 parses as 1 and FFFFFFFFF as 14. Signed values below 0x10000 use the uni prefix; other accepted values use u . Signed high-bit patterns take the BMP branch and bypass its upper-range guard. On the other branch, 10FFFE passes but 10FFFF fails. This is not a strict Unicode scalar validator. Names use that prefix plus the uppercase original text , not a reformatted parsed integer. The synthesized primary encoding preserves the same text only when its uppercase UTF16 length is 1–7. A longer valid record has unicode=None . No encoding is assigned to a font by reading one of these snapshots. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for text in ( "--41" , "04-1" , " 4 1 " , " " , "---" ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert info . name == "uni" + text and info . unicode == text for text in ( "00000041" , "80000000" , "FFFFFFFF" , "100000000" , "FFFFFFFFF" ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert info . name == "uni" + text and info . unicode is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "10FFFE" ) . name == "u10FFFE" for text in ( "10FFFF" , "110000" , "7FFFFFFF" , "nothex" ): assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) is None
title: Preserve the historical parser and raw encoding

text: Synthesized case is 0; subCategory and unicodeLegacy are None. Private Use gets category Private Use and no script in exactly E000–F8FF, F0000–FFFFD and 100000–10FFFD. Otherwise the audited historical Han set gives script han and category Letter ; other synthesized records have script None and category Other . Surrogate hex text, unassigned points, controls, punctuation and noncharacters are not generally filtered out. Direct indexed entries retain their maintained metadata and can mask these synthesis rules. The Han intervals are the following hexadecimal start/count pairs; each covers [start, start + count) . They describe retained source, not current Unicode Script data: Start Count Start Count 2E80 1A 2E9B 59 2F00 D6 3005 1 3007 1 3021 9 3038 3 303B 1 3400 19B6 4E00 51CD F900 16E FA70 6A 2F800 21E 20000 A6D7 2A700 1035 2B740 DE 2B820 1682 2CEB0 1D31 30000 134B 1F200 100 The seven-digit spellings below force a combined-index miss so the historical classification can be observed independently of canonical maintained entries. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for value , script , category in [( 0x9FCC , "han" , "Letter" ), ( 0x9FCD , None , "Other" ), ( 0x3134A , "han" , "Letter" ), ( 0x3134B , None , "Other" ), ( 0xF8FF , None , "Private Use" )]: text = " %07X " % value info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . script , info . category ) == ( script , category ) assert info . unicode == text and info . case == 0 assert info . subCategory is None and info . unicodeLegacy is None for value in ( 0xE000 , 0xF0000 , 0xFFFFD , 0x100000 , 0x10FFFD ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) assert info . category == "Private Use" and info . script is None
