text: Use the reviewed wheel or source distribution from each package's GitHub release. Private repositories require authenticated access. Keep credentials in your normal GitHub tooling; never put them in documentation, URLs or Python scripts. Install outside FontLab with uv pip install PATH_TO_WHEEL . For embedded use, install into a Python directory on FontLab's interpreter path using a compatible Python version. FontLab supplies its native bindings and existing Qt application. The captured API uses FontLab9, Python3.11 and Qt5. The source-only documentation environment uses Python3.12 or newer. A PySide2 binary wheel is a reference input; it is not loaded into FontLab's PythonQt runtime. Enable FontLab's MCP server, then connect: from fontlab_remopy import FontLab with FontLab () as app : print ( app . fonts ()) print ( app . output ()) eval() returns a JSON-native value. run() captures stdout/stderr and a result; bind variables as keyword arguments rather than interpolating them into code. The native execution deadline still applies. A timeout can leave an operation's outcome unknown, so mutating calls are never retried automatically. with FontLab () as app : answer = app . eval ( "value + 2" , value = 40 ) execution = app . run ( "print(message) \n result = 42" , message = "Hello, FontLab" ) For asynchronous programs, use AsyncFontLab with async with and await calls.
title: Install and connect

text: FontLab 9 lets Python draw on the Glyph canvas and register its own tools. Both hooks live on the host objects, so you need no helper package to use them. Plugmix and Glyport wrap them with friendlier APIs. Host build These methods exist only in FontLab 9 builds that include the Python scripting hooks. Check hasattr(flCanvas, "appendPythonPainter") before relying on them. Everything here runs on the GUI thread. Calling a registration function from another thread raises RuntimeError .
title: Native Python hooks in FontLab 9

text: from fontlab import flWorkspace canvas = flWorkspace . instance () . getActiveCanvas () # a flCanvas, or nothing getActiveCanvas() returns the canvas of the active window, or nothing when no canvas is active.
title: Get the canvas

text: from fontlab import flCanvas from PythonQt import QtCore , QtGui def paint ( painter , canvas ): painter . setPen ( QtGui . QColor ( "#d03030" )) centre = canvas . mapToViewportF ( QtCore . QPointF ( 0 , 0 )) painter . drawEllipse ( centre , 8 , 8 ) token = canvas . appendPythonPainter ( paint , flCanvas . OverOwner ) # later canvas . removePythonPainter ( token ) appendPythonPainter(callback, order=UnderOwner) returns an integer token. removePythonPainter(token) returns True when it removed the painter and False when the token is unknown or belongs to another canvas. Callback signature. callback(painter, canvas) . The painter is a QPainter ; the canvas is the flCanvas being painted. Order. flCanvas.UnderOwner ( 0 ) paints before the item that owns the canvas (the glyph); flCanvas.OverOwner ( 1 ) paints after it. Any other value raises ValueError . The default is UnderOwner . Coordinates. FontLab resets the painter's transform before each call, so you draw in viewport pixels, with the origin at the viewport's top-left corner. To place something at a canvas position, convert it first: mapToViewportF takes a QPointF and returns a QPointF , or takes a QLineF and returns a QLineF . mapToViewport is the integer form for QPoint , QRectF and QPolygonF . Pen widths and text sizes stay in pixels, so they do not scale with zoom. Painter lifetime. The painter is valid only during the callback. Do not store it, and do not use it after the callback returns. FontLab saves the painter state before calling you and restores it afterwards. Errors. An exception in your callback is printed to the Python console and does not stop the paint. Other painters still run. Scope and cleanup. A painter belongs to one canvas, and FontLab discards it when that canvas is destroyed. Painting does not nest: a callback that provokes another paint pass during painting is skipped for that pass. Adding or removing a painter asks the canvas to repaint.
title: Draw with a canvas painter

text: from fontlab import flWorkspace class Probe : def activate ( self ): print ( "probe on" ) def deactivate ( self ): print ( "probe off" ) def mousePressed ( self , event , canvas ): print ( event . pos ()) return True # handled def paint ( self , painter , canvas ): painter . drawText ( 10 , 20 , "Probe" ) workspace = flWorkspace . instance () token = workspace . registerPythonTool ( "Probe" , None , Probe ()) # later workspace . unregisterPythonTool ( token ) registerPythonTool(name, icon, object) returns an integer token. name must not be empty. icon is a QIcon or None . object is any Python object; FontLab looks up each method by name when the event happens, so implement only what you need. The tool appears as a checkable action in the Tools list and in the toolbar. unregisterPythonTool(token) removes those entries, deactivates the tool if it is active, and returns True on success. Method Arguments Called when activate , deactivate none The tool becomes, or stops being, the main tool. mousePressed , mouseMoved , mouseReleased , mouseDoubleClicked (event, canvas) A mouse event reaches a canvas of the tool's workspace. keyPressed , keyReleased (event, canvas) A key event reaches such a canvas. paint (painter, canvas) The canvas paints over the owner. Same rules as a canvas painter. Events. Mouse methods receive a QMouseEvent , key methods a QKeyEvent . Both are valid only during the call. Return a true value to mark the event as handled; FontLab then accepts it and stops normal processing. Return nothing to let FontLab continue. FontLab offers a key press to keyPressed before it resolves shortcuts, so a handled key beats a shortcut, and it reuses your answer for the key press that follows. Active tool only. Event methods and paint run only while your tool is the active tool. paint always runs over the owner. Cleanup. FontLab unregisters a workspace's tools when that workspace closes. A callback may safely unregister its own tool.
title: Register a tool

text: Need Hook An overlay that is always on, in every tool Canvas painter An overlay or interaction that belongs to one tool Tool paint and mouse methods A menu or toolbar entry that takes over the canvas Tool For ready-made reporters, filters and tools see Plugmix ; Glyport uses the same hooks for Glyphs reporters and tools. Fontlabapp's glyph_window.draw overlay is a separate mechanism, not a wrapper for these hooks; see Fontlabapp .
title: Choosing between the hooks

text: Inside FontLab, echopy.fontlab delegates to the original fontlab objects; echopy.fontgate and echopy.fontpr follow the same contract. from echopy import fontlab as fl font = fl . CurrentFont () glyph = fl . CurrentGlyph () node = fl . flNode ( 120 , 340 ) Use flNode and the complete class member indexes to inspect captured signatures and enriched documentation. Any and variadic arguments mark incomplete native signature information. They are not permission to pass arbitrary objects; confirm an uncertain operation against the running host. The optional fontlabpr module was absent from the captured host. Its absence is recorded rather than represented by invented APIs.
title: Native scripting

text: Fly provides nine lazy module aliases: Alias Target fly.fl echopy.fontlab fly.fg echopy.fontgate fly.tr typerig fly.pr echopy.fontpr fly.qt native PythonQt fly.ap fontlabapp fly.qs pythonqtside fly.gp fontlab_glyport fly.fp fontlab_fontport They share the canonical module objects. Documentation names use the live API's natural namespaces, while source and enrichment hashes retain provenance. Outside FontLab, native construction and operations fail with NativeUnavailable . Documentation builds read source and stubs without invoking these operations.
title: Short imports

text: These examples use the ordinary development App package 0.2.26.dev159+gb1e905b61 . Older versions can clear and rebuild the selection even with add=True . The examples below were checked against the installed artifact with owned native doubles; their FontLab behavior remains unqualified.
title: Read and extend the Font-window selection

text: Keep the two native identifiers separate. package.id binds App operations to a package; package.fgId identifies the FontGate carrier used by the legacy selection reader. The reader returns selected glyph names in font order. It is not a list of every displayed glyph, nor a record of selected chart cells: one glyph can occur in several cells. Defining this function does not access FontLab. Calling it reads selection and returns the package identifier with the names. A two-second deadline bounds the Python scan, but cannot interrupt a blocking native call. The final identity check rejects a font switch; it does not prove an atomic snapshot if native state changes and changes back during the scan. from time import monotonic from fontlabapp.core.scripting import current_package , names_font_window_selection def read_font_selection (): package = current_package () if package is None : raise ValueError ( "Open a font before reading its selection." ) package_id = int ( package . id ) names = names_font_window_selection ( expected_fg_id = int ( package . fgId ), deadline = monotonic () + 2.0 ) if current_package ( package_id ) is None : raise ValueError ( "The font changed during the selection read; run again." ) return package_id , names An empty selection is a valid empty list. This function does not fall back to the current Glyph-window glyph. Keep the returned package identifier with any report based on these names, so a later action cannot silently target another font.
title: Read names bound to one font

text: Pass the bound package identifier and the glyph names your report found to this function. Calling it changes the Font-window selection; it does not edit glyph outlines. Activate the regular Font window first. Readable selection data from a Glyph window does not make the legacy selection writers safe there. from fontlabapp.core.scripting import select_glyphs def add_report_names ( package_id , names ): selected = select_glyphs ( names , package_id = package_id , add = True ) print ( f "Selected { len ( selected ) } glyph names in total." ) return selected The helper validates every requested name before writing and rejects a stale package or unsupported active window. It adds only names that are not already selected, preserving the existing selection. Duplicate names do not cause repeated writes. Empty requests and already-selected names require no selection writes, but still undergo the package/window checks. The returned count is the total number of selected glyph names, not the number just added or the number of selected chart cells. An already-selected glyph's partial cell selection is left untouched. If a native addition fails, the exception propagates. Earlier additions can remain; this is not atomic rollback. Do not automatically retry, clear selection or apply a global Undo in an error handler. add=False is a different operation: it clears selection before selecting the requested names and does not have the same preservation behavior. Neither route calls UpdateAll() .
title: Add report results without clearing selection

text: Neither helper supplies the Font window's arranged, filtered cell list. A scan of all package glyphs or MCP list_glyphs with request filters is not equivalent to the current UI filter. The inspected C++ chart model has cell data, but its ordinary accessors are absent from the retained PythonQt capture. That bounded finding does not prove that every route is unavailable on every build. Before adapting a tool that operates on displayed cells, verify an exposed ordered snapshot with package-qualified glyph identities, duplicates and empty encoding cells. Define whether “visible” means included by the chart filter or inside the viewport. Test reads and writes on owned fonts, including font switches, filtered views and multiple cells for one glyph; source examples alone do not establish complete font, history or view-state preservation.
title: A displayed filter is a separate scope

text: A successful Python call does not prove that FontLab preserved every unrelated part of a font. Keep the returned counters and warnings, and qualify edits with Apply, Undo, Redo and saved-file reopen on owned copies before relying on a writer. Do not convert an exception into a success message or automatically repeat a failed edit: a partial write can already have changed the font. The examples below use the development App contract verified in ordinary package 0.2.26.dev158+g55fc09868 . This is a source/artifact checkpoint, not a published release or native acceptance claim. Older installed App versions may still refuse queued updates and may not accept the disclosure keyword.
title: Handle writer results and failures

text: FontLab can retain glyph IDs in its process-wide update queue after opening an editor or refreshing views. A later write may change those glyphs’ modification dates. Ordinary App writers disclose this as pending_updates and pending_note instead of refusing solely because the queue is nonempty. They do not clear the queue or restore unrelated dates to conceal the change. Field Meaning pending_updates Tuple of native glyph IDs captured before the write; these are not names or proof that those glyphs changed. pending_note Human-readable date caveat, or an empty string. undo_steps Raise Ascender’s completed changed occurrences, not a guarantee that a later Undo succeeded. nodes Raise Ascender’s counted node moves across its sequential occurrences. guides , layers Perpendicular Guides’ reported additions and affected-layer count. Use the stored note when formatting a result. Reading the native queue again can observe different state and lose the warning that applied to this action. from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note def raise_status ( result ): text = ( f "Moved { result [ 'nodes' ] } nodes across { result [ 'occurrences' ] } occurrences; " f " { result [ 'undo_steps' ] } Undo steps." ) return append_note ( text , result ) This formatter runs outside FontLab with an ordinary result dictionary. The helper appends a nonempty note once. A zero-move result is still a valid outcome: it does not mean every selected node required an edit.
title: Queued updates are a warning

text: Backend.execute() accepts an optional mutable disclosure dictionary. It resets the dictionary at entry and fills it before history, so a caller can display the queue warning even when no result is returned. A failure before queue sampling, or a no-op, leaves an empty disclosure; this does not prove that the native queue is empty. Without a dictionary, the backend prints the warning itself. This wrapper uses the formatter above. Defining it is safe outside FontLab; calling it requires FontLab and can change the current font. from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note from fontlabapp.contours.raise_ascender.native import Backend def raise_selected ( amount = "10" , * , all_layers = False ): disclosure = { "pending_updates" : (), "pending_note" : "" } try : result = Backend () . execute ( amount , all_layers , disclosure = disclosure ) except Exception as error : print ( append_note ( f "Raise Ascender failed: { error } " , disclosure )) raise print ( raise_status ( result )) return result all_layers=False uses the selected occurrences. True uses every foreground layer of the first selected glyph, including associated auxiliary layers; it is not an all-font operation. The writer retains its bound-font, source-change, automatic-dependent and history-scope checks. A queued-update warning does not waive any of those checks. On failure, the wrapper preserves the original exception and its Undo guidance. In a dialog, put the same formatted text in an owned status label instead of printing it. Keep the disclosure dictionary for that action only; do not reuse a previous action’s warning after a no-op or an early failure.
title: Preserve warnings when Raise Ascender fails

text: fontlabapp.guides.perpendicular.model.run() plans guides for the first selected layer. When the sampled queue is nonempty, it prints the warning before a possible append. On success it returns guides , layers , messages , pending_updates and pending_note . The warning is already printed; callers need not print it a second time. A no-op reports zero counts and empty disclosure without querying the queue. Source changes, automatic layers or affected automatic dependants still cause refusal. If an append partially fails, no success dictionary is returned. The warning has already been printed and the append-failure exception directs the user to inspect Edit > Undo. Notification/finalization errors can also propagate; do not infer rollback from an exception. No queue clearing, automatic retry or global Undo belongs in a caller’s error handler.
title: Perpendicular Guides uses the same warning

text: The background tools remove entire background layer objects, including their stored payload. They do not merely erase contours. Use Clear All Layer Backgrounds or Clear Master Backgrounds for a panel with a preview and an explicit Apply action. The programmatic equivalent below also separates inspection from the write. masters=False includes mapped backgrounds of all foreground layers in the current font, including auxiliary layers. masters=True restricts the plan to master foreground layers. Neither scope means selected glyphs only. A background shared by a master and an excluded auxiliary layer is refused in master-only mode; silently deleting it would change the excluded layer too. Defining these functions makes no edit. Call preview_backgrounds() in FontLab, inspect the printed glyph/background names, then explicitly pass its returned value to clear_previewed_backgrounds() . Pass masters=True to preview the master-only scope. A preview is bound to its original font and scope: the writer rechecks it before history and refuses stale facts rather than silently rescanning and applying a different plan. from fontlabapp.masters.background.clear.model import plan as background_plan from fontlabapp.masters.background.clear.native import Backend as BackgroundBackend from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note def preview_backgrounds ( * , masters = False ): backend = BackgroundBackend () source = backend . capture () if source is None : raise ValueError ( "Open a font before previewing backgrounds." ) for removal in background_plan ( source , masters ): print ( f " { removal . glyph } : { removal . mask_name } " ) return backend , source , masters def clear_previewed_backgrounds ( preview ): backend , source , masters = preview disclosure = { "pending_updates" : (), "pending_note" : "" } try : result = backend . apply ( source , masters , disclosure = disclosure ) except BaseException as error : # Report the action's warning, then propagate interruptions unchanged. print ( append_note ( f "Background clearing failed: { error } " , disclosure )) raise print ( append_note ( f "Removed { result [ 'backgrounds' ] } backgrounds from " f " { result [ 'layers' ] } foreground layers in { result [ 'glyphs' ] } glyphs." , result , )) return result backgrounds counts confirmed object removals; layers counts the affected foreground layers, which can differ when backgrounds are shared. glyphs counts owner glyphs. A no-op returns zero counts and empty disclosure without sampling the native queue. A nonempty warning is reported once by this wrapper; the supplied dictionary prevents the backend from printing it separately. Active or locked backgrounds, invalid ownership/mapping, affected automatic layers or automatic dependants, and unsupported history scope can still cause refusal. Queue disclosure does not waive these guards. A refused domain remains an incomplete compatibility boundary, not proof of equivalent original behavior. A failure after an attempted removal may leave changes in the font. Ordinary partial-write errors report attempted and confirmed removal counts and direct the user to Undo. Interruptions stop further removals, attempt remaining date updates and notification, then propagate the original interruption with recovery notes. The wrapper preserves those notes by re-raising the same exception. Neither cleanup nor an exception proves rollback, successful Undo, or that native cleanup finished within a deadline. Do not automatically retry the operation.
title: Preview complete background removal

text: The Raise Ascender formatter and caller are checked against the ordinary App artifact. Formatting uses the actual shared helper; wrapper success/no-op/failure tests substitute the native backend. Those tests prove message composition, disclosure forwarding and exception propagation. They do not prove FontLab editing, native window behavior, whole-font preservation or successful Undo/Redo. The writer’s artifact tests and its dedicated native qualification are separate requirements. The background example is also executed verbatim against the installed App backend and planner. Owned native doubles cover master/auxiliary scope, stale previews, no-op, partial removal and interruption. The backend itself is not replaced. These checks still do not exercise FontLab's compiled object model, native history, saved files, rendered documentation or publication.
title: Verification boundary
Choose the original node-duplication scope explicitly

text: Scriptmix now exposes three distinct Node Duplicator actions. They use App's guarded node_duplicator_native.duplicate_selected_nodes entry point, introduced in the matching 0.2.26.dev333 artifact. Older rescued adapters lack that name. Keep the separate Node Duplicator panel for its per-glyph reference selection, preview and declared-master controls. Menu action in Contours Source policy Duplicate Nodes All Foreground Layers Broadcast the first selected layer's on-curve indices to every stored foreground layer of each selected parent occurrence. Duplicate Nodes Current Layer Copy selected on-curves in the first selected layer only. Duplicate Nodes with Two Handles First selected layer only; insert two coincident controls and a copied curve endpoint per selected on-curve. The two-handle source's filename says “all masters”, but its body has no all-master loop. The actions preserve that distinction. All-layer mode retains auxiliary-layer identities and repeated parents; two layers with the same name remain separate targets. Missing target path/node indices are reported. These are immediate actions. Select nodes, activate the appropriate Font or Glyph window, and run the chosen menu entry. A broadcast that includes owners outside the active Glyph canvas is refused before staging; activate the Font window for that edit. Queued glyph ids are disclosed without clearing them. Automatic dependants, shared owners, hinted topology and unsupported generated or control mappings have explicit refusals. The following experiments execute the actual immutable App planning engine. They use invented node/layer identities and metadata, with no FontLab, Qt, framework, font, preference or document access. They do not establish native selection projection, copy fidelity, history or saved-font acceptance.
title: Choose the original node-duplication scope explicitly

text: Execute this setup afresh before each tagged experiment. Layers10/11 share one parent;20/21 share another. The occurrence list selects the first parent twice. Only node1 in the first selected layer supplies the reference selection. The native adapter keeps display names separately from these stable identities. from dataclasses import replace from fontlabapp.node_duplicator import Node , Path , Layer , Source , plan def owned_source (): def node ( key ): return Node ( key , key + 0.125 , key + 0.375 , "line" , 8 , f "node- { key } " , (( "corner_smooth" , 0.375 ),)) layers = tuple ( Layer ( key , glyph , ( Path ( key * 10 , ( node ( a ), node ( a + 1 )), False ),)) for key , glyph , a in [( 10 , 1 , 1 ), ( 11 , 1 , 3 ), ( 20 , 2 , 5 ), ( 21 , 2 , 7 )] ) return Source ( layers , ( 10 , 11 , 20 ), (( 0 , 1 ),), True )
title: Prepare an owned source graph

text: Both foreground layers of the first parent receive two insertions. Both layers of the second receive one, even though they have no independent selected node. The source graph remains unchanged. History enrollment can deduplicate owners; the operation program must retain repeated occurrences. source = owned_source () result = plan ( source , "all" ) assert result . inserted == 6 assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in result . layers ] == [ 4 , 4 , 3 , 3 ] assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in source . layers ] == [ 2 , 2 , 2 , 2 ] assert [ operation . layer for operation in result . operations ] == [ 10 , 11 , 10 , 11 , 20 , 21 ] assert result . skipped == ()
title: Replay each selected parent occurrence

text: Current mode inserts one line copy. Handles mode inserts two fresh controls and a curve endpoint copied from the target. The copied endpoint keeps its name, coordinates and properties; the new controls do not pretend to be copies. Only the first selected layer changes in either mode. source = owned_source () current , handles = plan ( source , "current" ), plan ( source , "handles" ) assert current . inserted == 1 and handles . inserted == 3 assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in current . layers ] == [ 3 , 2 , 2 , 2 ] nodes = handles . layers [ 0 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes assert [ node . kind for node in nodes ] == [ "line" , "off" , "off" , "curve" , "line" ] original , copied = source . layers [ 0 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes [ 0 ], nodes [ 3 ] assert ( copied . x , copied . y , copied . name , copied . properties ) == ( original . x , original . y , original . name , original . properties ) assert nodes [ 1 ] . name == nodes [ 2 ] . name == "" assert nodes [ 1 ] . properties == nodes [ 2 ] . properties == () assert handles . layers [ 1 :] == source . layers [ 1 :]
title: Keep current-layer and handle semantics distinct

text: The original all-layer policy uses fixed reference indices. It does not require every target to have identical topology. Here one target has no path and another has too few nodes. Both skips retain their target identities and exact indices; the native result window supplies captured glyph/layer names alongside them. source = owned_source () layers = list ( source . layers ) layers [ 2 ] = replace ( layers [ 2 ], paths = ()) short = replace ( layers [ 3 ] . paths [ 0 ], nodes = layers [ 3 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes [: 1 ]) layers [ 3 ] = replace ( layers [ 3 ], paths = ( short ,)) source = replace ( source , layers = tuple ( layers ), selection = (( 0 , 2 ),)) result = plan ( source , "all" ) assert result . inserted == 4 assert result . skipped == (( 2 , 20 , 0 , 1 ), ( 2 , 21 , 0 , 1 ))
title: Report unavailable target indices

text: A visual selection can contain objects other than editable on-curves. All mode asks for nodes when none are selected. Current mode uses the original truth of the entire selection; handle mode has no corresponding message branch. All three produce no insertions in this owned example. source = replace ( owned_source (), selection = (), any_selection = True ) all_layers = plan ( source , "all" ) current = plan ( source , "current" ) handles = plan ( source , "handles" ) assert all_layers . inserted == current . inserted == handles . inserted == 0 assert all_layers . no_selection_message is True assert current . no_selection_message is False assert handles . no_selection_message is False
title: Preserve the original empty-selection message rules

text: The native boundary captures and rechecks context before history, stages detached copies and uses current history-scope guards. It checks copied metadata and exact old-node state, and reports failed writes. Cleanup removes only exact owned new identities while its deadline permits; it stops further mutations after expiry. WriteError.pending_nodes retains owned contour/node handles for inspection. history_finalized records whether the notification returned successfully; it does not prove actual Undo/Redo or complete restoration. Inspect the affected font and history before retrying. Do not clear native update queues, normalize unrelated dates or discard a failed receipt to obtain a green result. The result window uses the shared parent/priority/lifecycle helper. Owned Qt tests cover parenting, the topmost flag, Close and reopen. Actual macOS FontLab stacking and lifetime, four-font full preservation, Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen, compiled binding behavior and release/promotion remain separate requirements. These behavior-only rewrites credit Fernando Díaz and Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts , whose retained README declares Apache-2.0. Original source identities stay separate in Scriptmix's provenance/backlog; no original body is redistributed here.
title: Handle a partial failure without a blind retry
Keep tool windows usable and recoverable

text: Keep the returned owner until its window has closed successfully. A failed Close must leave a reachable window and its exact signal records available for retry. This guide describes the dialog-ownership App candidate; it is not a released minimum version or evidence of native FontLab stacking.
title: Keep tool windows usable and recoverable

text: Use FontLab's existing application and PythonQt. This example belongs inside FontLab; do not install PySide6 there or start another application event loop. from fly import fl , qt import fly.ap.widgets as widgets def build ( content ): layout = qt . QtGui . QVBoxLayout ( content ) layout . addWidget ( qt . QtGui . QLabel ( "Inspect the current font here." , content )) owned_panel = widgets . create_panel ( fl . MainWindow (), "Inspection" , build , "right" ) # Keep owned_panel. When finished, retain it if close returns False or raises. accepted = owned_panel . close () The Unicode Issues Dock uses this same factory. A hidden MainWindow produces a floating dock. Later undocking also requests the TypeRig-style priority hint; the dock keeps its parent, area, content and native window type. Common Glyphs applies priority inside its existing bounded display/recovery path. Plugin panels and filter dialogs request priority through OwnedMenus.tool_window ; their shell is disposable, while the supplied plugin content remains caller-owned. The generic script launcher retains an exact candidate when flags, show or raise fails. A later launch closes that candidate before constructing its replacement. It also preserves an old owner whose Close refuses or raises. Some panels have a stronger, dedicated failed-owner fence; preserve that panel's recovery protocol.
title: Open a dock inside FontLab

text: The following setup is for a separate Python 3.11 process with App's test extra. It uses actual Qt widgets and the actual App helpers over an injected binding namespace. It never contacts FontLab, reads a font or proves macOS host stacking. Run the setup afresh for each experiment; retain the QApplication for the process. import os import sys assert not { "fontlab" , "FL" , "PythonQt" } . intersection ( sys . modules ) os . environ . setdefault ( "QT_QPA_PLATFORM" , "offscreen" ) from contextlib import contextmanager from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest.mock import patch from PySide6 import QtCore , QtWidgets from shiboken6 import isValid import fontlabapp.widgets as widgets APP = QtWidgets . QApplication . instance () or QtWidgets . QApplication ([]) BINDING = SimpleNamespace ( QtGui = QtWidgets , QtCore = QtCore ) def drain (): APP . processEvents () QtCore . QCoreApplication . sendPostedEvents ( None , QtCore . QEvent . DeferredDelete ) APP . processEvents () @contextmanager def sandbox ( binding = BINDING , parent_type = QtWidgets . QMainWindow ): parent = parent_type () try : with patch . object ( widgets , "_native" , lambda name : binding ): yield parent finally : if isValid ( parent ): parent . deleteLater () drain ()

Qt . WindowStaysOnTopHint assert parent . dockWidgetArea ( dock ) == QtCore . Qt . RightDockWidgetArea assert owned . close () is True drain () assert owned . closed and not isValid ( dock )

Qt . WindowStaysOnTopHint dock . setFloating ( False ) assert not dock . isFloating () and dock . widget () is owned . content assert owned . close ()

text: class Draft ( QtWidgets . QDialog ): allow_close = False def closeEvent ( self , event ): event . accept () if self . allow_close else event . ignore () with sandbox () as parent : dialog = Draft ( parent ) owned = widgets . OwnedWidget ( dialog , dialog ) dialog . show () assert owned . close () is False assert not owned . closed and owned . widget is dialog and dialog . isVisible () dialog . allow_close = True assert owned . close () is True drain () assert owned . closed and not isValid ( dialog )

QMainWindow . removeDockWidget ( self , dock ) with sandbox ( parent_type = Host ) as parent : owned = widgets . create_panel ( parent , "Report" , None , "right" ) dock = owned . widget try : owned . close () except RuntimeError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned removal failed" else : raise AssertionError ( "The removal failure was hidden" ) assert owned . widget is dock and not owned . closed and isValid ( dock ) parent . fail_removal = False assert owned . close () drain () assert not isValid ( dock )
title: Unregistration failure retains the unfinished stage

text: class Refusing ( QtWidgets . QDialog ): allow_close = False def closeEvent ( self , event ): event . accept () if self . allow_close else event . ignore () binding = SimpleNamespace ( QtGui = SimpleNamespace ( QDialog = Refusing ), QtCore = QtCore ) with sandbox ( binding ) as parent : original = ValueError ( "report setup failed" ) def fail ( content ): raise original try : widgets . create_dialog ( parent , "Report" , fail ) except ExceptionGroup as failure : assert failure . exceptions [ 0 ] is original recovery = failure . owner assert not recovery . closed and isinstance ( recovery . widget , Refusing ) recovery . widget . allow_close = True assert recovery . close () else : raise AssertionError ( "Refused cleanup lost its recovery owner" )

text: class Refusing ( QtWidgets . QDialog ): def closeEvent ( self , event ): event . ignore () with sandbox () as parent : dialog = Refusing ( parent ) owned = widgets . OwnedWidget ( dialog , dialog ) assert owned . close () is False parent . deleteLater () drain () assert not isValid ( dialog ) and owned . closed assert owned . widget is None and owned . content is None assert owned . close () is True Real FontLab acceptance still needs the installed candidate, observed host build, Font/Glyph-window switching, foreground/background applications, Close/reopen, parent destruction and all four named fonts' complete preservation/history tests. Qt flags, a passing standalone experiment and source coverage do not establish those results. Generated API reference, source-lock and publication remain held.
title: Parent destruction clears references without another Close

text: FontLab supplies PythonQt and an existing Qt5 application. Pythonqtside provides the QtCore/QtGui/QtWidgets namespace routing used by fly.qs . from pythonqtside import QtCore , QtWidgets The PySide2 reference package does not support the captured Python3.11 host. The expanded adapter will translate ordinary PySide2 app imports and binding behavior onto PythonQt, including property getters, constructors, signals, ownership, forms, models/views, painting, timers and processes. pythonqtside.run_app(path, *, parent=None) runs a PySide2 source file and its supported local imports inside FontLab's existing Qt application. It returns an AppHandle , retains execution globals, routes supported imports without replacing the host's import state, and tracks constructor-created Qt objects and connections for cleanup. An optional parent must be a native QWidget. Call it on the host thread. Run this from FontLab's scripting surface with your application's source path: from pythonqtside import run_app app_handle = run_app ( "/path/to/my_app.py" ) # Inspect app_handle.reports and app_handle.identity_report for routing details. # Keep the handle while the window is in use; close it when finished. app_handle . close () close() disconnects tracked connections, stops owned work and schedules owned object cleanup; repeated calls are safe. Inspect cleanup_errors for cleanup failures. Objects returned by arbitrary APIs are borrowed, not automatically owned. Dynamic exec/eval source, importlib imports, namespace packages and application subclasses/settings are unsupported. Namespace routing and this implemented runner do not establish full unchanged-app compatibility. Full acceptance still requires real native windows, callbacks, responsiveness, cleanup and owned-font editing/undo/save/reopen across the required application corpus. Reuse FontLab's application and event loop. Do not load a second Qt runtime or start a nested standalone application loop in the host.
