Local documentation builds and browser checks do not establish site publication.
title: Newly documented workflows

text: Fontlabapp provides direct native panel/window discovery, Output text, Preview and Glyph-window drawing, and owned custom widgets. Grablab exports actual widgets to bitmaps and SVG. from fontlabapp import FontLab with FontLab () as app : print ( app . output ()) preview = app . preview windows = app . glyph_windows () Inspect the native FontLab controller for the current API. A context closes only UI resources it owns. User-open documents and unrelated widgets remain owned by the application. PythonQt exposes several Qt properties as values, while PySide2 exposes methods: widget.width , line_edit.text , and scrollbar.maximum are examples in the captured host. Use the captured binding contract rather than blindly copying upstream PySide2 calls. Qt5/PySide2 documentation is labeled in this reference. Foreground overlays are useful for drawing over a view. Before/after-native-layer reporter painting also requires actual native paint ordering, per-glyph item transforms, clipping and callback-scoped painter lifetime. That expanded Glyport integration is pending; a child overlay alone does not prove background painting.
title: Panels and drawing

text: A modeless dialog returns control immediately. Retain it, connect only callbacks you own, and disconnect those callbacks before deleting the widget. Closing a window, pressing Escape, and replacing a previously opened tool must all reach the same cleanup path. A parent alone does not prove signal cleanup. The App's script-dialog helpers provide this ownership pattern. The completion owner routes finished through Close, including Escape/reject. Retain it under _completion_lifetime : close_script_dialog uses that attribute when it stops terminal callbacks. Do not add a second reject() override that calls close() . from PythonQt import QtGui import fontlabapp.core.completion as script_completion import fontlabapp.core.scripting as scripting class ExampleDialog ( QtGui . QDialog ): KEY = "example_owned_dialog" def __init__ ( self , parent = None ): QtGui . QDialog . __init__ ( self , parent ) self . _connections = [] self . setWindowTitle ( "Owned example" ) layout = QtGui . QVBoxLayout ( self ) self . status = QtGui . QLabel ( "Close this panel or press Escape" , self ) layout . addWidget ( self . status ) button = QtGui . QPushButton ( "Close" , self ) layout . addWidget ( button ) scripting . connect_guarded ( self , button . clicked , lambda * _ : self . close ()) self . _completion_lifetime = script_completion . install ( self , self . KEY ) def closeEvent ( self , event ): scripting . close_script_dialog ( self , event , self . KEY ) panel = scripting . show_script_dialog ( ExampleDialog , ExampleDialog . KEY ) The lambda discards the Boolean signal argument before calling argumentless close() ; PythonQt does not reliably trim native slot arguments. Run this inside FontLab with a matching App installation. It creates only an owned dialog; it does not edit a font. Do not construct QApplication , start an application-wide event loop, or load PySide/PyQt binaries inside FontLab. The standalone Qt checks for this example use a substitute main-window owner; they do not prove native PythonQt behavior. show_script_dialog retains one panel per key and adds the priority hint while preserving its other flags. That is a modeless-panel policy, not proof that every file chooser or macOS native sheet needs the same flags.
title: Keep an owned dialog alive until cleanup

text: Use an explicit file when testing a tool's own settings. This example writes a single value in a temporary INI file, synchronizes it, and reopens the same file. It never changes the process-wide default format or settings paths. from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from PythonQt import QtCore with TemporaryDirectory ( prefix = "fontlab-settings-example-" ) as directory : path = str ( Path ( directory ) / "tool.ini" ) settings = QtCore . QSettings ( path , QtCore . QSettings . IniFormat ) settings . setFallbacksEnabled ( False ) settings . setValue ( "family" , 2 ) settings . sync () assert settings . status () == QtCore . QSettings . NoError reopened = QtCore . QSettings ( path , QtCore . QSettings . IniFormat ) reopened . setFallbacksEnabled ( False ) assert int ( reopened . value ( "family" )) == 2 del reopened , settings For a tool that remembers window placement, use saveGeometry() and restoreGeometry() rather than parsing coordinates yourself. Restore after all controls exist and before the first show. Missing geometry keeps the layout's defaults; a false restore result or malformed value needs a usable fallback. Save before Close cleanup, and run cleanup in finally even if persistence fails. Do not call widget methods from its destroyed callback. Qt documents screen correction and the restore result in QWidget::restoreGeometry . A settings error recorded on a panel that is about to be deleted is not the same as a message the user can see. Choose a reporting surface deliberately if the saved state is important; do not prevent cleanup merely to retain that message.
title: Keep tool settings separate from chooser settings

text: The INI example isolates only the settings objects it constructs. It does not redirect QFileDialog 's internal settings. In upstream Qt 5.15.2 , file-dialog save/restore uses QSettings(UserScope, "QtProject") . That scoped constructor selects NativeFormat explicitly, so setDefaultFormat(IniFormat) does not change it. On macOS, setPath(NativeFormat, ...) also does not redirect the native store. Cancellation and destruction can still persist chooser state. A fresh process isolates the in-memory last-visited directory but not the persistent store. These are source findings, not verification of FontLab's compiled Qt build. See QFileDialog settings and the scoped QSettings constructor . DontUseNativeDialog selects a widget chooser; it does not disable those settings reads/writes. In that source version the Cocoa helper also refuses native display when WindowStaysOnTopHint is present. Adding the flag can therefore change which chooser implementation runs. See QCocoaFileDialogHelper::show . For chooser tests, use a disposable OS account or VM whose preferences are owned by the test. Keep the exact open() behavior: on macOS, conversion to a sheet can replace flags set earlier, and rejection restores prior modality. Compare complete flags, parent, modality, selected-file callbacks and cleanup across repeated opens. A plain QDialog experiment, offscreen platform, alternate working directory, or changed default settings format does not establish QFileDialog isolation or native acceptance.
title: QFileDialog has its own persistent state

text: FontLab 9 runs Python 3.11 with its own PythonQt (Qt 5). These packages extend it. Ecosystem and package boundaries explains which package owns what. Each page below gives an overview, installation, a quick start, examples and the current limits; the API reference links lead to every documented member. Package Import Use it to Echopy echopy , fontlab_echopy Read FontLab's native API as typed, documented Python Fly fly Import FontLab-related modules under short aliases Fontlabapp fontlabapp Drive menus, panels, preferences, windows and drawing overlays Remopy fontlab_remopy Control a running FontLab from another Python process Grablab grablab Capture panels, windows, menus and canvases as PNG, SVG or PDF Pythonqtside pythonqtside Run PySide2-style Qt code on FontLab's PythonQt Glyport fontlab_glyport Run Glyphs scripts and plugins inside FontLab Fontport fontlab_fontport Use FontParts, fontTools pens and ufoLib2 with FontLab fonts TypeRig typerig Use the TypeRig glyph and outline library Aidus Code fontlab_aidus_code Chat with an AI agent that inspects and edits fonts in FontLab Scriptmix scripts Copy practical menu tools into FontLab's Scripts folder Examples scripts Learn PythonQt workflows from one hundred menu scripts Plugmix fontlab_plugmix Add reporters, filters, palettes, tools and General plugins
title: Packages

text: Download a reviewed wheel from the package's GitHub release, then install it into FontLab 9's per-user Python folder with a Python 3.11 resolver: uv pip install --python 3 .11 \ --target " $HOME /Library/Application Support/FontLab/FontLab 9/python/3.11/site-packages" \ PATH_TO_WHEEL
title: Install into FontLab

text: To work on a package, install its Git checkout in editable mode into FontLab's per-user Python environment. When that folder is the site-packages of a virtual environment (for example a link into FontLab 9/.venv ), point --python at that environment's interpreter; --link-mode=copy copies files from uv's cache instead of linking them: FL_PY = " $HOME /Library/Application Support/FontLab/FontLab 9/.venv/bin/python" uv pip install --python " $FL_PY " --link-mode = copy -e path/to/fontlab-glyport uv pip install --python " $FL_PY " --link-mode = copy -e path/to/fontlab-fontport Repeat for each checkout you develop (Echopy, Fly, Fontlabapp, Grablab, Remopy, Aidus Code, Glyport, Fontport). Source edits are live in FontLab once the package's modules are reloaded. Restart FontLab, or remove the package's modules from sys.modules , to load a new version: FontLab keeps imported modules between script runs. Packages with compiled extensions must match FontLab's architecture (arm64 on Apple silicon). Install packages that run outside FontLab (Remopy, the documentation tools, TypeRig's core) into an ordinary environment with uv pip install PATH_TO_WHEEL . Private repositories require authenticated GitHub access; keep credentials in your GitHub tooling, never in scripts or URLs.
title: Editable install from a checkout

text: Every API page is generated without running FontLab: fontlab , fontgate , fontpr and PythonQt come from Echopy's captures of the live host (242,654 captured identities, each one documented). Echopy shims only fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , fontlabpr , FL and PythonQt . The Glyphs.app emulation modules ( GlyphsApp , vanilla , AppKit , Cocoa , Foundation , objc ) live in Glyport, FontLab's menu and panel names live in Fontlabapp, and the Aidus tools belong to Aidus Code. Each is documented from its own package source. The packages above are read from their source, never imported, so code that needs FontLab still documents completely. The build fails when any package renders no members or no documentation.
title: How this reference is built

text: Aidus Code adds an AI chat dock to FontLab 9. Ask about the current glyph, inspect fonts and metrics, change spacing, or have the agent write and run FontLab Python. Responses stream into the dock. This is the ported package, fontlab-aidus-code , with the dock GUI in aidus_code_plugin/ui.py : AidusCodeDock , a PythonQt QDockWidget that docks left or right in FontLab 9. It has a connection status label, Reconnect and Clear buttons, a read-only transcript with a colour per role (user, assistant, tool call, tool result, error), a "Thinking..." indicator and a one-line input field. It runs in the host and uses no PySide2. Chat history is saved locally and reappears when the dock starts. The FontLab plugin runs in FontLab's Python 3.11. The AI "brain" runs in a separate Python 3.13+ process, so no AI libraries go into FontLab. The AI provider you configure receives your prompts and the tool results the agent uses. The installation walkthrough describes Aidus Code v0.2.1. The read-preservation notes below describe the private 0.2.2.dev4+gb07867092.d20261101 candidate; they do not announce a release or establish compatibility with every FontLab build.
title: Aidus Code

text: Install the host package into a dedicated folder (Python 3.11): uv pip install --python 3 .11 --target ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host PATH_TO_AIDUS_WHEEL Create the brain environment (Python 3.13+) with the brain extra and Remopy: uv venv --python 3 .13 ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/brain uv pip install --python ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/brain/bin/python \ 'PATH_TO_AIDUS_WHEEL[brain]' PATH_TO_REMOPY_WHEEL Install the Scripts-menu entries and check the setup: PYTHONPATH = ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host python3 -m fontlab_aidus_code.install install PYTHONPATH = ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host python3 -m fontlab_aidus_code.install check The installer records the files it owns. Reinstalling or uninstalling keeps your own files. An install stops before changing anything when a script it would replace was modified, is not its own or is a symlink. Configure the brain Python path and your AI provider keys as described in the package's configuration guide.
title: Install

text: In FontLab, open the Aidus Code entry in the Scripts menu. Use owned fixture fonts when trying requests that inspect or edit glyphs; the current read path has the preservation limitation below. The built-in metrics tool targets the current glyph. A request to edit every selected glyph requires additional script execution and is not evidence that the single-glyph tool supports batch edits.
title: Quick start

text: This prints package identity without opening the dock or starting the brain: # Outside FontLab from importlib.metadata import version import fontlab_aidus_code assert fontlab_aidus_code . __version__ == version ( "fontlab-aidus-code" ) print ( fontlab_aidus_code . __version__ ) print ( fontlab_aidus_code . __file__ ) For maintainer diagnostics, the plugin executor can list its built-in tool metadata without calling a font operation. This is an internal diagnostic interface, not a replacement for the native tool API: # Outside FontLab; installed plugin diagnostic only from aidus_code_plugin.executor import FontLabExecutor result = FontLabExecutor () . run ( "list_tools" ) tools = { tool [ "name" ]: tool for tool in result [ "tools" ]} assert tools [ "get_current_glyph_info" ][ "requires_glyph" ] is True assert tools [ "set_glyph_metrics" ][ "optional_params" ] == [ "width" , "lsb" , "rsb" ] assert tools [ "run_fontlab_script" ][ "required_params" ] == [ "code" ] print ( sorted ( tools )) A listed tool is not a successful native operation. Neither example contacts an AI provider, creates a font or proves native read/write safety.
title: Identify an installed candidate offline

text: The agent's FontLab tools are registered by the plugin's executor and are not a public Python import. Reach them through the agent, or through Remopy from outside FontLab. The plugin's executor reads the current glyph from the workspace record ( flWorkspace.currentGlyph , checked against the workspace's current font) instead of calling CurrentGlyph() , whose export can lose the FontGate note mirror (fl#8525). It refuses a stale or ambiguous record. Builds without a workspace glyph keep the older CurrentGlyph() route.
title: Programmatic tools

text: get_current_glyph_info returns current-glyph metadata, but its name does not guarantee a side-effect-free read. On a historically affected FontLab build, CurrentGlyph() could export glyph data and lose the fresh FontGate note mirror. The public tool still calls that preflight. A later Unicode export was a second independent route to the same loss. The private candidate removes the inner export. It resolves the registered package, checks package/font identities, requires a unique glyph name and checks the record's name and ID before reading Unicode. It refuses missing or ambiguous ownership instead of reading another glyph or restoring metadata afterwards. It does not repair the earlier CurrentGlyph() call. Fresh wheel and sdist installs each pass 18 targeted checks and retain the preflight preservation failure. The full source suite in the brain environment passes 808 tests with that same failure. These tests use owned doubles; the current native build, full font state, Undo/Redo and save/reopen remain unqualified. The native snippet above is compile-checked only. Do not use it on owner fonts to demonstrate read safety. Tested private archive SHA256 values: Archive SHA256 Wheel f9745105a1aca6a738ce62b6ecb5b041eb5d783bf14aca1d6104853476a8d0ad sdist 64a431624d767e5ada8045dc4603e405a7bc116e4bda601abddaa1e3797338e1 Version text alone does not distinguish uncommitted builds. Keep exact archive hashes with test evidence. The obsolete aidus-code source remains protected until migration and retirement requirements are satisfied.
title: Glyph-info preservation boundary

text: Use a disposable font for your first editing experiments: the agent can change and run code on the open font. Prompts and tool results go to your configured AI provider. Reference: fontlab_aidus_code . Aidus Code is proprietary (© Fontlab Ltd); only its API documentation is published here.
title: Limits

text: Echopy makes FontLab's native Python API readable by editors, type checkers and documentation tools. Inside FontLab, it returns the original native objects. Outside FontLab, it provides declarations; it does not emulate the font editor. Use echopy for short imports or fontlab_echopy for explicit package names. Matching submodules imported through either name resolve to the same module objects. The examples below use Python 3.11.
title: Echopy

text: Install the fontlab-echopy wheel into the Python environment where you need its declarations. For host use, follow Install into FontLab . FontLab supplies the native modules; installing Echopy alone does not supply them. Do not install PySide or create a second Qt application inside FontLab. Run this outside FontLab to identify the installed distribution: # Outside FontLab from importlib.metadata import version import fontlab_echopy print ( version ( "fontlab-echopy" )) print ( fontlab_echopy . __file__ ) The package version identifies the installed declarations. It does not identify the running FontLab build or prove that every declaration matches that build. Keep the package version, native build and capture provenance together when reporting a mismatch. For maintenance work, see module values and their documentation : current-value identity, source-safe aliases, exact bookkeeping fields, absent offline values, captured attribute docs, maintained overlays and static Griffe checks. Its executable experiments use invented owned modules.
title: Install and identify your copy

text: This check runs outside FontLab and does not construct native objects: # Outside FontLab from echopy import fontlab as short_name from fontlab_echopy import fontlab as long_name assert short_name is long_name print ( short_name . __name__ ) Inside FontLab, check native identity before relying on argument conversion or isinstance . This snippet reads class objects only; it does not edit a font: # Inside FontLab; native execution required import fontlab from echopy import fontlab as fl assert fl . flNode is fontlab . flNode assert fl . flLayer is fontlab . flLayer Echopy does not wrap each node or layer in a Python replacement class. Native constructors, methods, errors and return values retain the host's behavior. A declaration does not repair a host defect or add an unsupported overload.
title: Use the two import names

text: Small .py facades keep runtime imports inexpensive. Their adjacent .pyi files hold the detailed declarations and docstrings. Inspecting an offline placeholder with inspect.signature can show a generic signature; read the sidecar when you need the recorded declaration. Locate the FontLab sidecar without importing the native module: # Outside FontLab from pathlib import Path import fontlab_echopy package = Path ( fontlab_echopy . __file__ ) . parent sidecar = package / "fontlab.pyi" assert sidecar . is_file () print ( sidecar . name ) Use Python's parser to extract one class and its documentation without executing its declaration. This example prints the recorded flNode class: # Outside FontLab import ast from pathlib import Path import fontlab_echopy sidecar = Path ( fontlab_echopy . __file__ ) . parent / "fontlab.pyi" source = sidecar . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" ) tree = ast . parse ( source ) node = next ( item for item in tree . body if isinstance ( item , ast . ClassDef ) and item . name == "flNode" ) print ( ast . get_docstring ( node ) or "No captured class documentation" ) print ( ast . get_source_segment ( source , node )) The same approach applies to fontgate.pyi and fontpr.pyi . PythonQt declarations use their package subdirectories. Read these files as text; do not execute them to create native objects outside the host.
title: Read the full declarations offline

text: Read the declaration and its docstring together. A Python signature can express argument order and defaults, but it cannot prove native overload selection or implicit conversions. Declaration text How to read it value, / The recorded parameter is positional-only. *, label The recorded parameter is keyword-only. count=3 The declaration records a literal default. value=... The actual default may be omitted; consult the captured documentation rather than passing ... as a substitute. *args, **kwargs The declaration is variadic. It may be a fallback for missing or ambiguous metadata; it does not mean every argument is accepted. Any The declaration does not constrain that type; it is not proof of native compatibility. @staticmethod or @classmethod The declaration records that binding kind. Its absence does not prove that an unknown native descriptor is an instance method. Print the recorded constructor signature and documentation from the installed sidecar. This reads text only, so an unsupported constructor is never called: # Outside FontLab import ast from pathlib import Path import fontlab_echopy path = Path ( fontlab_echopy . __file__ ) . parent / "fontlab.pyi" tree = ast . parse ( path . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" )) cls = next ( node for node in tree . body if isinstance ( node , ast . ClassDef ) and node . name == "flNode" ) constructor = next ( node for node in cls . body if isinstance ( node , ast . FunctionDef ) and node . name == "__init__" ) for decorator in constructor . decorator_list : print ( "@" + ast . unparse ( decorator )) print ( f "def { constructor . name } ( { ast . unparse ( constructor . args ) } )" ) print ( ast . get_docstring ( constructor ) or "No recorded constructor documentation" ) A single captured constructor can supply a specific signature. When several constructor records are present, the generator keeps a variadic declaration and retains their signatures and documentation together. Missing constructor records keep the generic fallback. These rules apply when generating new output; installing a newer generator does not refresh an older capture or sidecar. Python's AST reference describes the argument fields used here. Parsing and printing the declaration does not evaluate its annotations or default expressions.
title: Read a recorded call signature

text: Offline imports support documentation and analysis. An attempted native operation raises NativeUnavailable instead of returning a dummy object. This example expects that refusal in a normal Python process without FontLab's native modules: # Outside FontLab from echopy import fontlab as fl from fontlab_echopy import NativeUnavailable try : fl . flNode () except NativeUnavailable : print ( "Run native operations inside FontLab" ) else : raise AssertionError ( "This example requires an environment without FontLab" ) Catch this exception at an application's boundary if host access is optional. Do not catch every exception and present a failed native operation as success. Inside FontLab, other exceptions can indicate invalid arguments or a host defect.
title: Handle unavailable native operations

text: Read the packaged provenance to see which capture and enrichment records produced the declarations. The following prints its available top-level sections without assuming that every release uses an identical metadata schema: # Outside FontLab import json from pathlib import Path import fontlab_echopy path = Path ( fontlab_echopy . __file__ ) . parent / "_provenance.json" provenance = json . loads ( path . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" )) print ( sorted ( provenance )) A capture hash identifies input bytes, not complete behavioral coverage. Unknown signatures remain explicit as *args, **kwargs . PySide2-derived signatures are reference enrichment and may differ from FontLab's PythonQt bindings. Prefer a measured call on the actual host when an overload or property is uncertain.
title: Check capture provenance

text: Echopy shims only fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , fontlabpr (absent in measured builds), FL and PythonQt . The GlyphsApp , vanilla and related compatibility modules are supplied by Glyport (Echopy no longer ships them). They do not install Glyphs.app or turn an offline process into a running Glyphs-compatible session. Glyport owns the runtime providers used by adapted scripts. Producer-derived shim freshness and native API fidelity are separate checks: Check What it establishes Regenerate shims against pinned producer files Declarations match those producer inputs Compare the generated files and provenance The generated output is reproducible Run offline tests The tested Python behavior works outside FontLab Run installed artifacts in FontLab The exercised behavior works on that host build FontLab's menu and panel names (formerly fontlabapp_shim ) belong to Fontlabapp. Regenerating them does not refresh Echopy's capture of FontLab's native modules.
title: Understand runtime shims

text: FontLab's PythonQt exposes widgets through QtGui , not a QtWidgets namespace. This native-only identity check does not create or show a widget: # Inside FontLab; native execution required from PythonQt import QtGui as native_gui from echopy.PythonQt import QtGui assert QtGui . QWidget is native_gui . QWidget Use the existing application and event loop. Do not construct QApplication , start an application-wide exec() , or load another Qt runtime. For practical panels, use the shared application helpers and retain their handles until close. Do not probe every property on arbitrary native instances: some getters require initialized native state and can crash the host. Class declarations and recorded metadata are safer starting points for discovery.
title: Use PythonQt inside FontLab

text: Maintainers can test capture, generation and merge without FontLab. This example was checked with the private, uncommitted Echopy artifact 0.2.4.dev6+ga4f2fbf48.d20261101 containing the constructor-binding and decorator-resolution repairs. Earlier artifacts share this version but fail constructor binding or captured-name shadowing checks; use archive hashes to identify the tested snapshot. These fixtures are ordinary Python classes, not models of FontLab or PythonQt and not evidence of a published release. # Outside FontLab; owned fixture, no native calls import ast import builtins import inspect from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace from fontlab_echopy.tooling.generate import generate from fontlab_echopy.tooling.merge import merge class Fixture : def __init__ ( receiver , value = 3 , / , * , label = "a,b" ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not construct instances" ) def ordinary ( receiver , value = 3 , / , * , label = "a,b" ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call this method" ) @staticmethod def measure ( value = 3 , / , * , label = "a,b" ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call this method" ) @classmethod def create ( owner , value = 3 ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call this method" ) # Captured names can match Python builtins. These are ordinary methods. def staticmethod ( receiver ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call this method" ) def classmethod ( receiver ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call this method" ) class StaticInit : @staticmethod def __init__ ( value = 3 , / , * , label = "a,b" ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call constructors" ) class ClassInit : @classmethod def __init__ ( owner , value = 3 , / , * , label = "a,b" ): raise AssertionError ( "Metadata inspection must not call constructors" ) captured = namespace ( SimpleNamespace ( Fixture = Fixture , StaticInit = StaticInit , ClassInit = ClassInit ), "owned_fixture" , ) classes = { item [ "name" ]: item for item in captured [ "classes" ]} records = { item [ "name" ]: item for item in classes [ "Fixture" ][ "methods" ]} assert records [ "measure" ][ "binding" ] == "staticmethod" assert records [ "create" ][ "binding" ] == "classmethod" assert records [ "create" ][ "signature" ] . startswith ( "(owner," ) assert records [ "ordinary" ] . get ( "binding" ) == "instancemethod" assert classes [ "Fixture" ][ "constructors" ][ 0 ][ "binding" ] == "instancemethod" for name , kind in (( "StaticInit" , "staticmethod" ), ( "ClassInit" , "classmethod" )): assert classes [ name ][ "constructors" ][ 0 ] . get ( "binding" ) == kind , name assert classes [ "ClassInit" ][ "constructors" ][ 0 ][ "signature" ] . startswith ( "(owner," ) with TemporaryDirectory ( prefix = "echopy-fixture-" ) as folder : raw , merged = Path ( folder ) / "raw" , Path ( folder ) / "merged" generate ({ "modules" : { "owned_fixture" : { "namespace" : captured }}}, raw ) merge ( raw , merged , []) tree = ast . parse (( merged / "owned_fixture.pyi" ) . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" )) builtin_prefix = next ( ( alias . asname + "." for node in tree . body if isinstance ( node , ast . Import ) for alias in node . names if alias . name == "builtins" ), "" ) emitted = { node . name : node for node in tree . body if isinstance ( node , ast . ClassDef )} cls = emitted [ "Fixture" ] methods = { node . name : node for node in cls . body if isinstance ( node , ast . FunctionDef )} for name , kind in (( "measure" , "staticmethod" ), ( "create" , "classmethod" )): assert [ ast . unparse ( node ) for node in methods [ name ] . decorator_list ] == [ builtin_prefix + kind ] print ( name , ast . unparse ( methods [ name ] . args )) assert [ arg . arg for arg in methods [ "measure" ] . args . posonlyargs ] == [ "value" ] assert ast . literal_eval ( methods [ "measure" ] . args . kw_defaults [ 0 ]) == "a,b" for name in ( "ordinary" , "__init__" ): args = methods [ name ] . args assert [ arg . arg for arg in args . posonlyargs ] == [ "receiver" , "value" ] assert not args . args # No invented self before the recorded receiver. assert ast . literal_eval ( args . kw_defaults [ 0 ]) == "a,b" print ( name , ast . unparse ( args )) for name , kind , arguments in ( ( "StaticInit" , "staticmethod" , [ "value" ]), ( "ClassInit" , "classmethod" , [ "owner" , "value" ]), ): constructor = next ( node for node in emitted [ name ] . body if isinstance ( node , ast . FunctionDef ) and node . name == "__init__" ) assert [ ast . unparse ( node ) for node in constructor . decorator_list ] == [ builtin_prefix + kind ] assert [ arg . arg for arg in constructor . args . posonlyargs ] == arguments assert not constructor . args . args assert ast . literal_eval ( constructor . args . kw_defaults [ 0 ]) == "a,b" assert ast . unparse ( constructor . returns ) == "None" # Execute only these owned declarations, never native captures or methods. for path in ( raw / "owned_fixture.py" , merged / "owned_fixture.pyi" ): values = { "__name__" : "echopy_doc_owned_declarations" } exec ( compile ( path . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" ), str ( path ), "exec" ), values ) for member , kind in (( "measure" , builtins . staticmethod ), ( "create" , builtins . classmethod )): assert type ( inspect . getattr_static ( values [ "Fixture" ], member )) is kind for member in ( "staticmethod" , "classmethod" ): assert inspect . isfunction ( inspect . getattr_static ( values [ "Fixture" ], member )) The temporary files are deleted when the block finishes. Only owned generated declarations execute; no fixture method runs and no instance is constructed. Captured builtin names remain ordinary methods, while generated decorators retain builtin identity. Known Python static/class descriptors preserve their binding. Known ordinary methods and constructors preserve their recorded receiver, even when it is not named self ; inserting another receiver would change the callable's arguments. This identification uses Python function descriptors, not parameter-name guesses. Unclassified native descriptors keep the existing fallback. Tested private archive SHA256 values: Archive SHA256 Wheel 6f82d7856a52e7befb50c43e08b9786d86300303fff409dcf3bdb7a05f92e5ac sdist fe8ae224794fae742dfd193775febc2dd8f21d7dcf840af4edfad4e2c4f24bdb A passing fixture demonstrates the metadata pipeline only. It does not establish that every native wrapper exposes enough information to classify its methods. For a real mismatch report, include the installed Echopy version, actual FontLab build, relevant capture/provenance hashes, the exact declaration and the observed call or error from an owned native fixture. Do not replace an uncertain declaration with a guessed signature merely to silence a type checker.
title: Check the metadata pipeline with an owned fixture

text: Native spellings can contain characters that Python identifiers cannot use. For example, A-B and A_B both map to A_B . Emitting both would replace one class declaration and could make a name-only coverage check look complete. The generator rejects such collisions before writing any scope or removing stale output. Its error identifies the owner, original spellings and shared identifier. This example uses synthetic metadata and a disposable directory. It demonstrates that the existing file remains byte-for-byte unchanged when generation refuses the collision. It does not load a native module or execute generated code. # Outside FontLab; owned capture and output directory from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from fontlab_echopy.tooling.generate import generate capture = { "modules" : { "owned_collision" : { "namespace" : { "classes" : [{ "name" : "A-B" }, { "name" : "A_B" }], }}}} with TemporaryDirectory ( prefix = "echopy-collision-" ) as directory : output = Path ( directory ) previous = output / "owned_collision.py" previous . write_bytes ( b "# Previous owned output \n " ) before = { path . name : path . read_bytes () for path in output . iterdir ()} try : generate ( capture , output ) except ValueError as error : assert "Source name collision in owned_collision" in str ( error ) assert "'A-B'" in str ( error ) and "'A_B'" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "The conflicting declarations must be refused" ) assert { path . name : path . read_bytes () for path in output . iterdir ()} == before for name in ( "_bind" , "_echopy_unavailable" ): helper_capture = { "modules" : { "owned_helper" : { "namespace" : { "functions" : [{ "name" : name }], }}}} try : generate ( helper_capture , output ) except ValueError as error : assert "Reserved source name in owned_helper" in str ( error ) assert repr ( name ) in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "Captured helpers must not replace facade machinery" ) assert { path . name : path . read_bytes () for path in output . iterdir ()} == before Retain the capture and report the conflicting names. Do not delete a captured member to make coverage pass. This preflight checks both declared members and captured name inventories, across all scopes before writing. It is not a general transaction for filesystem errors. Top-level names mapping to Any , globals , _bind , _unavailable , _echopy_native , _echopy_name , _echopy_aliases or _echopy_unavailable are refused because they replace facade helpers or state. The rule also applies to normalized spellings such as -bind becoming _bind . Same-named class members remain allowed. Other built-in shadowing and duplicate records with an identical native spelling remain separate checks. The low-level module_source renderer does not perform this whole-capture preflight. The example requires the private helper-name preflight artifact. The earlier deletion-repair artifact has the same version string but does not reject the helper capture. Neither is a published release. Tested archive SHA256 values: Archive SHA256 Wheel 2a18dcdcc5aeff7879a24614f27c14ec8cb44109af5db741bef132980d8416c5 sdist fc0a00dd9d196bcaddbf47b3405a895b84db4667efacdf6303bf97d77b5e9df6
title: Reject ambiguous declaration names before writing

text: A native name such as value-name cannot appear after a dot in Python source. New declarations expose it as value_name . The alias refers to the original native attribute: later native changes remain visible, and writes or deletion through the alias affect the original spelling. This applies to top-level classes, functions, attributes, constants and modules. It does not wrap native objects or rename members on native classes. The following fixture generates and merges an annotated value, then loads the small facade twice: first without a provider, then with an owned module double. The offline annotation has no value. Ordinary native attributes also disappear from facade lookup and dir() when deleted, and reappear when rebound. The double demonstrates routing only; it is not FontLab or a test of font mutations. # Outside FontLab; owned metadata, modules and temporary files only import sys from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from types import ModuleType from fontlab_echopy.tooling.generate import generate from fontlab_echopy.tooling.merge import merge provider_name = "echopy_doc_owned_alias_provider" facade_name = "echopy_doc_owned_alias_facade" assert provider_name not in sys . modules and facade_name not in sys . modules capture = { "modules" : { provider_name : { "namespace" : { "names" : [ "value-name" , "ordinary" ], "attributes" : [{ "name" : name , "type" : "int" } for name in ( "value-name" , "ordinary" )], }}}} with TemporaryDirectory ( prefix = "echopy-alias-" ) as directory : raw , merged = Path ( directory ) / "raw" , Path ( directory ) / "merged" report = generate ( capture , raw ) assert report [ "modules" ][ provider_name ][ "missing_names" ] == [] merge ( raw , merged , []) path = merged / ( provider_name + ".py" ) try : offline = ModuleType ( facade_name ) offline . __file__ = str ( path ) sys . modules [ facade_name ] = offline exec ( compile ( path . read_text (), str ( path ), "exec" ), offline . __dict__ ) assert "value_name" in offline . __annotations__ assert not hasattr ( offline , "value_name" ) # No invented None value. provider = ModuleType ( provider_name ) provider . ordinary = 5 setattr ( provider , "value-name" , 7 ) sys . modules [ provider_name ] = provider live = ModuleType ( facade_name ) live . __file__ = str ( path ) sys . modules [ facade_name ] = live exec ( compile ( path . read_text (), str ( path ), "exec" ), live . __dict__ ) assert live . ordinary == 5 del provider . ordinary assert not hasattr ( live , "ordinary" ) # No stale copied value. assert "ordinary" not in dir ( live ) provider . ordinary = 6 assert live . ordinary == 6 assert "ordinary" in dir ( live ) assert live . value_name == 7 setattr ( provider , "value-name" , 9 ) assert live . value_name == 9 live . value_name = 11 assert getattr ( provider , "value-name" ) == 11 assert not hasattr ( provider , "value_name" ) del live . value_name assert not hasattr ( provider , "value-name" ) assert not hasattr ( live , "value_name" ) finally : sys . modules . pop ( facade_name , None ) sys . modules . pop ( provider_name , None ) The exec calls load only the generated owned fixture. Temporary files and module registrations are removed even if an assertion fails. The double does not establish how a real FontLab attribute setter affects document state. Annotation-only values remain unreadable offline, while declared functions and constructors raise NativeUnavailable when called. This example requires the private alias and ordinary-deletion repairs. The earlier alias-only build shares the version 0.2.4.dev6+ga4f2fbf48.d20261101 but fails the ordinary-deletion assertion. Tested archives are identified by SHA256, not version text alone: Archive SHA256 Wheel d77ba8a507702b53382a3c9c31211ef34ec29ba809b1d1d368d878e2eb072699 sdist 1d9f9e6f203aedc513d287838705461bafa94a60fe482c61c108f313cf18b27a These checks do not qualify actual native bindings, a regenerated reference site or a published release. Existing class aliases in merged facades remain supported; new nonidentifier declarations require reviewed generation from the capture.
title: Read and update a native name through its source alias

text: Glyphs.app compatibility is not an Echopy feature. Glyport owns the GlyphsApp , vanilla , AppKit , Cocoa , Foundation and objc modules and the glyph-info, description and manager providers behind them; Echopy no longer ships its own copies. Read the Glyport guide , the compound , description and manager guides, and the Glyport reference . Echopy's own declarations cover only FontLab's native modules.
title: Glyphs compatibility lives in Glyport

text: The offline examples can run in an ordinary Echopy installation. The two native identity snippets require FontLab; compiling them is not native verification. Neither example tests font edits, Undo/Redo, saving or reopening documents. fontlabpr was absent in the recorded FontLab 9.0.9780 baseline. Treat that as a build-specific observation, not a promise about every later release. Confirm availability in the actual target host before designing a dependency on it. Reference: fontlab_echopy , fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , PythonQt , and Glyport . For capture maintenance, see complete namespace discovery . Its five executable owned experiments distinguish discovered scope from capture-relative declaration coverage, without querying FontLab or refreshing retained native/generated inputs.
title: Verification boundaries

text: The FontLab Python packages split by one question: where does your code run, and what does it need to talk to? Each package owns one answer. Pick the package that matches your answer instead of reaching across a boundary. Package Role Remopy Pip-installable remote control of a running FontLab from an ordinary Python process outside it. Glyport Runs unmodified Glyphs.app scripts and plugins inside FontLab. Fontport FontParts, fontTools pens, UFO and DesignSpace interoperability. No user interface. Echopy Generates documented, pure-Python passthrough shims of fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , fontlabpr , FL and PythonQt . Fontlabapp The large object and UI API: menus, panels, windows, drawing overlays, dialogs. Fly Nine short, lazy import aliases for the packages above. It adds no behaviour. Aidus Code An in-FontLab coding agent with a graphical dock. Pythonqtside Runs PySide2-style code on FontLab's PythonQt. Scriptmix A collection of practical menu scripts for FontLab 9. Examples PythonQt-rich example scripts that show how to build panels and tools. Plugmix New: native FontLab plugins, reporters, filters, palettes, tools and General plugins.
title: Ecosystem and package boundaries

title: Where does my code go?

text: Outside versus inside. Remopy is the only package meant for code outside FontLab. Everything else imports FontLab's own modules and needs the host. Interop versus UI. Fontport converts font data and has no user interface. Its Qt editors live in fontlabapp.fontui and call Fontport lazily. Shims versus behaviour. Echopy documents and mirrors the native API. It does not add features. Behaviour that goes beyond the native API belongs in Fontlabapp. Compatibility layers stay separate. Glyport carries Glyphs.app behaviour; Pythonqtside carries PySide2 behaviour. Neither leaks into Fontlabapp. Aliases are not an API. Fly resolves names; it never wraps or extends the module it returns.
title: Boundary rules

text: The Python examples ( fontlab-python-examples ) are one hundred menu scripts that show useful Python and PythonQt workflows in FontLab 9: inspecting fonts, building proofs, editing selected data and showing modeless panels. Each script states its setup, scope and limits, and some change fonts, so read its Usage and Setup text before you run it. Like Scriptmix , this is a script collection, not a runtime package. The runtime code for the original Models, Forms and GetGo menus lives in a separate package, fontlab-python-lessons , inside the repository.
title: Examples

text: Use FontLab 9 with its embedded Python 3.11 (arm64). Install fontlab-fly , fontlab-fontlabapp and fontlab-python-lessons into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Add the Lessons fonttools extra for the pen and export lessons. Copy the category folders from the repository's Scripts/ folder into a FontLab Scripts location, keeping the one-level Scripts/<Category>/<Tool>.py layout. Open an owned copy of a font and run a menu from its category. Never start a second QApplication or install another Qt binding in FontLab.
title: Install

text: The Scripts/ folder holds Contours, Designer, Dialogs, Drag And Drop, Drawing, Forms, GetGo Fonts, Graphics, Models, Text, Tools, Widgets and Windows.
title: Categories

text: Tools > Kerning Copy Rules turns A|V A|W = T|o @ -5 into pairs, shows a preview, and applies them as one Undo step. Contours > Node Table lists the current layer's nodes and edits X and Y. Dialogs > Glyph Batch Recipe Settings builds a recipe that Glyph Proof Batch Wizard turns into proof text.
title: Examples

text: Fly gives the FontLab Python ecosystem nine short, lazy import aliases. Each alias is the exact original module object, not a copy or wrapper. Alias Module fl echopy.fontlab fg echopy.fontgate pr echopy.fontpr qt PythonQt tr typerig ap fontlabapp qs pythonqtside gp fontlab_glyport fp fontlab_fontport
title: fly

text: Install fontlab-fly with its target packages (Echopy, TypeRig, Fontlabapp, Pythonqtside, Glyport, Fontport) into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab .
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from fly import fl , fg , qt , gp , fp font = fl . CurrentFont () # same function as fontlab.CurrentFont import fly.gp , fontlab_glyport assert fly . gp is fontlab_glyport
title: Quick start

text: Child imports route to the canonical package: from fly.fp.pens import FontGatePointPen # same object as fontlab_fontport.pens from fly.tr.core.objects.point import Point
title: Examples

text: Importing fly loads none of its targets; each alias loads on first access. qt needs FontLab's native PythonQt; outside FontLab it raises a clear ModuleNotFoundError . Missing target packages raise the same way. Reference: fly .
title: Behaviour and limits

text: Fontlabapp is the Python layer for FontLab's application surface: menus and actions, panels, preferences, versions and paths, Glyph and Preview windows, drawing overlays, and docks, dialogs and widgets you create yourself. Fontport's Qt editors live here Fontport's Qt editors moved into Fontlabapp as fontlabapp.fontui . Fontlabapp is where FontLab user interface code belongs; Fontport keeps font-data interoperability only.
title: fontlabapp

text: Install fontlab-fontlabapp into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Its utilities import outside FontLab without loading native modules or creating preference files.
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from fontlabapp import Application app = Application ( with_ui = True , with_preflib = False ) print ( app . versions . app_version ) with app . control as fl : print ( fl . fonts ()) fl . panel ( "preview" ) . show () fl . preview . set_text ( "Hamburgefonts" ) . set_font_size ( 48 )
title: Quick start

text: Draw on the Glyph window without changing the font. The overlay is removed when the context exits: from PythonQt import QtGui with app . control as fl : glyph_window = fl . glyph_window () # raises if no Glyph window is open def paint ( painter ): painter . setPen ( QtGui . QColor ( "#008000" )) painter . drawLine ( 30 , 30 , 100 , 100 ) with glyph_window . draw ( paint , coordinates = "canvas" ) as overlay : overlay . raise_if_failed () Create your own panel, modeless dialog or tool widget: def build ( widget ): layout = QtGui . QVBoxLayout ( widget ) layout . addWidget ( QtGui . QLabel ( "My tool" , widget )) with app . control as fl : panel = fl . create_panel ( "My panel" , build , area = "right" ) panel . close () Edit vertical metrics or alignment zones on several masters as one Undo step: from fontlabapp import master_metrics , zone_native from fontlabapp.scripting import current_package package = current_package () # the current font, Font window active master_metrics . write_master_metrics ( package , { "Regular" : { "xHeight" : 500 }, "Bold" : { "capsHeight" : 705 }}, title = "Master Metrics" , ) zones = zone_native . backend () # the zone_editor.Backend for this font These writers refuse before any history call when FontLab is not on the GUI thread, when a Glyph window is the active editor, or when the font has an unknown field or master. A failure during the write restores every written value and adds nothing to Undo ( font_history.RolledBackError ). After Undo or Redo of such a step, FontLab shows only some metric guidelines until the font is reopened (fl#8574); the saved file is correct. outline_extent.vertical_extent(layer) measures glyph extents from outline nodes, because flLayer.boundingBox can stay stale after scripted edits (fl#8575). Fontlabapp owns the Python names for FontLab's menus, actions and panels (formerly the Echopy fontlabapp_shim ).
title: Examples

text: fontlabapp.fontui provides ready-made Qt tools that work on an explicit font model (ufoLib2, defcon, or live FontParts objects from Fontport ). Install the extra that matches the tools you need: Extra Adds fontlab-fontlabapp[fontui] font_browser , glyph_browser , glyph_preview , features_editor , designspace_panel fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport] (once Fontport is published; until then install both from checkouts) The FontParts-bound editors, which call Fontport lazily: font_info_editor , groups_editor , kerning_editor , transform_editor , batch_panel and glyph_sequence The FontParts-bound editors moved here from Fontport. Importing them from fontlab_fontport.ui raises an ImportError that names this module. Each function returns a handle. Keep a reference to it, show its .widget and call .close() when you are done. The browsers, preview and features editor also have .refresh() for edits made elsewhere; designspace_panel does not: # Inside FontLab, with the fontui extra and ufoLib2 installed from ufoLib2 import Font from fontlabapp.fontui import font_browser font = Font () # a detached demonstration model font . info . familyName = "Browser demonstration" glyph = font . newGlyph ( "A" ) glyph . width = 600 pen = glyph . getPen () pen . moveTo (( 50 , 0 )); pen . lineTo (( 300 , 700 )); pen . lineTo (( 550 , 0 )); pen . closePath () browser = font_browser ([ font ]) # keep this handle alive browser . widget . resize ( 850 , 1000 ) browser . widget . show () # ... later: browser . close () The features editor stages changes and applies them in one validated batch; a model without a batch apply opens read-only. While a script has unfinished point edits on a font, the controls that follow FontLab changes skip that font's reload rather than discard the edits, and show "A font has unfinished script edits; its view updates when the script finishes." The view updates on the next change after the script completes.
title: FontUI: font and glyph browsers and editors

text: Application(with_preflib=False) inspects the application without opening or saving the preference library. Native wrappers may be recreated on each access: compare fonts by native id, not with is . Created panels, dialogs and widgets own only themselves; close them when done. FontLab can keep its main window hidden. create_panel re-floats a dock that would otherwise be docked into that hidden window, so the panel stays visible. Reference: fontlabapp .
title: Limits

text: Fontport connects FontLab 9 to FontParts, UFO and DesignSpace data, and to the fontTools, fontPens and ufoLib2 libraries around them. It provides point pens over native FontGate glyphs, detached FontParts and UFO snapshots, and live FontParts objects bound to an open FontLab document. No user interface Fontport has no UI. Its Qt editors now live in fontlabapp.fontui .
title: Fontport

text: Fontport requires fontlab-fontlabapp (version 0.2.26.dev150 or later), plus defcon, fontTools, fontPens, FontParts and ufoLib2. Fontlabapp is not on a package index, so install it from a checkout or wheel first, then Fontport, into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Importing the package outside FontLab is safe; native access loads on demand.
title: Install

text: Draw into a native glyph with a fontTools pen: # Inside FontLab, with a glyph you own from fontlab_fontport.pens import FontGatePointPen from fontTools.pens.pointPen import SegmentToPointPen pen = SegmentToPointPen ( FontGatePointPen ( glyph )) pen . moveTo (( 0 , 0 )) pen . lineTo (( 200 , 0 )) pen . lineTo (( 100 , 300 )) pen . closePath ()
title: Quick start

text: Edit a detached FontParts copy, then write it back explicitly: from fontlab_fontport.transfer import to_fontparts , write_glyph snapshot = to_fontparts ( native_glyph ) # a real fontshell RGlyph snapshot . width = 600 write_glyph ( snapshot , target_glyph ) # explicit destination Bind live FontParts objects to an open FontLab document: from fontlab_fontport.host import NativeFontBackend from fontlab_fontport.live import RFont font = RFont ( NativeFontBackend ( font_id )) # font_id: the document's FontLab id font [ "A" ] . width = 600 # updates the FontLab glyph font . close () # detaches; the document stays open Stage font information and apply it in one validated batch: font . info . apply ({ "familyName" : "My Family" , "ascender" : 810.5 }, undo_name = "Edit font information" )
title: Examples

text: Fontport exports a whole FontLab font to UFO and DesignSpace, and opens UFO and DesignSpace files as new FontLab documents. Export a multi-master font as a .designspace plus one UFO per master. This example needs FontLab, because it reads a live font: from fontlab_fontport.designspace_io import export_designspace path , losses = export_designspace ( backend , "/absolute/path/Family.designspace" ) print ( path ) print ( * losses , sep = " \n " ) # what the export did not carry export_designspace(backend, destination, document=None) reads the backend and never changes it. Axes, master locations and instances come from the native package unless you pass your own DesignSpaceDocument . Each master is written as <stem>-<master>.ufo beside the .designspace , with its own outlines, anchors and kerning. write_designspace(font, document, destination, master_kerning) does the file writing for a font you already exported. Nothing is overwritten. Open UFO and DesignSpace files through FontLab's native open_font (this also needs FontLab): from fontlab_fontport.native_import import import_designspace , import_ufo_native backend = import_designspace ( "/absolute/path/Family.designspace" ) # or: import_ufo_native("/absolute/path/Master.ufo") # one master backend . close () # the result is an owned document Both need absolute paths, a matching suffix and an existing file; FontLab resolves the source UFOs of a designspace. Import converts nothing in Fontport. The file writing itself runs without FontLab. This example splits a ufoLib2 font whose layers are the masters into Family.designspace and one UFO per master, with each master's own kerning: from fontTools.designspaceLib import ( AxisDescriptor , DesignSpaceDocument , SourceDescriptor ) from ufoLib2 import Font from fontlab_fontport.designspace_io import write_designspace font = Font () font . layers . renameLayer ( font . layers . defaultLayer . name , "Light" ) font . layers . newLayer ( "Bold" ) for layer in font . layers : layer . newGlyph ( "A" ) . width = 500 doc = DesignSpaceDocument () axis = AxisDescriptor ( name = "Weight" , tag = "wght" , minimum = 300 , default = 300 , maximum = 700 ) doc . addAxis ( axis ) for name , weight in (( "Light" , 300 ), ( "Bold" , 700 )): doc . addSource ( SourceDescriptor ( name = name , location = { "Weight" : weight })) kerning = { "Light" : {( "A" , "A" ): - 50 }, "Bold" : {( "A" , "A" ): - 80 }} path = write_designspace ( font , doc , "/absolute/path/Family.designspace" , kerning ) Every source name must be a layer of the font, and nothing is overwritten. What an export loses. The losses list names it: designspace rules, axis and location labels, instances' generated UFOs (instances are listed only), and per-master groups, info, lib and features, which come from the key master and are shared by every master UFO. Brace layers are not exported. Kerning is the exception: each master's own kerning is exported. Why Fontport does not use fgFont.save("x.ufo") . The native UFO save is lossy. In a measured case it wrote the current master only (a three-master font gave one layer), no kerning.plist , and no anchors. The MCP save_font tool writes only VFJ, VFC and VFJP. Fontport's own exporter reads every master, so it keeps all masters, kerning and anchors. Use VFJ when you need a lossless native archive. See docs/UFO-INTERCHANGE.md in the Fontport repository for the full table.
title: UFO and DesignSpace

text: The six FontParts-bound Qt editors ( font_info_editor , groups_editor , kerning_editor , transform_editor , batch_panel and glyph_sequence ) live in fontlabapp.fontui . They call Fontport lazily, so install both packages in the same environment (Fontlabapp first). Once both are published, the Fontlabapp fontport extra installs Fontport for you. # old (removed): from fontlab_fontport.ui import font_info_editor from fontlabapp.fontui import font_info_editor fontlab_fontport.ui remains for one release as a tombstone: reading any name from it raises ImportError("fontlab_fontport.ui moved to fontlabapp.fontui") . The batch panel still starts a separate Python 3.11+ process that needs fontlab-fontport . Vanilla support moved to fontlab_glyport.ui.session . Fontport also reads and writes feature blocks ( fontlab_fontport.feature_blocks : read_feature_blocks and write_feature_blocks ), which need the original font to be active and compare the source snapshot before writing.
title: The editors moved to Fontlabapp

text: Undo: an edit through the live binding is undone by the first Edit > Undo. FontLab records one extra, empty Undo row with it (exact one-row Undo is the unsupported capability glyph.exactSingleUndo ; information batches likewise report info.exactSingleUndo ). Font information: metrics ( ascender , descender , capHeight , xHeight , italicAngle ), styleName and note are written to the current key master only; family name, version fields, copyright and units per em are stored on the font. Supported fields: familyName , styleName , unitsPerEm , ascender , descender , capHeight , xHeight , italicAngle , versionMajor , versionMinor , note and copyright . The structured fields openTypeOS2Panose , openTypeOS2WeightClass , openTypeOS2WidthClass , postscriptStemSnapH and postscriptStemSnapV are also written to the key master only. OpenType name records are refused, since FontLab does not persist them through this route. Default and strict modes: the v1.0.0 editing contract is the default. Stricter guarantees are opt-in: require_single_undo=True on font.info.apply and require_persistence=True on group and save operations refuse instead of accepting the extra Undo row or a legacy group mode. Named refusals: layer create, delete and rename; glyph rename; guidelines and images; hinted outlines; fractional anchors and kerning; non-ASCII names for new glyphs and groups; multi-layer UFO import; world selection. Each raises UnsupportedCapability with its name before anything is written. font.capabilities() lists every capability with its evidence. Edits made in FontLab itself do not notify the binding: call font.refresh() and reacquire glyph and layer handles afterwards. FontParts coverage (FontParts 1.1.1 upstream tests, host-free backend run): 1,748 of 1,797 pass, 48 raise a named UnsupportedCapability , one is skipped upstream, none fail unclassified. These are not FontLab-native passes. An unexpected FontLab error during the final write can leave partial changes; develop on a copy of your font. Reference: fontlab_fontport . Licence: Apache 2.0.
title: Behaviour and limits

text: The manager state, ranks and placeholder-font experiments show raw container identity, retained rank caches, debug/shared construction, observer cleanup and source-derived font/error control flow over visible owned primitives. Actual native fonts/defaults/resources remain separately qualified. The sidebar and document guide explains dynamic tree filtering, defaults, row ownership, list expansion, count publication and document-selected local loading with independent executable owned experiments. The numerical ordinary-artifact results below identify their retained predecessor checkpoint. The current manager/profile guide documents the H source changes. Earlier source assumptions are corrected below; original preimages remain in verification evidence. Old receipts do not qualify the new ordinary tuple or native behavior. Run the owned graph setup first for examples using owned_parsed_manager ; those examples explicitly select actual parsed owned data before a metadata refresh or rename. Glyport runs Glyphs scripts and plugins inside FontLab. It inspects and adapts the original source (including Glyphs 2 / Python 2 code), gives each run a live GlyphsApp model backed by the FontLab font, and translates Vanilla, AppKit and NIB/XIB interfaces to FontLab's Qt. Original files are never modified. The detached-transform examples below were checked with the ordinary development artifact 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548 and App 0.2.26.dev159+gb1e905b61 . They do not claim a published release or qualify native FontLab behavior. Older packages may not have the same input checks or overflow preflight.
title: Glyport

text: Install fontlab-glyport into FontLab's Python folder together with a matching fontlab-fontlabapp ; see Install into FontLab . Its dependencies include fissix and glyphslib . Its inspection API also works outside FontLab. Glyport never installs packages for you.
title: Install

text: Assess a script without running it: from fontlab_glyport import inspect_source assessment = inspect_source ( "OriginalScript.py" ) print ( assessment . required_capabilities ) For ordinary Glyphs imports, activate Glyport on FontLab's GUI thread first. The default profile is glyphs4 ; pass profile="glyphs3" or "glyphs2" to match the script, and call deactivate() when you are done: import fontlab_glyport ; fontlab_glyport . activate () from GlyphsApp import * Run a Glyphs script inside FontLab: # Inside FontLab from fontlab_glyport import run_script handle = run_script ( "OriginalScript.py" ) # profile chosen from the source print ( handle . state , handle . receipt ) handle . close ()
title: Quick start

text: Install a plugin bundle and remove it again: from fontlab_glyport import install_plugin plugin = install_plugin ( "MyReporter.glyphsReporter" ) # ... the reporter now draws in the Glyph window ... plugin . unload () # removes every registration Adapt Glyphs 2 source into an owned cache, keeping a map back to original lines: from fontlab_glyport import adapt_source adapted = adapt_source ( "OldScript.py" , profile = "glyphs2" , cache_dir = ".glyport-cache" ) code = adapted . compile () # compiles; does not execute print ( adapted . translate ( 1 , 1 )) # generated position -> original position
title: Examples

text: These examples run outside FontLab. They create Python-owned draft objects and change no open font. They demonstrate Glyport's arithmetic and object semantics; they do not test copying a native layer, native rounding, Undo or saved fonts.
title: Work with detached geometry

text: The six values (a, b, c, d, tx, ty) map a point as x_new = a*x + c*y + tx , y_new = b*x + d*y + ty . This example changes a path and an anchor on an owned detached layer. It does not resolve components or measure a native layer's bounds. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSAnchor , GSNode , GSPath from fontlab_glyport.model.copies import DetachedLayer layer = DetachedLayer () layer . paths = [ GSPath ([ GSNode (( 2 , 3 )), GSNode (( - 4 , 5 ))])] layer . anchors = [ GSAnchor ( "top" , ( 11 , 19 ))] layer . applyTransform (( 2 , 1 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 )) assert [ tuple ( node . position ) for node in layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ] == [ ( 18 , 20 ), ( 12 , 22 ) ] assert tuple ( layer . anchors [ 0 ] . position ) == ( 84 , 93 ) Composition order matters. A clockwise rotation followed by one combined scale/shear matrix differs from scale, then shear, then counterclockwise rotation. Do not use a similarly named menu as proof that two scripts implement the same transform, layer scope or component policy.
title: Apply one affine matrix

text: Layer/path transform entry points reject NaN and infinity before backend calls, history or geometry mutation. Finite zero and negative scales retain their existing behavior; this check does not forbid flattening or reflecting geometry. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSNode , GSPath path = GSPath ([ GSNode (( 2 , 3 ))]) before = [ tuple ( node . position ) for node in path . nodes ] try : path . applyTransform (( float ( "nan" ), 0 , 0 , 1 , 0 , 0 )) except ValueError as error : print ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "The non-finite matrix should be refused." ) assert [ tuple ( node . position ) for node in path . nodes ] == before Finite coefficients can still overflow when multiplied by a large coordinate. Python-managed paths, detached layers and selection-aware layer transforms calculate all results before entering history or writing. A failure on a later point therefore leaves earlier points untouched: from fontlab_glyport.model import GSNode , GSPath path = GSPath ([ GSNode (( 2 , 3 )), GSNode (( 1e308 , 5 ))]) before = [ tuple ( node . position ) for node in path . nodes ] try : path . applyTransform (( 2 , 0 , 0 , 2 , 13 , - 7 )) except ValueError as error : print ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "The overflowing result should be refused." ) assert [ tuple ( node . position ) for node in path . nodes ] == before This is arithmetic preflight, not a transaction. Setter failures after preflight, native coordinate conversion, and the native whole-layer transform remain outside that guarantee. The native layer route calls FontLab's flLayer.applyTransform ; it must not be assumed to preserve metrics and guides like the detached example.
title: Reject invalid coefficients and overflow before writing

text: The following deliberate alias illustrates draft-object identity. It is not a recommendation to create duplicate nodes in a font. Each occurrence uses the previous virtual result, so two factors of two give a factor of four. If a later occurrence overflows, preflight refuses the operation before the first write. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSNode , GSPath node = GSNode (( 2 , 3 )) path = GSPath ([ node , node ]) path . applyTransform (( 2 , 0 , 0 , 2 , 0 , 0 )) assert tuple ( node . position ) == ( 8 , 12 ) This identity rule covers the same draft object and ordinary cached live proxies. It does not prove equivalent behavior for distinct wrappers sharing external storage. A script that repeats a parent glyph may also need to recompute each layer's bounds between visits; repeatedly applying one fixed matrix is not a substitute for that workflow.
title: Repeated objects are transformed per occurrence

text: A layer's name is not its identifier. Ordinary auxiliaries have their own layerId and an associatedMasterId ; a missing name must not make an auxiliary look like its master. Use the ID to address a layer, and keep the raw name when checking a source script's condition. Converting it with str() turns None into the text "None" ; if not layer.name also matches an empty string. Layer Raw name isMasterLayer Matches name is None and not isMasterLayer Master Master name True No Unnamed auxiliary None False Yes Empty-string auxiliary "" False No Named auxiliary "Backup" False No The following diagnostic fixture runs outside FontLab. FakeBackend is a test double, not a font importer. It supplies the three auxiliary name values to the same proxy model used by Glyport. The example reads every glyph, keeps names unmodified and collects matching identities without deleting anything. from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.backend import LayerInfo from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend backend = FakeBackend () for identity , name in [( "unnamed" , None ), ( "empty" , "" ), ( "backup" , "Backup" )]: backend . layers [ "glyph" , identity ] = LayerInfo ( id = f "layer- { identity } " , masterId = "master" , width = 500 , layerId = identity , name = name , ) font = Model ( backend ) . font layers = list ( font . glyphs [ 0 ] . layers ) assert [ layer . name for layer in layers ] == [ "Regular" , None , "" , "Backup" ] assert [ layer . isMasterLayer for layer in layers ] == [ True , False , False , False ] assert layers [ 1 ] . associatedMasterId == layers [ 0 ] . layerId assert font . glyphs [ 0 ] . layers [ "unnamed" ] is layers [ 1 ] assert layers [ 1 ] . copy () . name is None matches = [ ( glyph . name , layer . layerId ) for glyph in font . glyphs for layer in glyph . layers if layer . name is None and not layer . isMasterLayer ] assert matches == [( font . glyphs [ 0 ] . name , "unnamed" )] All fixture layers have empty geometry, but only the absent-name auxiliary matches. The condition describes a missing name, not an empty outline. It also has whole-font scope; substituting selected glyphs changes the workflow. This example was verified with the private, uncommitted development artifact 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548.d20261101 . The earlier clean artifact 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548 fails the raw-name assertion: its proxy substitutes the master name for both None and "" . Master and background naming retain their existing behavior in the repaired candidate. This is not a published release. The fixture does not show whether FontLab's importer preserves a Glyphs None name or converts it to an empty string. Do not use this filter as a qualified native deletion script. Removing layers additionally requires preservation of locks, active layers, automatic dependants, history and saved/reopened payloads. Those native workflows remain unverified. The broader Layer Cleanup menu has its own explicit selection and layer-kind behavior; it is not an equivalent implementation of this predicate.
title: Distinguish layer names from layer identity

text: A glyph's stored Unicode is editable font data. A name-based Glyph Info lookup asks for database metadata. These differ when a glyph has been re-encoded: a script that resets Unicode cannot use the current encoding as its reference. Omitting font or passing font=None queries the shared manager without reading the active font. An explicit font selects font.glyphsInfo() ; the earlier unconditional .localData refusal is superseded. Integer Name dispatch differs by complete Glyphs2/3/4 profile. The manager/profile guide provides current document selection, exact keywords, formatting, forwarding and provider examples. Its default Glyphs4 Unicode keyword is string_or_int ; Glyphs2/3 retain String with their separate integer contracts. This diagnostic fixture runs outside FontLab. It instantiates the application facade with owned model/bridge doubles; it does not activate GlyphsApp, load a native host or edit an open font. The deliberately incorrect encoding on A remains untouched after the query. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp.application import GSApplication current_glyph = SimpleNamespace ( name = "A" , unicode = "0042" , category = "Symbol" , subCategory = None , script = "custom-script" , case = 2 , layers = [], ) local = owned_parsed_manager () current_font = SimpleNamespace ( glyphs = { "A" : current_glyph }, glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) model = SimpleNamespace ( font = current_font ) # This fixture never calls bridge methods or reads/writes persistent defaults. app = GSApplication ( model , object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) info = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) assert info . unicode == "0041" , "Name-derived data must not copy current encoding" assert info . category == "Letter" assert info . script == "latin" assert current_glyph . script == "custom-script" , "A lookup must not edit script metadata" # Filter by database script metadata; an unassigned script remains None. names = [ "A" , "Alpha" , "alpha" , "acutecomb" ] greek = [ name for name in names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . script == "greek" ] assert greek == [ "Alpha" , "alpha" ] assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "acutecomb" ) . script is None # Case is a database enum: upper=1, lower=2, not a Unicode category. case_names = [ "A" , "a" , "exclam" , "less" , "acutecomb" ] upper = [ name for name in case_names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . case == 1 ] lower = [ name for name in case_names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . case == 2 ] assert upper == [ "A" , "exclam" ] assert lower == [ "a" , "less" , "acutecomb" ] assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "acutecomb" ) . category == "Mark" assert current_glyph . case == 2 , "A lookup must not edit case metadata" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = None ) . unicode == "0041" assert current_glyph . unicode == "0042" , "A lookup must not edit the glyph" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = current_font ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "A" ) assert current_glyph . unicode == "0042" , "Explicit lookup must not edit current encoding" The read-only script field snapshots metadata supplied by the database. This example uses it to select Greek names without changing the font. An unassigned script stays None ; do not treat that as a missing glyph or invent a script from its Unicode. The read-only case field also snapshots database metadata. Its values are no-case (0), upper (1), lower (2), small-caps (3), minor (4) and other (5). They are not Unicode general categories: exclam has upper case metadata, while less and the combining mark acutecomb have lower case metadata. Missing case metadata maps to no-case; an unknown label raises an unsupported capability error. Other Glyph Info fields remain incomplete. This fixture needs the private global-lookup, script-field and case-field repairs. Several uncommitted builds share 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548.d20261101 ; version text alone does not identify them. The earlier lookup-only build raises an unsupported attribute error at info.script ; the later script-only build fails at the first .case read. These archives are not published releases. title: Query glyph metadata without copying the current encoding

text: GSGlyph.case is mutable glyph metadata; GSGlyphInfo.case above is a read-only database snapshot. A glyph can have a temporary case value while storeCase is false. Setting that flag to true preserves the current value through supported name changes and metadata refreshes. Setting an attached glyph's flag from true to false restores its database default. Assigning false when it is already false leaves a temporary value intact. The following owned fixture runs outside FontLab. It demonstrates the same minor-figure predicate used by kerning scripts, then changes case without editing an open font. FakeBackend supplies the attachment target; it is not a font file. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend names = [ "A" , "ordfeminine" , "one" ] assert [ name for name in names if GSGlyph ( name ) . case == 4 ] == [ "ordfeminine" ] glyph = GSGlyph ( "f_f_i" ) assert glyph . case == 2 glyph . case = 3 assert glyph . storeCase is False glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 3 # An unchanged flag does not refresh metadata. font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) assert glyph . case == 3 # Unique attachment retains the temporary value. glyph . storeCase = True glyph . name = "less" assert glyph . case == 3 # The stored value survives this name change. glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 2 # Attached reset restores the database classification. copied = glyph . copy () copied . storeCase = True copied . case = 5 assert glyph . case == 2 try : copied . storeCase = False except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyph.storeCase.detachedReset" else : raise AssertionError ( "Detached reset is not yet qualified" ) assert ( copied . case , copied . storeCase ) == ( 5 , True ) Detached true-to-false reset currently refuses before mutation; its upstream manager behavior still needs qualification. Custom global/font-local databases, synthesized names and complete updateGlyphInfo behavior remain incomplete. That historical candidate refused unknown-name updates. This fixture does not prove native history, saved/reopened metadata or complete kerning-script workflows. The lifecycle candidate uses the same private development version as the earlier case-field build above. title: Preserve a glyph's case override

text: GSGlyph.script reads named-glyph metadata, including for unencoded glyphs. Assignment changes the current value without enabling storeScript . An enabled flag preserves the value through supported name changes and refreshes. Disabling it on an attached glyph restores the database default. An already-false flag leaves a temporary assignment intact. None and an empty string are distinct explicit values. This owned fixture runs outside FontLab. It exercises the draft-before-append pattern used by script builders, followed by a stored override and reset. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = GSGlyph ( "f_f" ) assert glyph . script == "latin" glyph . script = "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "Rovas" font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) assert glyph . script == "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = True glyph . name = "Alpha" assert glyph . script == "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "greek" glyph . script = None assert glyph . script is None # Explicit None does not fall back to Greek. copied = glyph . copy () assert copied . script is None copied . script = "" assert copied . script == "" and glyph . script is None with font . glyphsInfo () . _scope (): copied . name = "A-cy" assert copied . script == "cyrillic" # A known name refreshes unstored metadata. Detached true-to-false reset refuses before mutation, as with case metadata. Custom metadata managers, synthesized names, complete original-script workflows, native Undo/Redo and saved/reopened metadata remain unqualified. The fixture uses an owned backend double and does not edit any font file. The script-lifecycle candidate retains version 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548.d20261101 .
