title: Preserve a glyph's script override

text: The source candidate now supports independent category , subCategory , storeCategory and storeSubCategory values. Classification accepts strings, including the empty string, or None . Assigning Unicode alone does not refresh classification. Turning an enabled storage flag off refreshes only that field; a flag already off is a no-op. Detached resets remain explicitly unsupported. Case, script and classification resets share Unicode-first resolution. For an A encoded as 0061 , case resets to lowercase; for 0A15 , script resets to Gurmukhi. The first resolvable encoding wins, including synthesized metadata: an unassigned 0378 prevents a later 0A15 from supplying Gurmukhi metadata, while 10FFFF , which yields no record, allows the next encoding to be tried. The Icon and SF-Symbol categories use the audited keep-name path. This owned example exercises the shared resolver without opening FontLab: from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] glyph . unicodes = [ "0061" ] glyph . category = "Symbol" glyph . storeCategory = True glyph . case = 3 glyph . storeCase = True glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 2 # Unicode metadata wins over the name A. assert glyph . category == "Symbol" and glyph . storeCategory glyph . storeCategory = False assert glyph . category == "Letter" assert glyph . name == "A" and glyph . unicodes == [ "0061" ] These are owned offline checks against retained upstream analysis, not native measurements. Custom data, full ROS mapping, complex small-cap mapping and language suffixes remain unqualified. The current private parameter/presentation update is described in the ordered parameter guide . Additional encodings now follow the audited helper gates; native workflow acceptance remains open. Earlier artifact hashes and examples above identify their historical, narrower candidates; they do not identify this source revision.
title: Classification and shared resolver

text: Refreshing an attached uppercase glyph can add its lowercase encoding when no other glyph owns that code. I can also gain dotless i; each ownership check is independent. Refresh applies the resolved metadata’s encoding list plus these additions; it does not preserve every arbitrary previous glyph encoding. Additions preserve the resolved list’s order and do not duplicate its entries. This uses the glyph's current case/script, including temporary overrides, before stored metadata overlays. Resetting a storage flag does not write encodings. The owned example below runs without FontLab: from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = GSGlyph ( "I" ) font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0069" , "0131" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0069" , "0131" ] # No duplicates. other_font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font other_font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () other_font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "i" )) capital = GSGlyph ( "I" ) other_font . glyphs . append ( capital ) capital . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert capital . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0131" ] # Another glyph owns ordinary i. Greek-script expansion requires both Phi and Sigma encodings in the font. U+0130 and the audited out-of-range sentinel bypass expansion. Ordinary rename and explicit refresh remain distinct: rename clears non-PUA encodings before resolution, while a subsequent refresh can add encodings. Parentless glyphs and keep-name categories have separate audited branches. The retained parentless Arabic branch can yield no metadata; it is not equivalent to attached refresh. Legacy-only Arabic .isol data does not become primary Unicode automatically. The bundled Unicode17 scalar mapping matches actual NSString.lowercaseString for all1,112,064 valid scalars on macOS27.2. Python3.11 casing differs on55scalars. This pins that measured casing contract, not all Foundation versions. The public data and licence ship with the package; no Objective-C bridge is loaded for this operation. Native history/reopen, complete local initialization and full ROS mapping remain unqualified. The newer source/artifact-tested Arabic presentation stage is described in the ordered parameter guide ; it does not establish native font-workflow acceptance.

title: What is supported

text: Compatibility is partial and still being extended; each run records a receipt with the outcome, and unsupported features raise UnsupportedCapability at the script line instead of failing silently. Native tools have no toolbar icon, never claim keys (so FontLab shortcuts keep working, with no shortcut override), and paint only while active. FontLab always reports the active tool as select. Bundles that ship only compiled macOS code cannot run. Creating glyphs makes FontLab rebuild auto-layer composites. Glyport restores existing composites afterwards and refuses with a named reason when it cannot. A FontLab defect can still drop component locks and attaching anchors on composites it rebuilds. Edits on auto layers (outlines, anchors, guides, hints, width, background) are refused before anything changes: telling FontLab about an auto-layer edit makes it rebuild every auto layer in the font. Test with a copy of your font: scripts can change the font they run on. See the Glyphs compatibility guide . Reference: fontlab_glyport .
title: Limits

text: Native triage on FontLab 9.0.9802 ran 98 corpus Glyphs plugins and scripts through Glyport on an owned font (final code). Pass means the target loaded, registered its menu, tool or window, ran the hooks the harness could trigger without errors, and closed cleanly. Partial means it loaded and ran but a hook raised. Fail means it did not load or did not close. Kind Targets Pass Partial Fail Reporters 30 14 9 7 Tools 7 2 2 3 Filters 12 11 0 1 Palettes 7 5 0 2 General plugins 12 4 0 8 Scripts 30 19 1 10 Total 98 55 12 31 A pass does not prove a plugin's whole behaviour: buttons, dialogs, filter output and outline edits were not exercised, and filters were only installed. Main known gaps: Compiled Objective-C bundles (for example ShowAngledHandles) have no Python entry point and cannot run. The triage environment lacked glyphsLib , which Glyport declares as a dependency. Plugins that import it failed there; a complete install avoids that failure class, so the counts understate what a complete install passes. Some AppKit and Cocoa members are missing (for example NSGradient , NSBeep and a few layout and window constants), and a few Glyphs model members are absent.

The manager guide covers the selected manager, six stored overlays, groupIdx/direction, canonical/shallow/ frozen distinctions and qualified custom parsing/finalization/discovery. Its connected local-manager section adds constructor/reload, base-versus-custom parsing, sidebar resources, queue identity and precise exception boundaries through invented lawful dependencies, with seven additional executable examples. Matching companion archives and the complete ordinary installed tuple remain separate. Complete default/private resources, native local initialization/reload, the original HTML tool and native FontLab behavior remain open. Earlier artifact receipts above retain their historical scope.
title: Stored descriptions

text: The complete-generation examples run all ten Chinese jobs and the full queued Hangul traversal through the actual manager implementation. They inspect fixed ranges, profiles, row fields, collision identity, callback completion order, Jamo links and partial failure state. Their four Chinese banks are explicitly invented lawful inputs. Missing private banks refuse; these examples do not qualify proprietary defaults, native font workflows, history, dialogs or publication.
title: Complete generation with owned inputs

text: Grablab captures FontLab's interface for documentation and tests: panels, menus, Glyph and Font windows, screens and widgets, as PNG, SVG or PDF with title and description metadata.
title: grablab

text: Install fontlab-grablab together with fontlab-fontlabapp into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Importing grablab is host-free; capturing needs FontLab.
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from grablab import Grab capture = Grab ( grab_canvas = False , grab_screens = False ) capture . newGrab () paths = capture . grabPanel ( "elements" ) print ( paths )
title: Quick start

text: Capture a widget, including a Fontlabapp drawing overlay, as SVG and PNG: from pathlib import Path from fontlabapp import Application from grablab import Grab app = Application () folder = Path . home () / "Desktop" / "captures" folder . mkdir ( exist_ok = True ) grab = Grab ( application = app , folder_base = folder ) with app . control as fl : grab . getWidgetSVG ( fl . preview . widget , folder / "preview.svg" )
title: Examples

text: Capture temporarily changes OpenGL, outline-thickness and pixel-rendering preferences and restores them afterwards, even on failure. OpenGL canvases have Qt framebuffer limits; the non-OpenGL Glyph view and Preview paths are verified. Reference: grablab .
title: Limits

text: Plugmix is a package of native FontLab 9 plugins. It has five plugin kinds: reporters (toggleable, read-only overlays on the Glyph window), filters (undoable edits to selected glyphs), palettes (dockable panels), tools (native FontLab tools) and General plugins (menu commands and font events). Plugmix uses FontLab's PythonQt and, on older builds, Fontlabapp's editor painters. It does not use PySide2, and it does not emulate Glyphs.app. Under revision Plugmix is being revised. This page describes the stable concepts. Exact module names and defaults can still change.
title: Plugmix

text: FontLab 9 builds with native canvas painters expose two Python hooks on the host itself: a canvas painter ( flCanvas.appendPythonPainter ) and a workspace tool ( flWorkspace.registerPythonTool ). See Native Python hooks in FontLab 9 . Plugmix reporters build on the painter hook. Registry. Finds plugins of every kind, remembers your choices, and attaches or detaches them. Built-in plugins and plugins published through the fontlab_plugmix.plugins entry-point group are discovered the same way, and the kind comes from the class's base class. A plugin needs a unique name and a human-readable title ; names are unique across kinds. Native-painter backend. When flCanvas.appendPythonPainter exists, Plugmix attaches one painter per Glyph window as it becomes active and registers each reporter on it. Reporters with layer = "background" paint under the glyph; the others paint over it. On older builds the backend falls back to Fontlabapp's EditorPainters , paints everything over the canvas and logs the background substitution once. Coordinates. A glyph point is mapped through the glyph's position in its text block, then the text block's placement, then canvas.mapToViewportF into viewport pixels. Cost. Each reporter reads the glyph again on every repaint. That is fine for the built-in set but adds up with many reporters enabled. Plugins compute from immutable, plain-Python snapshots, so you can test them without FontLab.
title: How it works

text: Install fontlab-python-plugmix and its fontlab-fontlabapp dependency into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Start Plugmix once per FontLab session from your own initScript.py : try : from fontlab_plugmix import install ; install () except Exception as error : print ( f "Plugmix startup: { error } " ) The package ships this snippet as initScript-snippet.py . Nothing in the package edits a FontLab installation. Alternatively, run Install Plugmix Menu.py from the Script menu. install() adds menu entries and restores your choices: Kind Where it appears Reporter One checkable Plugmix: Show ... action per reporter in the View menu. Filter Plugmix: Delete Small Paths… in the Glyph menu, opening a non-modal parameter dialog. Palette Plugmix: Step and Repeat Panel in the Window menu, checkable, hidden until shown. Tool Plugmix: Tool Smart Select , which registers a native tool when enabled. General Plugmix: Zoom to Selection in the View menu. Choices live in one JSON file in FontLab's Data folder, with these keys: enabled (reporters), enabled_filters , enabled_palettes , enabled_tools , enabled_general and params (last-used filter values). Older files with only enabled still load, filters, tools and General plugins are enabled by default, and enabled_palettes is written only after you choose a visibility. A selection saved under the former name nodes_outside_paths restores as offcurve_outside_bounds . uninstall() removes the actions, overlays and panels and keeps the saved choices.
title: Install

text: Built-in reporters: Reporter Overlay Duplicate Anchor Rings Rings around anchors less than one font unit apart. Node Indexes Contour index beside every on- and off-curve node. Selected Node Coordinates Coordinates beside selected nodes. Two Point Distance Segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes. Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds ( offcurve_outside_bounds ) Off-curve handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle. It tests bounds, not path containment. Center Lines Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines. Vertical Metrics Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline. Angled Handles Rings on off-curve handles outside horizontal, vertical and italic axes. Crosshair Guides through selected nodes. Tops and Bottoms Rings and y labels at tied highest and lowest on-curve positions. Segment Length Straight and flattened curve lengths for selected segments. Glyph Focus Shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender. Emphasise Selected Handles Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes. Anchor Cloud Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors. RSB Line Advance boundary plus RSB and LSB labels. Unitizer Vertical grid at UPM / 18 increments. Nodes Close to Zones Rings on on-curves near zone edges or metric heights. Imprecise Italic Angle Straight segments close to, but not exactly on, the master slant. Smooth Node Angles Handle-angle mismatch and handle-length ratio at smooth nodes.
title: Reporters

text: from fontlab_plugmix import Mark , Reporter class Origin ( Reporter ): name = "origin" title = "Origin" def compute ( self , snapshot ): return [ Mark ( "ring" , (( 0 , 0 ),), diameter_px = 12 ), Mark ( "text" , (( 6 , 6 ),), text = "origin" , text_px = 11 ), ] compute() returns marks in font units. Mark kinds are ring , line , polyline , polygon (with an RGBA fill ) and text ; stroke width, text size and ring diameter are view pixels, so overlays keep their size while you zoom. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph on builds with native painters. Publish the class so Plugmix finds it. In your package's pyproject.toml : [project.entry-points. "fontlab_plugmix.plugins" ] origin = "my_package.reporters:Origin" Reinstall your package and restart FontLab; the reporter appears in the View menu.
title: Write your own reporter

text: A filter computes a proposed edit for one layer from a frozen snapshot and typed values, and Plugmix applies the result to the selected glyphs as one Undo step. Param(key, label, kind, default, minimum=None, maximum=None, choices=()) declares a dialog field. kind is "float" , "int" , "bool" or "choice" ; values outside the declared domain are rejected. LayerEdit(contours=None, advance=None, anchors=None) holds replacement values; None leaves that part of the layer alone. Filter.compute(snapshot, values) returns a LayerEdit . Filter.validate(values) fills defaults and rejects unknown or invalid parameters. from fontlab_plugmix.filter import Filter , LayerEdit class DropOpenPaths ( Filter ): name = "drop_open_paths" title = "Drop Open Paths" params = () def compute ( self , snapshot , values ): kept = tuple ( c for c in snapshot . contours if c . closed ) return LayerEdit ( contours = kept ) The writer currently supports contour deletion. It skips shared or transformed outlines and automatic layers per glyph and still edits the other selected glyphs. Delete Small Paths ( delete_small_paths , one parameter threshold , default 400 font units squared) deletes a closed contour when its area, measured on the flattened curves, is strictly below the threshold. A contour whose flattened bounding-box area is below the threshold is treated the same way. Open paths always stay, and a contour exactly at the threshold stays.
title: Filters

text: A palette is a dockable panel. Palette.build(ui) creates controls once through PaletteUI , refresh(context) runs when the active glyph, master, revision or node selection changes, and close() releases resources. PaletteUI offers label , number , checkbox and button , so palettes import no Qt. One timer serves all visible palettes and stops when none are visible. Step and Repeat ( step_and_repeat ) duplicates the selected contours of the active glyph. count is the number of additional copies, and each copy is shifted by another ( dx , dy ), so offsets accumulate. Apply is one Undo step. It works on the current master layer only: when the Glyph window shows another layer, Apply refuses with a status message instead of writing to the master.
title: Palettes

text: A tool becomes a native FontLab tool through flWorkspace.registerPythonTool . Tool.activate(ctx) and deactivate() bracket its use; press , move , release , double_click , key_down and key_up each take a ToolEvent and return True when they handled it; marks(glyph) returns overlay marks drawn only while the tool is active. ToolContext offers snapshot() , select(indices, toggle=False) , edit(plan_fn, title) and redraw() . Viewport events are mapped through FontLab's pan and zoom and the glyph's text-block transforms. Smart Select drags a rectangle and selects whole contours touched by any node; Shift toggles those contours. It is selection-only and never changes outline geometry. It omits the source plugin's double-click containment and native move handling.
title: Tools

text: A General plugin is a menu command with optional font events. General.start(ctx) and stop() bracket its life, run() handles the command, and on_font_opened(font_id) and on_font_closed(font_id) report fonts by the stable flPackage.fgId , the id that MCP, Remopy and Fontport use. GeneralContext offers notify , snapshot , edit , timer and zoom_selected . Plugmix owns the extra actions and timers a General plugin creates and removes them on uninstall() . General font watchers share the palettes' 250 ms timer. Zoom to Selection fits the active glyph's selected nodes in the canvas with a margin. It omits the source plugin's delayed viewport adjustment. Shortcut conflicts are reported, not overridden. Shortcut handling and keyboard cursor mapping still need an in-app recheck.
title: General plugins

text: The repository's Scripts/ folder holds two ordinary FontLab menu scripts: Scripts/Plugmix/Install Plugmix Menu.py installs the Plugmix menus, and Scripts/Reports/Duplicate Anchor Rings.py runs one reporter from the Script menu. Copy them into FontLab's Scripts folder to use them.
title: The Scripts folder

text: Reporters are read-only. Filters, palettes and tools edit only through Plugmix's shared outline writer. Painting runs inside FontLab's paint event on the GUI thread. Keep compute() quick. The palette refresh key reads the glyph modification timestamp and node selection; confirm that edits outside Plugmix advance it in your build. Native behaviour needs an in-app check: the test suite uses fake Qt and FontLab objects, and some newer reporters have offline coverage only.
title: Limits

text: Pythonqtside lets code written for PySide2 ( QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets , …) run on FontLab's built-in PythonQt. It routes each PySide2 name to the native class and adapts the differences that matter in practice: keyword arguments, property getters, overloads and protected event handlers. It never loads a second Qt binding or creates a QApplication .
title: pythonqtside

text: Install pythonqtside (it depends on Echopy) into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab .
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from pythonqtside import QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets widget = QtWidgets . QWidget () # the original native QWidget layout = QtWidgets . QVBoxLayout ( widget ) layout . addWidget ( QtWidgets . QLabel ( "Hello from PySide2-style code" )) widget . show ()
title: Quick start

text: Port an existing PySide2 tool by changing only its import: # from PySide2 import QtCore, QtWidgets from pythonqtside import QtCore , QtWidgets In FontLab 9, natively, QFileDialog.getOpenFileName and getSaveFileName return a str and getOpenFileNames returns a tuple. The adapter always returns PySide2-style pairs instead: (path, "") for the single-file pickers and (list_of_paths, "") for getOpenFileNames . The chosen filter cannot be read back, so a selectedFilter argument is dropped and reported as "" . options keeps its native position, and a result that is already a pair passes through. The repository's examples/pyside2_dialog.py is an unmodified PySide2 dialog that uses this; run it with pythonqtside.run_app("examples/pyside2_dialog.py") and keep the returned handle. Available namespaces: QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets , QtNetwork , QtOpenGL , QtSvg , QtUiTools , QtXmlPatterns and the combined Qt .
title: Examples

text: Use FontLab's running application; do not call QApplication.exec() . Names alone do not guarantee identical behaviour: enum conversion, ownership and some overloads differ from PySide2. See the PySide2 guide . Qt 6 / PySide6 is not supported (FontLab 9 uses Qt 5). Reference: pythonqtside .
title: Limits

text: Remopy controls a running FontLab 9 from another Python process through FontLab's native MCP server: run code, read values, open and save fonts and call any FontLab tool. It also launches FontLab and submits scripts on macOS.
title: Remopy

text: Install the fontlab-remopy wheel into your ordinary Python 3.11+ environment (not into FontLab). Enable FontLab's MCP server once: fontlab-remopy launch fontlab-remopy --timeout 15 setup setup submits a macro that sets FontLab's mcp.enabled preference and verifies it. From inside FontLab, call fontlab_remopy.enable_mcp() to do the same preference update directly.
title: Install

text: from fontlab_remopy import FontLab with FontLab () as fl : print ( fl . fonts ()) answer = fl . eval ( "value + 2" , value = 40 ) # 42 done = fl . run ( "print(message); result = {'ok': True}" , message = "Hello" ) print ( done . value , done . stdout )
title: Quick start

text: Write a function locally and run it inside FontLab: with FontLab () as fl : @fl . python def metrics ( name : str ): import fontpr return fontpr . get_glyph_metrics ( glyph_name = name ) print ( metrics ( "A" )) # with an open font containing A Run a script file and call tools from the command line: fontlab-remopy tools fontlab-remopy execute example.flpy fontlab-remopy call list_fonts Use AsyncFontLab with async with and await in asynchronous programs. Call any other FontLab tool by name with fl.tool(name, **arguments) . Remopy checks the argument names against the tool's input schema and raises ValueError for an unknown name before anything is sent. This matters because FontLab's MCP server silently drops unknown arguments: set_kerning_pair(master="Bold") would write to the current master. The kerning tools take master_name : with FontLab () as fl : fl . tool ( "list_kerning_pairs" , master_name = "Bold" ) Only names are checked, not types, and tools missing from the catalogue or with open schemas are not checked. The one-shot call_tool function and the CLI call command apply the same check (one catalogue request per call); pass check_arguments=False to opt out. run_python skips the check.
title: Examples

text: Values travel as JSON; native objects cannot be returned directly. FontLab's fixed five-second script deadline applies. A timeout leaves the outcome unknown, so mutating calls are never retried automatically. Launch and file association are macOS only; MCP works wherever FontLab's bridge executable is available. Reference: fontlab_remopy . Remopy is proprietary (© Fontlab Ltd); only its API documentation is published here.
title: Limits

text: Scriptmix ( fontlab-python-scriptmix ) is a menu collection of practical tools for FontLab 9: metrics, names and anchors editors, component writers, master navigation and layer copying, contour editing, kerning editors, proof texts, reports and drawing panels. The tools inspect, proof and edit fonts through FontLab's native APIs, PythonQt and Fontlabapp helpers. Scriptmix is not an installable Python package. It is a set of scripts you copy into FontLab; its pyproject.toml only configures documentation tools.
title: Scriptmix

text: Install matching fontlab-fly , fontlab-fontlabapp and fontlab-fontport into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Some tools also need fontTools , and Glyphs-specific tools use Glyport. Open FontLab's Scripts folder from the application. Copy the category folders from the repository's Scripts/ folder into it. Keep the layout Scripts/<Category>/<Tool>.py ; FontLab accepts one category level. Open a copy of a font, select the glyphs and master, and choose the tool from the Script menu. Each tool's docstring states its controls, scopes and refusals.
title: Install

text: Metrics, Names, Anchors, Components, Masters, Contours, Features, Font Info, Guides, Kerning, Cleanup, Proof, Reports and Utilities. Each is a folder under Scripts/ .
title: Categories

text: Metrics > Scale Advances scales selected advances by a percentage, with a preview, keeping outlines centred. Masters > Duplicate Current Layer backs up the current master or all masters. Names > Duplicate Unicodes scans the font and lets you choose assignments to keep or remove. Proof > Text Filter simplifies proof text with persistent input and regex fields.
title: Examples

text: Source tests do not establish correct Undo/Redo, saved font state or panel lifetime inside FontLab; native acceptance is tracked separately in the repository. Work on owned copies of fonts. See the repository's README and porting backlog for the full tool list and status. Where a task needs an interface or helper you write yourself, build it on Fontlabapp .
title: Limits

text: TypeRig is Vassil Kateliev's font-development library: outline objects, points and contours, interpolation and adaptive scaling, and proxies over FontLab's objects. This package distributes the complete library; TypeRig's GUI scripts, panels and toolbars stay in kateliev/TypeRig .
title: typerig

text: python -m pip install typerig TypeRig needs Python 3.10 or newer and installs fonttools for font file I/O. The core needs no FontLab. Install it into FontLab's Python folder as well to use the FontLab proxies; see Install into FontLab .
title: Install

text: from typerig.core.objects.point import Point point = Point ( 10 , 20 ) + Point ( 2 , 3 ) print ( point . x , point . y ) # 12.0 23.0
title: Quick start

text: Inside FontLab, use the proxy layer on the current glyph: from typerig.proxy.fl.objects.glyph import eGlyph glyph = eGlyph () # wraps the current glyph print ( glyph . name , glyph . getBounds ())
title: Examples

text: Proxy modules need their host API (FontLab, or Glyphs for the Glyphs proxies). Licence: Mozilla Public License 2.0 (upstream TypeRig). Reference: typerig .

text: Glyport constructs a GlyphsApp module for each adapted Glyphs script. Its Glyphs object belongs to that script's FontLab context. text: =============================================== Canvas - class to represent screen paint area and operations =============================================== This class can perform automatic coordinates transformations, so you can draw in Glyph coordinate space or, if you prefer, in screen coordinates directly Use constants defined for FontLab module to assign attributes to Canvas object CONSTRUCTOR: ++ Never create Canvas object explicitly - they must be obtained from the FontLab's window classes Canvas() - generic constructor, creates an empty Canvas Canvas(Canvas) - copy constructor ATTRIBUTES: delta (Point) - horizontal shift during coordinates transformation scale (Point(float)) - scaling during coordinates transformation width (integer, read-only) - width of the canvas in pixels height (integer, read-only) - height of the canvas in pixels draw_style (integer, write-only) - sets current drawing mode (copy, XOR, invert etc.) pen_color (integer, write-only) - sets current pen color pen_style (integer, write-only) - sets current pen style (solid, dashed etc.) brush_color (integer, write-only) - sets current brush color brush_style (integer, write-only) - sets current brush style (solid, patterned etc.) text_color (integer, write-only) - sets color for a text bk_color (integer, write-only) - sets color for a text background bk_mode (integer, write-only) - sets background mode for a text output (transparent or opaque) OPERATIONS: METHODS MoveTo(Point p) | (x, y) - moves current position to p or (x, y) coordinates LineTo(Point p) | (x, y) - draws a straight line to the position p or (x, y) CurveTo(Point p0, Point p1, Point p2) - draws a 3th-order Bezier curve from the current point to points p0, p1, p2 SplineTo(Point p0, Point p1) - draws a 2th-order Bezier curve from the current point to points p0, p1 Ellipse(Rect r) | (Point p0, Point p1) | (x0, y0, x1, y1) - draws a filled ellipse defined by the Rect r, points p0 and p1 or set of coordinates Rectangle(Rect r) | (Point p0, Point p1) | (x0, y0, x1, y1) - draws a filled rectangle defined by the Rect r, points p0 and p1 or set of coordinates Convert(Point p) - converts coordinates from the source coordinate space to screen coordinates UnConvert(Point p) - converts screen coordinates to the currently defined coordinate space FitGlyph(Rect r, Glyph g) | (Rect r, Glyph g, WeightVector w) - recalculates parameters of coordinate conversion function to fit glyph g into rectangle r using currently selected options. FillGlyph(Glyph g) | (Glyph g, WeightVector w) - fills the glyph g using current coordinate transformation. OutlineGlyph(Glyph g) | (Glyph g, WeightVector w) - draws the glyph g outline using current coordinate transformation. TextOut(Point p, string s) | (x, y, string s) - draws the string s in the position p or (x, y) PutImage(Image i, Point p) | (Image i, Pioint p, int mode) - puts Image i at the selected point Native bases: object

text: =============================================== Component - class to represent glyph component =============================================== Components are defined by the glyph index which they reference, shift of components origin point and scale factor of a component scale is measured in relation to 1.0, so 100% scale is 1.0 and 60% - 0.6 This class is Multiple Master - compatible CONSTRUCTOR: Component() - generic constructor, creates an empty Component Component(Component) - copy constructor Component(index) - creates component referencing glyph index with zero shift and 100% scale Component(index, Point(integer) delta) - creates component referencing glyph index with delta shift and 100% scale Component(index, Point(integer) delta, Point(float) scale) - creates component referencing glyph index with delta shift and scale factor defined by scale ATTRIBUTES: parent (read-only) - parent object, Glyph index (integer) - referencing glyph index delta (Point(integer)) - shift value scale (Point(float)) - scale factor deltas [(Point(integer))]- list of shift values for each master scales [(Point(float))] - list of scale values for each master OPERATIONS: METHODS Get() | (Font f) - creates a glyph from component applying delta and scale transformations. Font parameter is not needed when component has a parent Paste() - appends component to a parent glyph as a set of outlines. Component must have a parent Native bases: object

list of componets replace_table [Replace] - hint replacing program, list of Replace objects kerning [KerningPair] - list of kerning pairs layers_number (integer) - number of masters flags (integer) - flags set for this glyph nodes_number (integer) - number of nodes, same as 'len(Glyph)' width (integer) - advance width for the first master height (integer) - advance height for the first master unicode (integer) - first Unicode index in integer form unicodes [integer] - list of Unicode indexes name (string) - glyph name mask (string) - mask STORED TRUETYPE DATA advance_width (integer) advance_height (integer) left_side_bearing (integer) top_side_bearing (integer) y_pels (integer) bounding_box (Rect) number_of_contours (integer) end_points [integer] points [TTPoint] instructions [Byte] hdmx[Byte] OPERATIONS: len() - returns number of nodes in the glyph [] - can be used to access individial nodes slice - can be used to access portion of the glyph's nodes array + or concatination - can be used to append Glyph, Node or sequence of Nodes multiply - second operand must be Matrix, applies matrix transformation to a glyph METHODS Assign (Glyph) - copies all information from the assigned glyph Transform(Matrix m) - applies Matrix transformation to the Glyph (see Matrix(). doc ) SetLayersNumber(mastersnumber) - changes the number of masters, is applicable only to glyphs that have no parent Clear() - removes all nodes Add - refer to '+' operator Insert (Node | Glyph | [Node]) | (Node | Glyph | [Node], nodeindex) - inserts Node, Glyph or sequence of Nodes at the begining of glyph's nodes or at specified node index Present (style) - returns True if a layer or a combination of layers are present in the glyph Delete (index) | (index0, index1) - removes node or range of nodes ExpandLayer (masterindex) - expands selected master to all other masters Shift (Point) | (Point, masterindex) - shifts positions of all nodes at first or specified master Scale (Point(float) scale) | (Point(float) scale, Point center) | (Point(float) scale, Point center, masterindex) - scales the glyph Layer (masterindex) - returns list of Points for all nodes for the selected master Section (masterindex, pointindex, nodetype) - returns list of Points that conform to selected options MoveNode(...) - moves the node copying Edit tool behavior (see User manual for details) DeleteNode(nodeindex) - removes the node InsertNode(nodeindex) | (nodeindex, float time) | (nodeindex, float time, masterindex) - insers new node on a contour SELECTION OPERATIONS Selection() - returns list of selected nodes SelectAll() - selects all nodes UnselectAll() - deselects all nodes InvertSelection() - selects unselected nodes and deselects selected nodes isAnySelected() - returns True if at least one node is selected SelectedCount() - returns number of selected nodes SelectRect(Rect r) | (Rect r, masterindex) - selects all nodes that are inside the rectangle UnselectRect(Rect r) | (Rect r, masterindex) - deselects all nodes that are inside the rectangle DeleteSelected() - deletes all selected nodes METRICS AND BBOX OPERATIONS GetBoundingRect() | (masterindex) - returns Rect - bounding box of the glyph GetMetrics() | (masterindex) - returns glyph advance width and advance height in a form of Point SetMetrics(Point p) | (Point p, masterindex) - assigns new values to the width and height of the glyph GetVSB() | (masterindex) - returns glyph bottom sidebearing position SetVSB(value) | (value, masterindex) - assigns new values to the bottom sidebearing of the glyph OVERLAP OPERATIONS RemoveOverlap() | (masterindex) - removes overlap Badd(Glyph g) | ([Node]) | (Glyph g, masterindex) | ([Node], masterindex) - performs bollean Add operation with the glyph or list of nodes Bsubtract(Glyph g) | ([Node]) | (Glyph g, masterindex) | ([Node], masterindex) - performs bollean Subtract operation with the glyph or list of nodes Bintersect(Glyph g) | ([Node]) | (Glyph g, masterindex) | ([Node], masterindex) - performs bollean Insersect operation with the glyph or list of nodes OPERATIONS ON CONTOURS GetContoursNumber() - returns number of contours in the glyph GetContourBegin(contourindex) - returns index of the first node for a contour GetContourLength(contourindex) - returns number of nodes in a contour SelectContour(contourindex) - selects all nodes in the contour DeleteContour(contourindex) - removes contour ReverseContour(contourindex) - reverses contour's direction ReorderContour(contourindex, newindex) - reorders contours in the glyph isContourClockwise(contourindex) - returns True if direction of contour is clockwise SetStartNode(nodeindex) - makes the node a starting node of the contour FindContour(nodeindex) - returns number of contour containing the 'nodeindex' HINTS OPERATIONS RemoveHints(mode) - removes hints and links Autohint() | (masterindex) - automatically generates Type 1 hints ANCHOR OPERATIONS FindAnchor(string name) - finds anchor by name TRANSFORMATION ACTIONS Decompose() - pastes all components to the glyph outline MakeExtremeNodes() | (masterindex) - automatically detects and adds extreme nodes Audit() | (masterindex) - performs test of the glyph and returns list of AuditRecord objects Iterate(Iterator) - iterates glyph trough iterator class which must unclude following methods: Start(); ClosePath(); StartPath(Node); LineTo(Node); CurveTo(Node); SplineTo(Node); Finish() Rotate3D Extrude3D(outlinewidth, shift_x, shift_y) Shadow(outlinewidth, shift_x, shift_y) College(outlinewidth, distance) Gradient(outlinewidth, direction, stripes_number, start_y, finish_y) Distance(width_x, width_y, cornermode) | (width_x, width_y, cornermode, Glyph dest) Interpolate([(nodeindex, Point newposition]) Warp([Point], float force) Rasterize() | Rasterize(Image, [, active layer[, height]]) | Rasterize(Image, [, WeightVector[, height]]) - Returns resulting image_rect. Height is relative to font's UPM Blend(Glyph source, integer layer1, integer layer2, Point amount) - returns blend of the glyph and source JoinAll() - tries to join all open contours SaveEPS(string filename) | (string filename, layer) - writes layer into the EPS file named filename LoadEPS(string filename) - reads EPS from filename and returns Glyph object.
